model: LongCat-2.0（4 个仓库的 24 个阶段降级到 gemini-3.1-pro-preview）

repos.fit: 候选人是 GPU kernel / 训练性能工程师，但当前无 GPU。SGLang 的 Rust 服务化（sgl-router、sgl-kv-indexer、rust server）、Python 调度层（radix_cache、schedule_batch、mem_cache）以及采样/请求验证逻辑都是纯 CPU 可开发与验证的模块，与候选人的性能工程、算子融合、分布式训练 rollout 后端经验高度契合。尤其是 sgl-router 的 KV 感知路由策略、可观察性、契约测试方向，与候选人做端侧部署与跨语言系统的经验直接对口。
repos.current_direction: SGLang 当前处于 Rust 服务化加速期（sgl-router、rust server 提交活跃）、HiCache / PD 分离 / HiSparse 等分布式 KV 缓存路线快速推进、扩散模型与多硬件后端（NPU/AMD/Intel/TPU）并行扩张。维护者明显欢迎：Rust 路由策略与可观察性改进、请求验证与 DoS 防护、调度层正确性修复、文档与 benchmark 基建。
recommended_order: 补全 sgl-router cache_aware / load_based 策略单元测试与边界用例
补全 SamplingParams 上界校验（top_k / logprobs / n）
修复 DisallowedTokensLogitsProcessor 跨请求 batch 语义
为 sgl-router 添加路由决策延迟与 prefix cache 命中指标
补全 GenerateReqInput / SessionParams 原生路径类型校验
补全 sgl-router ↔ Python load_publisher LoadStat 契约测试
为 sgl-router 添加策略对比 benchmark 脚本
新增 sgl-router 上手文档与最小示例
maintainer_path: 首次 PR 尽量小：只加测试、只加校验、或只加指标埋点，不重构核心路径
在 Issue 下先留言说明方案（尤其是 #41482、#41471、#41466 这类有多种修复方向的），得到维护者确认再动手
优先跑 cargo test / pytest 中能在本机通过的 CPU 子集，Colab T4 只用于最终确认
关注 #23206（Rust 迁移）和 #21846（Distributed KVCache）两个 RFC，长期贡献方向可向 sgl-router / HiCache 靠拢
how_to_engage: 在 Issue 下用英文简短留言说明理解、方案、预计时间，得到维护者确认后再开 PR（README 与 CONTRIBUTING 均强调先沟通）
加入 Slack（https://slack.sglang.io/）和每周 Dev Meeting（https://meet.sglang.io/）了解当前优先级
PR 标题遵循现有风格：test(sgl-router): … / fix(sampling): … / feat(metrics): … / docs: …
代码风格遵循 .pre-commit-config.yaml（isort、codespell 等），文档遵循 docs/ 的 Mintlify 风格
维护者响应节奏较快（单日十余条合并），但大功能需先 RFC；小 fix / 测试通常几天内审完

positioning.overview: SGLang（sgl-project/sglang，LMSYS 非营利组织托管）是高性能大模型与多模态模型推理服务框架，2024 年初以 RadixAttention 前缀缓存起家，README 自称支撑全球 40 万+ GPU、日产数万亿 token，被 xAI、NVIDIA、AMD、Cursor 及各大云厂采用，2025/03 加入 PyTorch 生态，已是工业界事实标准之一。架构为双语言引擎：Python 侧（python/sglang，目录约 3863 个文件）承载调度器、KV 缓存、模型实现与 OpenAI 兼容服务；Rust 侧（rust/sglang-server、sglang-mm、sglang-renderer、experimental/sgl-router、sgl-model-gateway）承担高性能服务器、多模态数据面与路由，rust/sglang-server 是提交热点第二位，服务化正在加速。能力覆盖 continuous batching、paged attention、PD 分离、投机解码（DFlash/Spec V2）、TP/PP/EP/DP 并行、FP4/FP8/INT4/AWQ/GPTQ 量化、多 LoRA、结构化输出；模型覆盖主流 LLM、embedding/reward 模型与扩散模型（WAN、Qwen-Image，即 SGLang Diffusion）；硬件覆盖 NVIDIA/AMD/Intel XPU/Xeon CPU/TPU/昇腾 NPU。它同时是 RL 后训练 rollout 后端，被 verl、slime、AReaL、Miles、Tunix 集成。与 vLLM 为最直接竞品（README 致谢承认借鉴 vLLM/FlashInfer/LightLLM），差异化在 RadixAttention、零开销调度器、DeepSeek/Kimi K3 等 day-0 支持与大规模 EP/PD 分离工程。当前 v0.5.x、约两周一个 release、单日十余条合并，成熟期中仍快速扩张（Rust 服务化、扩散管线、TPU 后端均为近一年新增）。对无 GPU 的读者：仓库提供 pyproject_cpu.toml（CPU 安装路径）与可本机构建的 Rust 组件，是可行的切入面。
positioning.problem: 解决大模型推理从「能跑」到「高吞吐、低延迟、可规模化服务」的工程问题，具体拆解为： 多请求并发下 KV 缓存浪费与前缀重复计算——RadixAttention 树形缓存（官方博客称最高 5x 提速），并有 hicache 层级缓存与 unified_memory 扩展； prefill 与 decode 互相争抢——PD 分离、chunked prefill； decode 受算力与带宽限制——投机解码（2026/06 的 DFlash/Spec V2 为新一代）、FP4/FP8/INT4/AWQ/GPTQ 量化； MoE 模型多机扩展——大规模专家并行（96×H100、GB200/GB300 NVL72 集群博客，称 25x 提升）； agent/RL 场景的高并发重复前缀 rollout——被 verl/slime 等用作 rollout 后端； 新模型发布当天可部署——DeepSeek-V4、Kimi K3、GLM5.2 等 day-0 支持； 视频与图像扩散生成纳入统一服务框架（SGLang Diffusion，WAN/Qwen-Image）。
positioning.users: 四类目标用户： 推理平台/服务工程师——xAI、Cursor、LinkedIn 及 Oracle/Azure/AWS/GCP 等云厂商（README 采用名单），典型场景是单卡到千卡集群上跑 OpenAI 兼容 API； RL/post-training 团队——作为 verl、slime、AReaL、Miles、Tunix 的 rollout 后端做大规模采样； 模型方与早期采用者——需要 DeepSeek-V4、Kimi K3、GLM5.2、Nemotron 3 等新模型的 day-0 部署与调优（GLM5.2 NVFP4 agentic 500 TPS 案例）； 多模态与生成式应用开发者——VLM（LLaVA 类）、OCR、ASR/TTS，以及 2025/11 起的视频/图像扩散生成（WAN、Qwen-Image）。对内核/性能背景的读者，最相关的用户故事是：kernel 与调度优化直接决定其吞吐指标，benchmark/ 目录（146 个文件）就是这些用户的验收场。

landscape.difference: 最直接竞品，也是 README 致谢的代码来源。PagedAttention 首创者、社区规模最大；SGLang 差异化在 RadixAttention 前缀复用、零开销调度器、DeepSeek/Kimi 等 day-0 深度优化、大规模 EP 与 PD 分离、RL rollout 集成。
NVIDIA 官方推理栈，kernel 级优化极致但绑定 NVIDIA 硬件生态；SGLang 开放且多硬件（AMD/Intel/TPU/NPU），v0.2 博客曾直接对标其 Llama3 serving 性能。
README 致谢的借鉴项目，轻量 Python serving 框架；SGLang 的功能广度、Rust 组件与 CI/硬件矩阵投入远超。
面向 CPU/端侧的 GGUF 推理库，无 PD 分离、EP、多 LoRA 等服务端特性；定位互补（端侧 vs 数据中心），与读者端侧部署经验衔接但非同类。
早期主流 serving 框架，迭代相对平缓；SGLang 在投机解码、PD 分离、新模型支持速度上更激进。
非竞品而是被致谢/依赖的 attention kernel 库，SGLang 在其上构建；可作为理解其 kernel 层的对照。

positioning.stage: 成熟期但仍在快速扩张：核心 serving 能力（调度、缓存、量化、PD 分离）成熟并大规模生产部署；v0.5.x 约两周一个 release（v0.5.18→v0.5.20），主干单日十余条合并、PR 编号已到 4.1 万+；扩张方向为 Rust 服务化（rust/sglang-server 为提交热点第二）、SGLang Diffusion、TPU/XPU/NPU 等新后端；experimental/sgl-router 仍在 experimental 目录，属演进中。

codemap.layers: SGLang 采用「双语言、五层」架构。最上层是接入层（Rust 服务器 + Python 前端），负责 HTTP/gRPC 入口、OpenAI 兼容 API、多模态数据面与 KV 感知路由；Rust 侧由 experimental/sgl-router（KV 感知路由、策略、健康检查）与 rust/sglang-server、rust/sglang-mm（统一数据面）构成，Python 侧由 python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/ 下的 OpenAI 兼容服务器与前端语言接入组成。第二层是调度层，核心是 python/sglang/srt/managers/ 下的 Scheduler、SchedulerProfiler 与 scheduler_components/（load_publisher、chunked_prefill、radix_cache 等），实现 continuous batching、chunked prefill、RadixAttention 前缀缓存、PD 分离调度、投机解码调度。第三层是执行层，包括 python/sglang/srt/executor/（GPUModelRunner、overlapping_scheduler）、python/sglang/srt/layers/（attention、moe、quantization、linear、norm、rope 等算子包装）、python/sglang/srt/model_executor/（模型前向、采样、logits 处理）。第四层是 kernel 层，主要是 python/sgl-kernel/ 与 python/sglang/srt/layers/ 调用的 Triton/CuTe/CUTLASS/FlashInfer 自定义算子，以及 3rdparty/amd/ 等厂商特化实现。第五层是工具层，包括 benchmark/、docs/、examples/、docker/、test/、scripts/ci/、.claude/skills/（性能剖析、事故分诊、机械重构验证）等工程支撑。双语言边界清晰：Python 承载调度与模型实现，Rust 承担高性能数据面与路由；两者通过 rust/sglang-server 与 python/sglang/srt/ 的 FFI/HTTP 边界协作，近期提交热点显示 Rust server 正在统一多模态与生成请求的数据路径。

codemap.data_flow: 一次典型推理请求（以 OpenAI /v1/chat/completions 为例）的完整路径：1) 请求进入接入层，由 rust/sglang-server 或 python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/ 的 OpenAI 兼容服务器接收，解析 HTTP body 为内部请求对象；若是 Rust 入口，sgl-router 的 server/routes/chat.rs 会先做请求预处理（preparation）与路由选择。2) 对于启用 KV 感知路由的集群，sgl-router 通过 sgl-kv-indexer 的 gRPC 接口查询请求前缀匹配（PrefixMatch），结合 worker 负载（LoadStat，由 python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/load_publisher.py 发布）与路由策略（cache_aware、session_aware、power_of_two 等）选定目标 worker。3) 请求进入调度层 python/sglang/srt/managers/Scheduler，由 continuous batching + chunked prefill 逻辑切分为 chunk，RadixAttention 树形缓存（radix_cache）检查前缀命中，命中部分跳过 prefill 计算。4) 调度后的 chunk 进入执行层 python/sglang/srt/executor/GPUModelRunner，组装 batch 并调用 python/sglang/srt/model_executor/ 的前向逻辑；前向中逐层调用 python/sglang/srt/layers/ 的算子包装（attention、moe、linear、norm、rope、quant），这些包装进一步调用 python/sgl-kernel/ 的 Triton/CuTe/CUTLASS/FlashInfer 自定义 kernel。5) 前向完成后，采样（sampling）与 logits 处理在 model_executor 层完成，生成 token；投机解码（DFlash/Spec V2）会在该阶段验证或回退。6) 生成的 token 写回 KV 缓存（paged attention + radix_cache），调度器决定是否继续 decode 或释放请求；最终 token 流通过接入层返回客户端（streaming 或完整响应）。关键数据结构包括：内部请求对象（含 input_ids、sampling_params、radix_cache 指针）、LoadStat（worker 负载）、PrefixMatch（KV 索引结果）、batch 描述符、KV cache page 表。调度点包括：Scheduler 的 chunk 切分与 batch 组装、radix_cache 的前缀查询与插入、sgl-router 的 worker 选择、sgl-kv-indexer 的前缀匹配。

extension_points.how: 在 python/sglang/srt/models/ 下新增模型文件，实现对应的 nn.Module 与前向逻辑；在 python/sglang/srt/model_executor/ 或 layers 中注册；参考现有模型（如 llama.py、qwen.py、deepseek.py）与 docs/cookbook/ 中的 recipe
在 python/sglang/srt/layers/ 下新增或特化算子后端（如 attention_backend、quantization）；在 docker/ 下新增对应 Dockerfile（如 rocm.Dockerfile、npu.Dockerfile、xpu.Dockerfile）；在 3rdparty/amd/ 等厂商目录下添加特化实现；参考 [AMD] 与 [NPU] 相关提交

install:
# 1. 克隆仓库
git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git
cd sglang

# 2. 创建 Python 虚拟环境（推荐 Python 3.10–3.12）
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

# 3. 安装 CPU 专用依赖（依据 pyproject_cpu.toml）
pip install -e python[cpu]
# 或显式指定：pip install -e python -f python/pyproject_cpu.toml

# 4. 安装 Rust 工具链（用于编译 sgl-router）
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
source $HOME/.cargo/env

# 5. 编译 Rust sgl-router（可选，无 GPU 也可编译）
cd experimental/sgl-router
cargo build --release
cd ../..

# 6. 安装测试依赖
pip install pytest pytest-asyncio

# 注意：跳过以下依赖（需要 GPU）：
# - sgl-kernel（CUDA kernel 包）
# - flash-attn、flash-infer（NVIDIA 专用）
# - torch 的 CUDA 版本（使用 CPU/MPS 版本）
no_gpu_paths:

# CI 主要检查项：

## 1. 必需检查（PR 会被卡住）
- pre-commit：代码格式（black、isort、flake8）
- 文档 lint：mint broken-links
- Python 单元测试（部分 CPU 测试）
- Rust 编译和测试（cargo test、cargo clippy）

## 2. GPU 测试（需要 NVIDIA GPU runner）
- test/srt/ 下的模型推理测试
- benchmark/kernels/ 性能测试
- 多 GPU 分布式测试

## 3. 硬件特定测试
- AMD GPU：rocm 相关 workflow
- Intel XPU：xpu 测试
- NPU：昇腾测试

## 4. 提交热点显示的高频 CI
- test/registered/：23 次提交（核心测试）
- python/sglang/：45 次提交（主代码）
- rust/sglang-server：29 次提交（Rust 服务）

## 5. 避免 CI 失败的注意点
- 不要修改 .pre-commit-config.yaml 中的 hook
- 确保 Rust 代码通过 cargo clippy -- -D warnings
- 文档修改需通过 mint broken-links
pr_blockers: Python 单元测试（至少 CPU 子集）

pitfalls:
# 1. 依赖混淆
- pyproject_cpu.toml 用于 CPU 安装，不要直接用 pyproject.toml
- sgl-kernel 是 CUDA 专用，CPU 环境不要安装

# 2. Rust 编译问题
- sgl-router 依赖 tokio、tonic 等，首次编译可能较慢（5–10 分钟）
- 确保 Rust 工具链更新：rustup update

# 3. Apple Silicon 特定问题
- PyTorch MPS 后端支持有限，不要期望 MPS 加速
- 部分 Python 包可能需要 Rosetta 转译

# 4. 测试陷阱
- 默认 pytest 会尝试运行 GPU 测试，需显式过滤
- test/registered/ 中部分测试需要模型权重（需下载或跳过）

# 5. 调度器实例化
- Scheduler 依赖 KVCache 等组件，单独实例化需要 mock 依赖
- 建议从 test/registered/test_scheduler.py 学习正确用法

# 6. 文档站依赖
- docs/ 需要 Node.js >= 20 和 mint CLI
- 不要修改 docs.json 中的导航结构

# 7. 性能剖析
- torch.profiler 在 CPU 上功能受限
- 主要 GPU kernel 剖析必须在 Colab T4 上进行

# 8. 提交规范
- 提交信息需清晰（参考 feat:、[Bugfix]、[CI] 前缀）
- 大 PR 需拆分为 mechanical_provable 提交（参考 .claude/skills/mechanical-refactor-verify）

community.process: 入口：README「Getting Started」列出 Contribution Guide（https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html），仓库内有 docs/CONTRIBUTING.md、.github/MAINTAINER.md 与 .github/CODEOWNERS（后两者内容需验证）。注意：证据中抓到的 contributing 文本是 docs/ 文档站（Mintlify）的贡献模板——fork → 建分支 → npm i -g mint → mint dev 本地预览 → mint broken-links 检查链接 → 提 PR，并附写作规范。Issue 流程：.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE 存在，标题带强制前缀（[Bug]/[Feature]/[RFC]/[Roadmap]/[Tracking]/[Perf]/[Kernel]）；大改动先开 [RFC] issue（#33852、#23206、#41514 均为此惯例），跨版本工作用 [Roadmap] issue 跟踪并指派负责人（#21788、#21846、#28874）。PR 流程：.github/pull_request_template.md 存在（具体勾选项需验证）；提交信息带 scope 标签（[Bugfix]/[CI]/[AMD]/[Intel GPU]/[XPU]/[NPU]/[diffusion]/[CPU]）。质量门禁：.pre-commit-config.yaml、.isort.cfg、.codespellrc、.coveragerc；CI 由 .github/workflows、scripts/ci、test/registered（提交热点第 3 位，23 条提交）与 test/run_suite.py 承担，另有独特的 CI_PERMISSIONS.json + audit_permission.py + update_ci_permission.py 管理 CI 权限。治理：根目录 CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md，项目托管于 LMSYS 非营利组织。CLA/DCO：证据中未见，需验证。特别之处：.claude/ 目录（rules + skills，112 个文件）表明项目深度使用 AI 编码代理；README 明确「Long-term active SGLang contributors are eligible for coding agent sponsorship, such as Cursor, Claude Code, or OpenAI Codex」，长期贡献者可携代表性 commits/PRs 发邮件 sglang@lmsys.org 申请。另有 .devcontainer 支持容器化开发环境。

issues.title: [Bug] GDN packed decode and KDA replay decode round sigmoid(beta) through bf16; recurrent-state drift accumulates with context length
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

The GDN packed decode kernel computes the beta gate as follows.

```python
# python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/fused_recurrent.py:255
beta_val = tl.sigmoid(b_val).to(b.dtype.element_ty).to(tl.float32)
```

`tl.sigmoid` is evaluated in fp32, the result is rounded to the input dtype (bf16 in serving), then cast back to fp32. No bf16 arithmetic happens between the two casts, so the round-trip only discards the low mantissa bits of the fp32 sigmoid. The rounded beta then feeds the delta-rule update.

```python
b_v *= beta_val
b_h += b_v[:, None] * b_k[None, :]
```

`b_h` is the persistent SSM state, loaded and written back on every decode step, so this rounding error enters the state once per token and accumulates with context length.

The identical line also sits in the KDA replay decode kernel at `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/fused_recurrent_linear_replayssm.py:138`.

Two references show that keeping fp32 is the intended behavior.

1. In the same `fused_recurrent.py`, the KDA packed decode kernel keeps beta in fp32 on purpose (lines 490–493).

   ```python
   # Keep beta in fp32 (no bf16 round-trip) to match the generic decode
   # kernel `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`, which is the reference
   # validated against torch.
   beta_val = tl.sigmoid(b_val).to(tl.float32)
   ```

2. vllm carries a same-origin copy of this kernel (the packed decode kernel originated in vllm-project/vllm#36596; sglang#20627 imported it byte-identical, pre-fix). vllm fixed the identical line in vllm-project/vllm#53877 because "the beta rounding error accumulates with context length and can eventually degrade generation accuracy and stability". The fix was never ported here. Both sglang locations still match vllm's pre-fix code character for character (verified on current main `92dffebe`, 2026-09-10).

The suggested fix is one line per file, the same as vllm's fix.

```python
beta_val = tl.sigmoid(b_val)
```

### Measured impact

Verified on A100-PCIE-40GB, torch 2.9.0+cu129, kernel invoked directly at commit `9a1b1d2d5e`.

1. **Single step.** In the degenerate config (B=H=HV=K=V=1, zero initial state) the stored state after one decode step equals `sigmoid(b)` exactly, so the comparison reads the round-trip straight out of the state pool. State = `0.62109375` vs fp32 reference `0.622459352016449`, a rel err of 0.22%, which is exactly one bf16 rounding. With the round-trip removed, the state matches fp32 bit-exactly.

2. **1000-step decode drift** (B=1, H=16, HV=48, K=V=128, bf16 activations, fp32 state, vs an independent torch fp32 recurrence that keeps beta in fp32).

   | variant            | state rel-L2 @ step 1000 | max output rel-L2 |
   | ------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------- |
   | HEAD               | 1.41e-3                  | 2.19e-3           |
   | round-trip removed | 1.05e-7                  | 2.39e-7           |

   The gap between the two variants is four orders of magnitude.

3. **Attribution control.** The KDA packed decode kernel in the same file already keeps beta in fp32 (point 1). Setting its per-K gate to the GDN head scalar makes the two kernels mathematically identical, so the only remaining semantic difference is whether beta is rounded through bf16. Running the two HEAD kernels head-to-head on identical inputs yields state rel-L2 1.409e-3, matching HEAD-vs-reference (1.409e-3) to three significant digits, so the entire drift is attributable to the beta round-t

issues.title: [Bug] Falcon-H1 with tied word embeddings cannot serve a single request, tied LM head's `.float()` upcasts the embedding in place
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


`FalconH1ForCausalLM.__init__` points `self.lm_head` at the embedding **module** when `tie_word_embeddings` is set, and then calls `.float()` on it. `nn.Module.float()` converts that module's parameters in place, so the token embedding becomes float32 while every other parameter stays bfloat16. The first forward pass hands a float32 `hidden_states` to the first layer's fused RMSNorm, whose weight is bfloat16, and the kernel refuses to dispatch:

```
RuntimeError: rmsnorm(at::Tensor&, at::Tensor&, at::Tensor&, double, bool)::<lambda()> failed to dispatch data type Float
```

The scheduler dies with it. Under `sglang.launch_server` this happens during the server's own warmup, so the server never becomes ready, nothing is ever served.

### Reproduction

python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path tiiuae/Falcon-H1-Tiny-90M-Instruct --port 30000

script: [repro_sglang_falcon_h1_tied_head_float.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/d55a68a6505d3fbbb7f8ccd91c4be557#file-repro_sglang_falcon_h1_tied_head_float-py)

The server never prints "The server is fired up and ready to roll". Instead:

```
[…] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  …  File "sglang/srt/models/falcon_h1.py", line 432, in forward
  …  File "sglang/srt/models/falcon_h1.py", line 323, in forward
  …  File "sglang/srt/layers/communicator.py", line 739, in prepare_attn
  …      hidden_states = self.input_layernorm(hidden_states)
  …  File "sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py", line 601, in forward_cuda
  …      result = rmsnorm(x, self.weight.data, self.variance_epsilon)
RuntimeError: rmsnorm(…)::<lambda()> failed to dispatch data type Float
[…] Received sigquit from a child process. It usually means the child failed.
```

### Environment

`python -m sglang.check_env` on the arm this was found on:

```
Python: 3.12.8 | packaged by Anaconda, Inc. | (main, Dec 11 2024, 16:31:09) [GCC 11.2.0]
CUDA available: True
GPU 0,1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
GPU 0,1 Compute Capability: 8.9
CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda
NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88
CUDA Driver Version: 580.126.09
PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
sglang: 0.5.19
sglang-kernel: 0.4.6.post1
flashinfer_python: 0.6.18
flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found
flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found
triton: 3.7.1
transformers: 5.12.1
torchao: Module Not Found
numpy: 2.3.5

issues.title: [Roadmap][Feature] Support T-Head PPU
issues.body:
# [Roadmap][Feature] Support T-Head PPU ## 1. Motivation & Background This roadmap describes upstreaming **first-class support for T-Head PPU** (ZW810 / ZW810E, and the ZW-M890P card) into SGLang. ZW810, ZW810E, and ZW-M890P are hereafter abbreviated to 810, 810e, and 890p, respectively. T-Head PPU exposes a **CUDA-compatible API** through its torch backend (`torch.device("cuda")` is the only valid device type for PPU in PyTorch), so SGLang can run on PPU with a **vendor-isolated branching model**: we keep upstream CUDA code paths untouched wherever possible, detect the platform at runtime, and inject PPU-optimized implementations only where they matter. The work has already been validated internally across a broad model matrix (DeepSeek-R1/V3.2/V4, GLM-4.5/5.2, Kimi-K2.5/K2.6/K3, Qwen3 / Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, MiniMax-M2.7/M3, MiMo-V2.5-Pro, Llama4) with quantizations **bf16 / fp8 / mxfp4 / w8a8-int8 / w4a8-int8 / awq / gptq-marlin**, and features **TP / EP (DeepEP) / DP-attention / PD-disaggregation / EAGLE(E3) & MTP speculative decoding / CUDA graph (incl. piecewise) / context parallelism (incl. cross-machine) / DSA sparse prefill**. ## 2. High-Level Approach ### 2.1 Core strategies Four core strategies: 1. **Progressive PPU branching** — introduce a `PlatformEnum.PPU` / `PPUSRTPlatform` that inherits CUDA behavior, detected via the `PPU_SDK` environment variable. `is_cuda()` stays `True` and `device_type` stays `"cuda"` for PyTorch compatibility, so PPU changes are additive and cannot regress CUDA users. 2. **Plugin-hook injection instead of code edits** — use the existing `sglang.srt.plugins.hook_registry` (`@plugin_hook` with `HookType.REPLACE` / `AROUND`) to swap PPU attention ops (FA3, FlashMLA, DSA) into the community backends **without modifying `flashattention_backend.py` / `flashmla_backend.py` themselves**. Hooks are loaded from `platforms/ppu.py` only when `PPU_SDK` is present. 3. **Build-time adaptation** — AOT `sgl-kernel` build via `setup_ppu.py` / `pyproject_ppu.toml` / `common_extension_ppu.cc` targeting PPU 810/810e/890p (810/810e are roughly SM80-equivalent; 890p is roughly SM89-equivalent), plus a new `get_jit_cuda_arch_suffix()` interface so 810/810e devices JIT-compile with the `sm80a` arch variant. 4. **Targeted optimizations & tuned configs** — PPU-specific kernels (fused silu+mul+quant, DSA/DSv4 indexer quantization & topk kernels, INT8 indexer cache, FLA fast path) and shipped Triton/DeepGEMM tuned configs for `PPU-ZW810`, `PPU-ZW810E`, `ZW-M890P`, all gated behind `SGLANG_PPU_*` env flags with automatic fallback to the community paths. ### 2.2 Three-layer library mapping SGLang sits on the upper layers — the model layer on top, the backend layer in the middle — while the bottom layer is the PPU ops provided by the T-Head SAIL software libraries, injected into the backends via plugin hooks and env-flag dispatch: ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph SG_MODELS["Model layer (SGLang)"] MODELS["models: DeepSeek / GLM / Kimi / Qwen / ..."] end subgraph SG_BACKENDS["Backend layer (SGLang)"] ATT["attention backends
fa3 / flashmla / dsa / dsv4"] MOE["MoE runner
triton / ACEXT / deep_gemm"] QUANT["quantization
fp8 / mxfp4 / w8a8_int8 / w4a8"] end subgraph SAIL["PPU ops layer (T-Head SAIL software libraries)"] FA3["PPU FlashAttention-3
(flash_attn_interface)
@plugin_hook REPLACE"] FMLA["PPU flash_mla lib

issues.title: [Bug]: scheduler Req.decoded_text is never written: dead stop-string fallback at schedule_batch.py:1846 and empty DecodeStatus seed on eviction re-init
issues.body:
### description

`Req.decoded_text` is initialized to `""` at python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:1163 and never written anywhere in the tree. it has three readers:

1. scheduler stop-string fallback, python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:1846:

```
if stop_str_in_tail or stop_str in self.decoded_text:
```

under the `_stop_match_tail_len` window (python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:1735-1745, sized from `stop_str_max_len`, which normalize() sets to the max stop length, python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py:317-323), any live match ends inside `tail_str`, so the `self.decoded_text` clause is unreachable. dead check on the finish hot path.

2. the output streamer forwards it to the detokenizer payload, python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/output_streamer.py:478 -> :693 (`decoded_texts=self.decoded_texts`).

3. the detokenizer seeds `DecodeStatus.decoded_text` from it on first registration, python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:313. for a fresh request `""` is correct. but first registration also happens after decode-status eviction (the `SGLANG_DETOKENIZER_MAX_STATES` path, #2812, same territory as #41236/#41237), so the re-initialized status loses the accumulated-text base. at finish, `trim_matched_stop` runs over `s.get_decoded_text() + new_text` (python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:407-410), i.e. post-eviction text only. a stop string that completed partly before eviction and partly after escapes the trim. only `incremental_output` is emitted downstream (python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:417), so the full-text truncation itself is contained today.

### question

was the scheduler supposed to maintain `decoded_text` (the writer looks never implemented rather than removed), or should the field and its readers be dropped? i can send either fix:

- remove the field, the dead fallback clause at :1846, and the payload plumb-through, or
- maintain the accumulated text on the scheduler side so the eviction re-init and the fallback get real data (hot-path cost: an append per step).

verified on current main fc9e1c8d. no test pins the current behavior (no test references `decoded_text` on the scheduler Req).

issues.title: [Bug] GLM-5.3-Flash DSA k-pool indexer corrupts long-context (16K) NIAH needle digits — vLLM/transformers read the same inputs correctly
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


## Summary

Serving **GLM-5.3-Flash** on SGLang, long-context RULER NIAH accuracy collapses at 16K (~55%). The model attends the correct passage — it quotes the needle sentence verbatim — but emits **wrong digits** for the needle number. The same inputs, same model weights, and the *same fp8 DSA sparse-MQA approach* read correctly on **vLLM** and on **transformers**, so this is a SGLang-side bug in the DSA k-pool lightning-indexer path, not a limitation of the sparse indexer or of fp8.

## Repro

- Model: `GLM-5.3-Flash` (fp8 checkpoint), TP4 on 4×H200
- Benchmark: RULER `niah_single_2`, length 16384, greedy (`temperature=0`), `max_tokens` >= 512 (reasoning is always-on; short caps truncate before the answer)
- Two representative failing examples (0-indexed within the 16K validation split):

| case | gold needle | SGLang output | vLLM 0.30.1 | transformers |
|------|-------------|---------------|-------------|--------------|
| idx 6 | `2921859` | `7803` ✗ | `2921859` ✓ | `2921859` ✓ |
| idx 9 | `5418934` | `5906` ✗ | `5418934` ✓ | `5418934` ✓ |

Aggregate SGLang NIAH accuracy on this task: **4K = 100%, 8K = 95%, 16K = 55%** (n=20, `max_tokens=16384`, CUDA graph on, single stream). The 16K failures finish with `finish_reason=stop`, the model stating it cannot find the magic number — i.e. the needle key was dropped/garbled by selection, not truncated by the token budget (accuracy is flat 45–55% across `max_tokens` = 64/512/8192/16384).

## Why this looks SGLang-specific

Three engines, identical inputs / weights / indexer params (`index_kpool=4`, `index_topk=2048`, `index_n_heads=32`, `index_head_dim=128`):

- **transformers** — scores the indexer logits in **fp32** (`Glm5NextTextIndexer.forward` casts `.float()`): both needles correct.
- **vLLM 0.30.1** — DSA indexer uses **deep_gemm fp8 sparse-MQA on an fp8 K cache** (the same low-precision approach SGLang uses): both needles correct.
- **SGLang** — DSA **fp8 k-pool** indexer: both needles wrong.

Since vLLM gets it right with the *same* fp8 deep_gemm sparse-MQA, the corruption is not inherent to fp8 or to the sparse selection — it points at SGLang's k-pool indexer implementation (kernel semantics, key-scale handling, or the top-k selection over the pooled logits).

## Notes

- Reproduced on **v0.5.20** and on **latest main** (`nightly-dev-20260927-425a1f8f`, version `g425a1f8f2`) — not fixed upstream.
- `--dtype bfloat16` only shifts the main activations (weights stay fp8-detected, the indexer keeps its own fp8 key cache + fp8 scoring). It partially helps (recovers idx 6) but not idx 9 (`5709`), so it is a workaround at best, not a fix.

## Environment

- SGLang v0.5.20 and main `nightly-dev-20260927-425a1f8f`
- 4×H200, TP4, `--trust-remote-code`, fp8 checkpoint
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`, hybrid MLA + DSA sparse + KDA linear attention)

- Model: `GLM-5.3-Flash` (fp8 checkpoint), TP4 on 4×H200
- Benchmark: RULER `niah_single_2` (needle: "one of the special magic numbers for `<key>` i

issues.title: [RFC / HiCache] Same-node peer L2 sharing across DP ranks via /dev/shm
issues.body:
# [RFC / HiCache] Same-node peer L2 sharing across DP ranks via `/dev/shm`

## Motivation

In deployments running multiple DP ranks on a **single node** (e.g. one host with 8 GPUs and `--dp-size 8`), each rank maintains a fully private L2 host KV cache. When two ranks receive requests with the same prefix — a common pattern for system prompts, few-shot examples, or shared document context — Rank B cannot see the KV pages that Rank A already produced, and must recompute the prefix from scratch.

Existing HiCache L3 backends (Mooncake, NIXL, AIBrix, 3FS, LMCache) do solve cross-instance sharing, but they all go through a networked / service-mediated data path. For **same-node** sharing that is common in single-box multi-DP deployments, the network round-trip is pure overhead — the ranks are all local processes with access to the same physical DRAM.

## Proposed design: `shm_peer_l2` HiCache storage backend

Two DP ranks on the same node map the same L2 host pool via named shared memory (`/dev/shm` tmpfs). Metadata (key → owner rank + slot address) is exchanged through a small direct-mapped index (also in `/dev/shm`). When Rank B misses in its own L1/L2, it looks up the index; on a hit, it performs one `memcpy` within the shared SHM to bring the peer's page into its own slot, then DMAs to GPU — no recompute.

Compared to a hypothetical "share via existing L3 file" approach (see `shm_cross_dp` below), the peer variant eliminates the L3 data copy: only a 288-byte pointer per page is written, giving:

- **Storage overhead**: ~55 MB total for a 475 GB L2 (vs. ~L2_size for a full mirror)
- **Read path**: 1 index lookup + 1 SHM memcpy + 1 DMA (vs. L3→CPU_buf→L2 + memcpy + DMA)
- **Write path**: 1 GPU→shared_L2 DMA + 1 index write (vs. + 1 memcpy to L3 file)

### Correctness

A per-page **generation counter** in shared memory prevents stale reads: when Rank A evicts and reallocates a slot, its generation counter increments. Rank B compares the stored generation against the current one; a mismatch is treated as a miss instead of copying whatever bytes now occupy the slot. The check is best-effort (no full memory barrier) — the tiny TOCTOU window between the generation read and the memcpy is accepted as per the "stale reads may be silently accepted" contract already present in HiCache read paths.

### Operational envelope

- `--dp-size >= 2`
- All DP ranks on the **same node** (`/dev/shm` is node-local tmpfs)
- `--hicache-write-policy write_through` required (`write_back` only flushes on eviction, so Rank B would not see data timely)
- Optionally with `--hicache-io-backend kernel` and `page_first`/`page_first_direct` layouts

Auto-computed capacity (`page_num × 4`, 25% load factor) at startup; explicit override via `--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"peer_l2_capacity": N}'`.

Collision rate emitted every 10,000 writes; WARNING once it exceeds 10% (actionable — increase capacity).

## Existing prototype

A working implementation exists in a downstream fork. It shipped as two related backends registered through `backend_factory.py`:

- `shm_cross_dp` — shared L2 pool + full SHM L3 data file (simpler, more memory, extra copy)
- `shm_peer_l2` — shared L2 pool + tiny SHM index only (optimized; strict improvement)

Both reuse a common `ShmHostTensorAllocator` and named-SHM helpers added to `pool_host/common.py` and `storage/mmap/mmap_allocator.py`. Tests included: `test/registered/mem_cache/test_shared_l2_hicache.py` (CPU-only, `register_cpu_ci`),

issues.title: HiSparse Roadmap for Long-Context Sparse Serving
issues.body:
## Motivation

HiSparse[[Blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-04-10-sglang-hisparse)] is designed to support long-context sparse attention in SGLang with much lower GPU memory usage during decode. Instead of keeping the full KV history in HBM, HiSparse keeps only a small hot working set on device and backs the full token history in CPU pinned memory, swapping selected tokens back to GPU on demand.

For 1MB-class contexts and PD serving, the main challenges are IO overhead, kernel efficiency, KV transfer cost, and compatibility with HiCache/offloading, MTP, and more sparse model families. The roadmap focuses on improving model coverage, reducing long-context overhead, and making HiSparse decode robust in production PD scenarios.

Slack Channel：kv-cache-store

## Roadmap

### 1. Sparse Model Support

- [ ] MiniMax-M3 (Call For Contribution)
- [x] DeepSeek-V4
- [x] GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.1

### 2. Performance Optimization for 1MB Long Context

- [ ] For GLM-5.2, implement IO prefetch and compute overlap based on the IndexShared mechanism to reduce IO impact. #28523 
- [ ] Make HiSparse compatible with MTP. @huangtingwei9988 
  - Option A: Dynamic balancing: use MTP for small batches and HiSparse for large batches.
  - Option B: Direct compatibility based on [sglang#26445](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26445).
- [ ] Optimize HiSparse kernels by reducing the performance impact of heavy shared-memory usage and adopting a more aggressive parallelization strategy.   @DarkSharpness 
- [ ] Support TwoBatch Overlap to hide io latency  @SYChen123 @BJWang-ant 

### 3. HiSparse Decode Optimization in PD Serving

- [ ] Integrate with the Decode L2 RadixTree stack and make it compatible with HiCache offloading. @hzh0425 
- [ ] Fix HiSparse host-backed max request length: [sglang#28753](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28753).
- [ ] Prevent startup OOMs caused by over-estimating `max_total_num_tokens`: [sglang#28752](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28752).
- [x] Support NIXL DRAM KV destinations for HiSparse: [sglang#27563](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27563).
- [ ] Share CPU memory across TP ranks: [sglang#27370](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27370).
- [ ] Fix HiSparse max token configuration: [sglang#25288](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25288).
- [ ] Fix DSV4 HiSparse PD state page sizes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28879
- [ ] HiSparse V2: Unified logical kv space for hisparse https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32314

### 4. Support More Training-Free Sparse Algorithms

- [ ] Add extension points for Quest and other training-free sparse attention algorithms. @magicYang1573 @Ronnie-Rui

issues.title: [Roadmap]: SGLang Distributed KVCache System For Agentic Workload
issues.body:
### Motivation

As agentic workloads drive rapid growth in KV cache storage and transfer volumes, the existing PD disaggregation + HiCache stack is hitting significant bottlenecks. Meanwhile, HiCache's compatibility with hybrid models and other evolving features remains limited. There is an urgent need for a robust, high-performance distributed KV cache system capable of sustaining the heavy demands of large-scale agentic scenarios.

The core objective is to achieve end-to-end integration of PD incremental transfer, HiCache / HiSparse, pipeline parallelism, and Eagle — validated at scale on DeepSeek DSA (V32、GLM5) and Linear model (Qwen35) families.

### Q3 Roadmap

- [ ] **Agentic KV Cache Scheduling**
  - [x] Support session-aware RadixTree and HiCache ([PR #29173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29173))
  - [ ] Build a KV cache orchestrator across the router and engine to detect agentic workflows—including sessions, sub-agents, and tool calls—and provide scheduling hints such as `PREFETCH`, `DEMOTE`, and `PIN`; integrate with the router roadmap for global KV cache scheduling ([Issue #25760](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25760)) @hzh0425 
  - [x] Support direct L3 cache mode to enable a larger globally shared memory pool https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35687 @hzh0425 @huangtingwei9988 @maning00 
  - [ ] Enable supernode-wide sharing of L1 and L3 KV caches through Router scheduling and linker mode.
  - [x] Build a CPU-only KV cache simulator that replays representative agentic workloads without GPUs ([Issue #21891](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21891)) @littlefatfat
  - [ ] Support KVCache Sequence Split Mode to distribute VRAM pressure evenly. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30501 @Shunkangz 
    - [x] [PR #38356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38356) — Add logical-page placement and a rotated allocator to distribute KV pages evenly across shard ranks.
    - [x] [PR #37615](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37615) — Add sharded KV pools that store each rank's owned pages and assemble the full prefix for prefill attention.
    - [x] [PR #38468](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38468) — Add the KV cache sharding flag and wire the sharded pools into prefill scheduling and capacity checks.
  - [ ] Support Unified-KVCache Layout https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33651 @Shunkangz  @huangtingwei9988 
    - [ ] [PR #39727](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39727) — Add the page-unified host KV layout and topology-independent L3 keys for KV chunks.
    - [x] [PR #39726](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39726) — Add a JIT kernel that loads page-unified host KV back to the device one layer at a time.
    - [ ] [PR #39815](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39815) — Connect page-unified host pools and unified storage keys to the HiCache linker path.
 
- [ ] **UnifiedRadixTree Enhancements**
  - [x] Decouple the tree core and implement it in Rust to accelerate hot paths such as matching and eviction ([PR #29901](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29901)) 、https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32710
  - [ ] Integrate with KVCache-Canary to enable debugging capabilities for KV cache correctness. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32476

- [ ] **PD Disaggregation Integration**
  - [ ] Support an L2 `DecodeRadixTree` to increase transfer batch sizes and reduce GPU memory usage
  - [ ] Support SWA/DsV4/M

### Describe the bug

`session_params` on `/generate` is not type-checked. A single request with a non-string `id` or a non-integer `offset` raises a `TypeError` inside the scheduler's event loop, the scheduler SIGQUITs and the whole server goes down (every in-flight request fails, `/health` stops answering). No session needs to exist for the `id` case.

| `{"id": 123}` (control) | — | clean 400 "session id 123 does not exist" |
| `{"id": ["a"]}` | `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` (`session_id in self.sessions`) | server dead |
| `{"id": {"x": 1}}` | `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'` | server dead |
| `{"id": <open session>, "rid": <turn>, "offset": "abc"}` | `TypeError: slice indices must be integers ...` (`_concat_token_arrays`) | server dead |

`GenerateReqInput.session_params` is `Optional[Dict[str, Any]]`; `TokenizerManager` builds `SessionParams(**obj.session_params)`, and a msgspec `Struct` constructor does not validate field types (`id: Optional[str]`, `offset: Optional[int]` are annotations only). The values reach `SessionController.__contains__` / `Session.create_req` in the scheduler process unchanged.

Found it totally by accident: `/open_session` answers an error object (`{"error": {...}}`) when streaming sessions are disabled, and a client that passed that response on as the session id took the server down.

issues.title: [Bug][MLX] return_logprob silently returns empty logprobs without --mlx-enable-sampling, so /v1/score answers 500
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On the MLX backend, output logprobs are only computed when `--mlx-enable-sampling` is set (the flag's help text says so, and `MlxTpWorker._logprob_rows` returns `None` unless `_sampling_active(batch)`). Without the flag, a `/generate` request with `return_logprob: true` succeeds and returns empty `output_token_logprobs` / `output_token_ids_logprobs`, with no warning. Nothing tells the caller the option was ignored.

`/v1/score` is built on exactly that (`GenerateReqInput(return_logprob=True, token_ids_logprob=..., max_new_tokens=0)`), so on a default MLX server every `/v1/score` call fails with an opaque 500:

```
RuntimeError: output_logprobs is empty for request <id>.
  File "sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager_score_mixin.py", line 342, in _process_single_item_scoring_results
```

The Apple Metal guide (`docs/hardware-platforms/apple_metal.mdx`) lists the MLX key parameters but not `--mlx-enable-sampling`, so a user following it has no way to know that logprobs and scoring need the flag.

### Reproduction

```bash
SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --disable-cuda-graph --port 30000
```

```python
import requests
r = requests.post("http://127.0.0.1:30000/generate", json={
    "text": "Is Paris the capital of France? Answer Yes or No.",
    "return_logprob": True, "token_ids_logprob": [9454, 2753],
    "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0}})
print(r.json()["meta_info"]["output_token_ids_logprobs"])   # []  (also [] for output_token_logprobs)

r = requests.post("http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/score", json={
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", "query": "Is Paris the capital of France? Answer",
    "items": [" Yes", " No"], "label_token_ids": [9454, 2753], "apply_softmax": True})
print(r.status_code, r.json())   # 500 {"message": "Internal server error: output_logprobs is empty for request ..."}
```

Relaunching with `--mlx-enable-sampling` makes both work (`/v1/score` returns `[[0.9997, 0.0003], ...]`).

### Suggested fix

Either or both:

1. **Fail fast with a clear message.** `Scheduler.handle_generate_request` already aborts MLX requests that ask for prompt logprobs on the sampling path (`"Prompt input logprobs (logprob_start_len) are not supported on the MLX sampling path..."`). The same spot can abort a request with `return_logprob=True` when the MLX backend is active and `mlx_enable_sampling` is off: `"Output logprobs on the MLX backend require --mlx-enable-sampling."` `/v1/score` would then return that message instead of a 500, and `/generate` callers would stop getting silently empty logprobs.
2. **Document the flag** in the Apple Metal guide's key parameters, next to `SGLANG_MLX_CLEAR_CACHE_STEPS`.

I am happy to open a PR for (1) + (2) if @yeahdongcn agrees with the approach.

### Environment

- SGLang `main` @ 6103a8c743 (editable install, `srt_mps` extra)
- Apple M2, 16 GB, macOS 15.7.5, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.13.0, MLX 0.32.2

### Describe the bug

`SamplingParams.verify(vocab_size)` (`python/sglang/srt/sampling/sampling_params.py`) range-checks almost every sampling field, but it never checks an **upper** bound — even though `vocab_size`, the natural bound for `top_k` and `top_logprobs_num`, is the argument it is handed. `n` is not checked at all. The values then reach torch inside the scheduler, where the exception kills the event loop and the server SIGQUITs: every in-flight request fails and `/health` stops answering. (Not surprising at all) 

These are ordinary fields of the OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so no native-API field is involved. 

| request (`/v1/completions`, `max_tokens: 4`) | result |
|---|---|
| `"top_k": 2147483648` | `RuntimeError: value cannot be converted to type int32 without overflow` — server dead |
| `"logprobs": 2147483648` | `RuntimeError: selected index k out of range` — server dead |
| `"n": 2147483648` | request times out, server stops answering; no traceback in its log |
| `"min_tokens": 2147483648` (control) | clean 400 from `verify()` |
| `"top_k": -2147483648` (control) | clean 400 from `verify()` |
| `"frequency_penalty": 1e308` (control) | clean 400 from `verify()` |

The three controls show the intent is already there, `verify()` is exactly the place that rejects an out-of-range `top_k`, it just only looks downwards. Which is why I think this might be an issue of interest?

### Describe the bug

Serving **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** with **DSPARK speculative decoding** (`--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`) and **fp8_e4m3 KV cache** on **TP2, 2×B300 (288GB)**, the server passes startup and serves normal traffic fine, but a deep queue of long-context requests (170k–212k prompt tokens each) draining into a single prefill step reliably OOM-crashes the whole TP group:

```
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 27.20 GiB.
GPU 0 has a total capacity of 267.68 GiB of which 26.77 GiB is free. Including
non-PyTorch memory, this process has 240.52 GiB memory in use. Of the allocated
memory 235.23 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, with 5.54 GiB allocated in private
pools (e.g., CUDA Graphs), and 1.43 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated.
```

Both TP ranks hit the same error at the same time. The scheduler raises, and the whole server process exits (`kill_process_tree`). Every in-flight request drops. A second replica took over the failover traffic and hit the same crash 12 minutes later, at a smaller allocation size (15.40 GiB tried, 12.74 GiB free). So this is not a one-off. It reproduces whenever the queue depth and context length are large enough compared to whatever memory happens to be free at the time.

Traceback (identical shape on both occurrences, both ranks):
```
Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 5696, in run_scheduler_process

    self._buffer = torch.empty(

torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 27.20 GiB. ...

    return self._buffer[:num_tokens]
```

issues.title: [SM120] Field report: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in production on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (PCIe, no NVLink) - working config, measured throughput, rejected topologies
issues.body:
## Summary

Field data from running **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** as a production SGLang backend on **8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe-only — no NVLink)**, including the *only* topology we could get to start, measured prefill/decode, a speculative-decoding A/B, and the configuration traps that cost us real experiments. Posting because SM120 + V4.1-Flash users currently have to rediscover all of this from scratch.

Full write-up (with methodology and reproduction artifacts): https://github.com/Lei-010/hermes-agent/blob/main/docs/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-SM120-Performance-and-Production-Config.md

Related: vLLM field report https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56700 (same hardware, vLLM side), vLLM https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56892 (SM120 bug/perf tracker).

## What works

```bash
docker run --gpus all -d --name dsv41 \
  --shm-size=64g --ipc=host --network host \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -e TP_SIZE=8 -e DP_SIZE=1 -e EP_SIZE=8 \
  -e SPEC_ALGORITHM=dspark -e DSPARK_BLOCK_SIZE=6 \
  -e CHUNKED_PREFILL_SIZE=2048 \
  -v /ssd/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:/model \
  <sglang image>
```

Effective `server_args` (verified at runtime via `/get_server_info`):

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `tp_size` / `ep_size` / `dp_size` | 8 / 8 / 1 |
| `speculative_algorithm` | DSPARK, `speculative_dspark_block_size = 6` |
| `chunked_prefill_size` | 2048 |
| `context_length` | 1,048,576 |
| `kv_cache_dtype` | `fp8_e4m3` |
| `mem_fraction_static` | 0.72 |
| `max_running_requests` | 16 |
| `attention_backend` / `moe_runner_backend` | `dsv4` / `flashinfer_mxfp4` |
| CUDA graph decode / prefill | full (max_bs 16) / **disabled** |

**TP8/EP8 is not a preference — it is the only layout that starts** (see "Topologies SGLang rejects" below).

## Measured throughput (cold, single stream, tokens from `usage`, not SSE chunk counts)

128K cold prefill:

| Config | tok/s |
|---|---|
| `chunked_prefill_size=2048` (production) | **6,853** |
| same config re-run | 6,765 (−1.3%) |
| flashmla prefill backend | 6,845 |
| fused-MoE all-reduce | 6,828 |
| `chunked_prefill_size=4096` | 6,301 |
| `chunked_prefill_size=1024` | 6,012 |

32K prompt: ≈7,196 tok/s. GPU util ≈87% at 220 W of 600 W → **communication-bound on PCIe**, not compute-bound. ~7K tok/s looks like the ceiling for this board without NVLink.

Radix/prefix cache is the only large multiplier: cache-hit prefill **0.34 s for a 112K-token prefix ≈ 325K tok/s (≈39×)**.

Decode (client path over SSH tunnel, production config): prose 93.9 tok/s, structured/JSON 134.1 tok/s, TTFT 143–169 ms.

## DSPARK A/B (block_size=2, clean legs, each verified via `server_info` + acceptance length)

| Prompt class | DSPARK ON | DSPARK OFF |
|---|---|---|
| prose | 76.5–78.9 tok/s | 36.4–36.5 tok/s |
| structured | 120.3–120.5 tok/s | 36.5 tok/s |
| `accept len` | 3.0 tokens/step | 1.0 |

With DSPARK off the model flattens to ~36.5 tok/s regardless of prompt class — speculation is the difference between usable and unusable latency on this hardware. Production ships `block_size=6` (structured ≈237–252 tok/s vs 120 at block 2).

## Traps that cost us experiments (SGLang-specific)

1. **`--enable-expert-parallel` is a vLLM flag** — SGLang takes `ep_size`; the vLLM spelling is rejected outright.
2. **`docker run` must pass `TP_SIZE`/`DP_SIZE`/`EP_SIZE` explicitly.** Without `-e`, the container silently serves TP8 defaults and your "new" config never happens (we recorded a full sweep of false data this way before ad

### Motivation

NVIDIA released SANA-Video 2.0, a hybrid linear/softmax video diffusion transformer with Attention Residuals. The released 5B 720p checkpoint supports text-to-video (T2V) and text-image-to-video (TI2V).

SGLang currently supports SANA images, SANA-Video 2B and SANA-WM, but not the SANA-Video 2.0 architecture or its checkpoint. Diffusers currently has no SANA-Video 2.0 implementation, so NVIDIA's released implementation is the numerical reference. A native implementation is in progress.

issues.title: [Bug] Two concurrent requests using DisallowedTokensLogitsProcessor with different token_ids crash the server
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

With `--enable-custom-logit-processor`, two requests that use the built-in `DisallowedTokensLogitsProcessor` with **different** `custom_params.token_ids` and land in the same batch take the whole engine down: the scheduler raises `AssertionError` and SIGQUITs, every in-flight request fails and `/health` stops answering. One such request alone works.

`DisallowedTokensLogitsProcessor.__call__` (`python/sglang/srt/sampling/custom_logit_processor.py`) takes the first request's `token_ids` for the whole batch and asserts every other request's list is equal:

```python
disallowed_token_ids = custom_param_list[0]["token_ids"]
assert all(disallowed_token_ids == c["token_ids"] for c in custom_param_list), (f"{custom_param_list=}")
logits[..., disallowed_token_ids] = -float("inf")
```

The unit test `test_mismatched_params_raises` shows the assertion is intended at the processor level, but nothing upstream of it keeps two requests with different `custom_params` out of one batch, and the error is not contained to the requests involved: a legal pattern of client requests (two users each banning their own tokens) is a denial of service. Without the assert the same code would apply the first request's ban to every request in the batch, so the per-request semantics are wrong either way.

### Reproduction

SGLang v0.5.19 (0bcd8223); the same code is on `main` at 31b931edc3 (2026-09-25).
[repro_sglang_disallowed_tokens_batch_assert.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/65e56e5c3ce7b97fc53950d5a1a983e6#file-repro_sglang_disallowed_tokens_batch_assert-py)
```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 30000 --enable-custom-logit-processor

issues.title: [Bug] Aborting a constrained request while its grammar compiles returns HTTP 400 `BadRequestError`
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

A non-streaming request aborted through `/abort_request` normally returns **200** with `finish_reason: "abort"`. If the request is still in the grammar queue (its `regex` / `json_schema` / `ebnf` is being compiled), the client instead gets

```
HTTP 400 {"object":"error","message":"Aborted by AbortReq.","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}
```

`GrammarManager.abort_requests` (`python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py`) finishes those requests with `req.set_finish_with_abort("Aborted by AbortReq.")`, and `set_finish_with_abort` defaults to `status_code=HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST, err_type="BadRequestError"` — it is the helper for rejecting invalid requests. `TokenizerManager._handle_abort_output` then raises a 400 for any abort carrying that status.

So the same server-side abort reaches the client as "your request was invalid" or as a normal aborted completion depending only on whether the grammar was already cached: on a server where each request brings its own schema, most aborts that land early become 400s. Clients and gateways treat 4xx as non-retryable caller errors, and error-rate dashboards count them against the caller.

**Suggested fix**: finish grammar-queue aborts like the other abort paths (`FINISH_ABORT()` without a 400 status, e.g. `req.to_finish = FINISH_ABORT()` or `set_finish_with_abort(..., status_code=None)`), so the response is 200 with `finish_reason: "abort"`.

### Reproduction

SGLang v0.5.19 (0bcd8223); the same code is on `main` at 38ec649048 (2026-09-26).

[repro_sglang_abort_grammar_400.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/42826e1fe6a83f3bb15298ed3bb1ac56#file-repro_sglang_abort_grammar_400-py)

```bash

python repro_sglang_abort_grammar_400.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000

issues.title: [Bug] `/abort_request` with a rid also aborts every request whose rid starts with it
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`POST /abort_request {"rid": "job-1"}` aborts `job-1` **and** `job-10`, `job-11`, … — every in-flight request whose rid has `job-1` as a prefix. Requests the caller did not name end with `finish_reason: "abort"` part-way through.

The scheduler matches abort targets by prefix in every queue it searches (`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`, `Scheduler.abort_request`; the grammar queue in `constrained/grammar_manager.py` does the same):

```python
if recv_req.abort_all or req.rid.startswith(recv_req.rid):
```

`TokenizerManager.abort_request` only checks that the named rid exists exactly; the prefix match then reaches everything it prefixes. Caller-supplied rids are a documented request field (`rid` on `/generate` and the OpenAI endpoints), and sequential ids (`job-1` … `job-10`) or a shared prefix per tenant/session are the ordinary way to choose them; #36189 (pass `X-Request-Id` through as the rid) would make caller-chosen rids the default for many deployments.

Suggested fix: match exactly, plus the children the engine itself derives from the rid, e.g. `req.rid == rid or req.rid.startswith(rid + "_")` (the `<rid>_<i>` naming from `GenerateReqInput._normalize_rid`), or record the child rids on the parent's state and abort those.

### Reproduction

SGLang v0.5.19 (0bcd8223); the same prefix match is on `main` at 38ec649048 (2026-09-26).

issues.title: [Bug] #35061 rejects multi-node custom all-reduce v2 without expandable segments, causing ~19% Llama-4 TP8 regression on GB300
issues.body:
[by Codex]

## Summary

On a two-node GB300 NVL72 configuration (4 GPUs per node, TP=8), commit `7dcaf119875eaa2e14e479c039c367c69959f21b` rejects custom all-reduce v2 under the default non-expandable PyTorch allocator and falls back to a substantially slower collective path for Llama-4 Scout at concurrency 1. Making the allocator VMM-backed with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` admits v2 and restores throughput.

This appears to be a performance regression introduced by #35061's new `_is_vmm_backed_allocator()` capability requirement. The GB300 group is a valid single NVLink clique, and custom all-reduce v2 itself is the faster path for this workload, but a normal launch does not make the PyTorch caching allocator VMM-backed.

## Results

Llama-4 Scout BF16, random ISL=1000 / OSL=1000, 5 measured requests, 1 warmup request, streaming, concurrency=1. Each mode was measured three times after one server startup.

| Mode | Output throughput runs (tok/s) | Mean (tok/s) | Delta vs v2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| VMM-backed allocator, custom all-reduce v2 admitted | 220.66, 220.65, 220.67 | **220.66** | baseline |
| Same VMM-backed allocator, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2=0` (isolates the fallback path) | 180.02, 180.03, 180.03 | **180.03** | **-18.41%** |
| Default allocator, v2 left enabled but rejected by the VMM gate | 178.30, 178.25, 178.26 | **178.27** | **-19.21%** |

The first two rows were run sequentially on the same NVL72 pair and isolate communicator dispatch. The exact default-allocator validation was repeated on another NVL72 pair; it agrees with the forced-fallback control to within 1%.

## Environment

- GPU: 8x NVIDIA GB300, 2 nodes x 4 GPUs, within one NVL72
- Tensor parallelism: TP=8
- Model: `meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct`, BF16
- SGLang commit: `7dcaf119875eaa2e14e479c039c367c69959f21b` (#35061)
- Container: `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13`
- GPU compute capability: 10.3
- Driver: 580.159.03
- NCCL: 2.30.7
- Host architecture: aarch64

Use two GB300 nodes from the same NVL72, with four visible GPUs per node. Check out the suspect commit in the container:

```bash

issues.title: [Bug] streaming silently loses up to 5 tokens of text when detokenizer state is evicted mid-request
issues.body:
setup: with more than SGLANG_DETOKENIZER_MAX_STATES (default 65536) concurrent states, LimitedCapacityDict evicts an in-flight request's DecodeStatus (detokenizer_manager.py:153). this is the scenario from #2812 that the env var and the KeyError message at detokenizer_manager.py:378 exist for, and the re-init path at detokenizer_manager.py:311 exists to survive it without crashing.

the bug: the re-init uses recv_obj.read_offsets[i] as the count of already-committed tokens inside this chunk's decode_ids. but the scheduler sends read_offset as an absolute offset into the request's cumulative surrogate+decode id list: init_incremental_detokenize returns read_offset - surr_offset, a constant 5 (INIT_INCREMENTAL_DETOKENIZATION_OFFSET, schedule_batch.py:156) that never advances, while decode_ids is sliced to only the ids since the last send (output_streamer.py:479). on every chunk after the first, the constant 5 points at ids that are not in the chunk.

effect: after eviction re-init, while the accumulated decode_ids list has 5 or fewer entries, surr_ids == read_ids (detokenizer_manager.py:327-334), so new_text computes as "" and the text of up to the first 5 tokens generated after the eviction is never emitted in any streaming delta. if the request finishes inside that window the final chunk emits "" as well (detokenizer_manager.py:412-420 derives the tail from the same empty new_text), so the text is lost from the assembled stream entirely, not deferred. the first chunk is unaffected only because it carries the 5 prompt-tail tokens inside decode_ids, which is exactly what the constant 5 is meant to skip (first_iter branch of init_incremental_detokenize).

fix direction: send the committed-prefix count relative to the chunk, max(0, read_offset - send_decode_id_offset) at output_streamer.py:481, computed before send_decode_id_offset advances. first chunk value is unchanged (5), later chunks send 0, and the detokenizer needs no change because it is already faithful to what the field claims to be. will follow with a pr carrying a red-green test that drives the real scheduler accumulator and the real detokenizer with an injected eviction.

separately noticed while tracing this: req.decoded_text is initialized "" at schedule_batch.py:1137 and never written anywhere, so the stop-string fallback `stop_str in self.decoded_text` at schedule_batch.py:1821 never fires. not part of this fix; flagging it in case maintainers want it split out.

issues.title: [RFC] Allow prefill CUDA graph bs below chunked_prefill_size under post-capture KV sizing
issues.body:
## Summary

Post-capture KV sizing currently requires the prefill CUDA graph to have captured every reachable prefill shape. This RFC proposes relaxing that to the treatment the decode side already uses: allow the prefill bucket list to top out below `chunked_prefill_size`, and reserve activation headroom for the eager prefill instead of disabling the feature.

## Current behavior

`post_capture_kv_sizing_planned()` in `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py` bails out entirely when the largest reachable prefill forward batch is not already captured:

```python
if (
    prefill_cfg.backend == Backend.DISABLED
    or self.chunked_prefill_size <= 0
    or self.max_prefill_buffer_tokens() > max(prefill_cfg.bs or (0,))
):
    return False
```

`max_prefill_buffer_tokens()` is `chunked_prefill_size` outside PP dynamic chunking, and `prefill.max_bs` defaults to `chunked_prefill_size`, so the condition holds under default settings. It stops holding as soon as anyone passes `--cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill` below `chunked_prefill_size`, at which point the feature turns off with no log saying why.

## Why the constraint is stronger than the requirement

**The two values are independent knobs.** `chunked_prefill_size` is a scheduling ceiling; prefill `max_bs` is capture coverage. Requiring the latter to be >= the former makes "capture covers every reachable prefill shape" a precondition of post-capture sizing. That is an implementation convenience, not something the mechanism needs.

**What the mechanism needs is a bound on eager activation, not the absence of eager forwards.** The benefit of post-capture sizing is that graph memory is *measured* rather than *estimated*. That benefit is orthogonal to whether some forwards run eager. The decode side already operates on exactly this reading: `compute_post_capture_kv_resize()` in `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_components/kv_pool_runtime.py` accepts a captured decode `max_bs` below `max_running_requests` and raises the reserve instead of bailing out.

```python
eager_decode_gap = (... and decode_max_bs < running_requests)
if eager_decode_gap or mambaish_config(...) is not None:
    headroom_gb = max(headroom_gb, ...pre_capture_activation_reserve_mb(...) / 1024)
```

**The current gate makes two legitimate goals mutually exclusive.** Lowering prefill `max_bs` is a reasonable thing to want: the bucket list runs to `chunked_prefill_size` and its largest buckets cost seconds each to capture. Today you can have a shorter capture or post-capture sizing, never both.

The one defensible argument for the status quo is that the eager prefill activation peak is hard to estimate, and under-reserving means OOM. But decode carries the same uncertainty and chose to reserve. That argues for a more conservative formula, not for a hard gate.

## Proposal

Move the prefill condition out of the gate and onto the headroom path that `eager_decode_gap` already uses:

- keep `backend == DISABLED` and `chunked_prefill_size <= 0` as hard gates, since those are genuinely inapplicable
- when `max_prefill_buffer_tokens() > max(prefill_cfg.bs)`, warn and raise `headroom_gb` to cover the eager prefill activation peak

No new estimate is needed: `pre_capture_activation_reserve_mb()` already has a prefill branch keyed on `chunked_prefill_size`. Its 10GB floor on large-memory GPUs makes the relaxed path less profitable than the fully-captured one, but still better than the current fallback, which on top of the same activation r

issues.title: [Bug] Client disconnect during active request crashes entire engine (uncaught asyncio.CancelledError bypasses except Exception)
issues.body:
## Environment

- **System**: 4x NVIDIA RTX 6000D (SM120 / Blackwell, no NVLink, PCIe only)
- **Docker Image**: `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dsv41`
- **Image Digest**: `sha256:4a5d132a06a77c8331e15845f2e925adc788b00105097ad55409afa3f4fa4860`
- **sglang Version**: 0.0.0.dev1+gda64c5cbb
- **Model**: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
- **Python Version**: 3.12
- **Server Runtime**: uvicorn (as deployed in dev-dsv41 image)

## Description

A long-context chat completion request (~200,000 input tokens) was sent to sglang via `POST /v1/chat/completions` with a client-side timeout of 120 seconds. The prefill phase exceeded this timeout, so curl aborted the TCP connection mid-request.

**Instead of failing gracefully for that single request, the entire sglang engine process crashed**, causing a complete outage of all in-flight and future requests. This is a critical production robustness issue.

## Root Cause Analysis

The sglang engine has a request-state monitoring loop (in `tokenizer_manager.py`'s `_stream_one_response` / `_wait_one_response`) that periodically polls whether the client is still connected. This poll runs every `SGLANG_REQUEST_STATE_WAIT_TIMEOUT` seconds (default: 4 seconds from `environ.py`).

The poll calls `await request.is_disconnected()` (from Starlette), which internally calls `await self._receive()` on the underlying ASGI channel. When the TCP connection is forcibly closed by the client, uvicorn cancels the pending receive operation, raising `asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError` from *inside* that call.

**Key issue:** Since Python 3.8, `asyncio.CancelledError` is a subclass of `BaseException`, **not** `Exception`. This is deliberate Python design to prevent generic `except Exception` handlers from swallowing task cancellation. However, sglang's request-handling code has numerous `except Exception as e:` blocks throughout `http_server.py` and related modules. None of these catch `CancelledError`.

The uncaught `CancelledError` propagates all the way up the stack, and something at a higher level in the process interprets any uncaught exception as fatal, calling `kill_process_tree` and terminating the entire engine.

Because the disconnect check runs every ~4 seconds for every actively-processing request, this is not an edge case — it's a broadly reproducible failure mode affecting any request where the client disconnects (timeout, user cancellation, network blip, load balancer health-check churn) while the server is mid-generation.

## Traceback

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/sglang/lib/python3.12/site-packages/fastapi/routing.py", line 706, in app
    raw_response = await run_endpoint_function(

  File "/opt/sglang/lib/python3.12/site-packages/fastapi/routing.py", line 352, in run_endpoint_function
    return await dependant.call(**values)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py", line 1742, in openai_v1_chat_completions
    return await raw_request.app.state.openai_serving_chat.handle_request(
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_base.py", line 107, in handle_request
    return await self._handle_non_streaming_request(
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

issues.title: [Bug] A session turn with replace: true and no rid crashes the server ("dictionary changed size during iteration")
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Another issue find by accident

`SessionParams.replace` without `rid` is documented in `io_struct.py` as clearing all request nodes of the session ("the request node identified by `rid` (or all nodes if `rid` is None) is aborted and its children are cleared"). On any session that has had one turn, such a request kills the server:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/session/session_controller.py, Session.create_req
elif session_params.replace:
    if session_params.rid is None:
        for _, req_node in self.req_nodes.items():
            req_node.clear(self.req_nodes)      # SessionReqNode.clear: del req_dict[self.req.rid]
```

`clear` deletes from the dict being iterated, so the loop raises `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration` in the scheduler and the server SIGQUITs. (Iterating a snapshot would still hit a `KeyError` once a child that was already deleted through its parent's `clear` comes up in the snapshot.)


### Reproduction

SGLang v0.5.19 (0bcd8223); the same loop is on `main` at 38ec649048 (2026-09-26).

issues.title: [Bug] `/generate` does not type-check its fields: one wrong-typed field takes the server down
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`GenerateReqInput` / `SamplingParams` / `SessionParams` are dataclass and msgspec `Struct` annotations, and nothing enforces them on the native `/generate` path: `SamplingParams(**...)` and `SessionParams(**...)` are plain constructor calls, and a msgspec Struct constructor does not validate field types. Several fields are used for the first time inside the scheduler or the detokenizer, where the resulting exception kills the event loop and the server SIGQUITs — every in-flight request fails and `/health` stops answering.

The OpenAI-compatible endpoints have pydantic models and reject the *same values* with a clean 400, so the validation layer already exists; the native path simply does not have one.

A sweep of one wrong-typed or out-of-range field per request across every `GenerateReqInput` and `SamplingParams` field (637 requests, 7 values each) took the server down **25 times**, across 10 fields that group into 7 causes:

| field | value | exception in the scheduler |
|---|---|---|
| `positional_embed_overrides` | any non-conforming value (7/7 tried) | `AttributeError: '...' object has no attribute 'positions'` |
| `lora_id` | a list | `TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "list") to str` |
| `sampling_params.max_new_tokens` | `1.5` | `TypeError: slice indices must be integers or None ...` |
| `sampling_params.beam_width` | `1.5` | `TypeError: topk(): argument 'k' (position 2) must be int, not float` |
| `sampling_params.regex` / `json_schema` / `ebnf` / `structural_tag` | a list or dict | `TypeError: unhashable type` |
| `sampling_params.skip_special_tokens` | anything not a bool | `TypeError: ... cannot be converted to 'PyBool'` |
| `sampling_params.top_k` | `2**31` | `RuntimeError: value cannot be converted to type int32 without overflow` |

The remainder of the sweep was well behaved: 403 clean 4xx, 155 accepted, and 54 that answered `500 Internal Server Error` without dying (a wrong error class, not a crash).



### Reproduction


SGLang v0.5.19 (0bcd8223); the same unchecked path is on `main` at 38ec649048 (2026-09-26).
Use this script: [repro_sglang_native_field_crash.py](https://gist.github.com/Yunzez/f5c99cdaa9758cf3c713e0c7f74e7c5e#file-repro_sglang_native_field_crash-py)
```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 30000
python repro_sglang_native_field_crash.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 --variant regex
# one variant per fresh server: positional_embed_overrides, lora_id, max_new_tokens,
# beam_width, regex, json_schema, skip_special_tokens
python repro_sglang_native_field_crash.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 --variant regex --openai-control
```

```

POST /generate {'text': 'Hello', 'sampling_params': {'max_new_tokens': 4, 'regex': ['a']}}
  -> RemoteProtocolError: Server disconnected without sending a response.
/health afterwards: unreachable (ConnectError)
    server log: TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'

issues.title: [Perf] DeepSeek-V4 dsv4 prefill on SM120 (4x RTX PRO 6000, TP=4): ~2-7K tok/s vs ~12.5K reported via vLLM/marlin on identical hardware — expected? tuning guidance?
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues; found SM120 kernel-coverage work (#19637 roadmap, #30272) but nothing on dsv4-backend prefill throughput specifically.
- [x] English.

### Question / observation

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, 96 GB, TP=4, PCIe gen5, no NVLink), sglang v0.5.16, `dsv4` attention backend, `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE, fp8_e4m3 KV: **prefill throughput sits at ~2-7K tok/s**, while a stock **vLLM 0.25.1 recipe on identical hardware reports ~12.5K tok/s prefill at 256K context** (marlin MoE backend, expert parallelism, fp8 KV — https://github.com/hermia-ai/deepseek-v4-flash-sm120-stock-vllm). A 4-6× gap at large context on the same GPUs suggests the SM120 dsv4 prefill path has significant headroom. Is this expected/known, and is there tuning guidance?

### Our measurements (sglang v0.5.16 + the #33407 dispatch fix, DSPARK enabled)

- Aggregate prefill, 9 concurrent ~90K-token prompts: **~5,540 tok/s** (813K prompt tokens / 146.9 s wall; outputs negligible at 61 tokens each)
- Aggregate prefill, 3 concurrent ~650K-token prompts: **~2,805 tok/s** (1.95M / 695.5 s)
- Single ~650K-token prompt: **~2,870 tok/s** (226.4 s to first token)
- Live scheduler logs show per-batch input throughput starting ~6.5K tok/s at low sequence position and declining to ~1.8-2.1K past several hundred K tokens (attention cost growth expected — but the absolute level is the question)
- `--chunked-prefill-size` 4096 vs 8192: statistically identical wall time (146.9 vs 149.0 s on the 9×90K test), so chunking overhead isn't the limiter
- Startup notes `Breakable CUDA graph is incompatible with DeepSeek-V4 (heavy capture-pool memory pressure); disabling prefill CUDA graph` — so DSV4 prefill runs graph-less on this path
- `--max-prefill-tokens` at default 16384; `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` set (SM120 autotune instability, upstream rec)

### Relevant config

```
--tp-size 4 --trust-remote-code
--mem-fraction-static 0.90 --context-length 1048576
--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1
--max-running-requests 64 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64
--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4
--speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-attention-mode decode
--disable-custom-all-reduce --chunked-prefill-size 4096
--disable-flashinfer-autotune
```

(`--disable-custom-all-reduce` because sgl_kernel custom allreduce fails CUDA-graph capture on our PCIe GPU pairs, #11957 class.)

### Questions

1. Is dsv4-backend prefill on SM120 known to be unoptimized relative to the decode path (which benchmarks well for us — ~1,280 out tok/s at concurrency 64 with DSPARK)?
2. The vLLM recipe uses expert parallelism (`--enable-expert-parallel`) and the marlin MoE backend. Would `--ep-size 4` (or an EP/TP hybrid) be expected to materially improve MoE prefill on PCIe-only SM120 boxes with sglang, and is that combination supported with `flashinfer_mxfp4`?
3. Is the disabled prefill CUDA graph a meaningful contributor at these chunk sizes, or is the gap dominated by MoE GEMM kernel choice on SM120?
4. Any recommended experiments/flags for prefill specifically on this hardware class? Happy to run and report numbers — SM120 hardware is available for validation.

Context: prefill throughput directly bounds a fairness problem we've documented (a single large-context prefill monopolizes chunked-prefill admission for its full duration — several minutes at ~2K tok/s for near-1M prompts — starving concurrent small requests).

### Motivation

**Status**: Draft
**Author**: @rainj-me
**Created**: Apr 20 2026
**Version**: 0.1

# Rust Server Migration Plan

**Status:** Draft · **Last updated:** 2026-06-18 · **Owner:** Rain Jiang

Migration of the SGLang request front-half (everything from network ingress up to
the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler) from Python to a
multi-threaded Rust implementation.

---

## 1. Goals & scope

**Goal.** Replace the Python tokenizer/detokenizer managers and HTTP server with a
single-process, thread-per-core Rust implementation that owns the request lifecycle
up to scheduler submission.

**In scope:** HTTP(S)/gRPC/WS/h2/h3 server, request FSM, tokenizer & detokenizer
managers, multimodal encoder dispatch, control API (abort/flush/weight update etc.),
large tensor zero-copy handoff to the scheduler, cross-dp-group dispatch.

**Out of scope (this plan):** model kernels, attention backends, KV-cache internals,
quantization. The Rust server keeps the existing Python scheduler and GPU worker framework; it does not reimplement them.

**Non-goals:** behavioral changes to the public API. The Rust server must be a
drop-in for the Python one — same endpoints, same request/response schemas, same
streaming semantics — so it can ship behind a flag and be A/B'd against Python.

---

## 2. Architecture summary

The design this phase implement (decided separately; recorded here for context):

- **Two FSMs, one process.** An **ingress FSM** (per request, multi-threaded,
  thread-per-core) carrying a request from `Received` through validation and
  optional encode/tokenize to `Queued`; and an **egress FSM** handling streaming
  (`Streaming` self-loop → `Finalizing` → `Completed`). They are the two halves of
  one request's lifecycle, owned by the same core and meeting at the ring-buffer /
  scheduler boundary — no shared locks.
- **Six thread groups:** (1) **api-server** on an async runtime — accepts
  connections, terminates protocols; (2) **tokenizer-manager** running the
  ingress/egress request FSMs, CPU-core-bound; (3) **encoder** (core-bound);
  (4) **tokenizer** (core-bound); (5) **detokenizer** (core-bound); and
  (6) the python **scheduler** group within main thread. Groups talk only via channels — no shared locks across group boundaries.
- **Channels:** bounded **MPSC** TokenizerManager→Scheduler (`try_send` = backpressure), per-core **SPSC** returns; userspace rings carry the payload, no ZMQ involved. Crossing the Rust→Python boundary, request objects are serialized with **msgpack** so only immutable bytes transfer — keeping the GIL out of the hot path. Tensor data bypasses msgpack entirely and is shared through **pinned memory**, handed across as a handle rather than copied or serialized.
- **Zero-copy:** for encoded multimodal data, Python pre-allocates the pinned buffer pool at startup and Rust writes into slots by index during the encode/tokenize phase. Channels move slot handles (plus small msg

issues.body:
We noticed the current triton decoding kernel is very slow on long context. This is due to a missing flash decoding like optimization.

## Reproduce
We test the decoding speed with a context length of 200 and 2,000.

triton backend: The decoding speed drops from 147.64 token/s to 126.41 token/s
```
$ python3 -m sglang.bench_offline_throughput --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --dataset-name random --num-prompt 1 --random-input 128 --random-output 2048 --random-range 1 --attention-backend triton

[2024-11-30 05:10:04 TP0] Decode batch. #running-req: 1, #token: 234, token usage: 0.00, gen throughput (token/s): 147.64, #queue-req: 0
... 
[2024-11-30 05:10:18 TP0] Decode batch. #running-req: 1, #token: 2154, token usage: 0.00, gen throughput (token/s): 126.41, #queue-req: 0
```

flashinfer backend: The decoding speed only drops from 144.17 token/s to 143.35 token/s
```
