```

## Possible solutions
We can learn from the flash decoding triton kernel from lightllm and improve the [current triton decoding kernel](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_ops/decode_attention.py). Related links:

issues.title: [Feature] Reduce constrained-decoding overhead in TP
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

Currently, when tensor-parallelism (TP) and constrained-decoding are enabled, each TP worker will compile the same grammar across different TP ranks. This will incur non-trivial CPU overhead (for TP $n$, the overhead is $n \times$. In fact, we only need to compile the grammar and sample the result on the first rank.

A possible implementation can be:

1. Only apply grammar token mask on the rank 0.
2. Broadcast the next tokens id from rank 0 when there're grammars in batch.
3. Keep the old code path when there's no grammar in batch (i.e. no extra all-reduce).

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5c2915494c83f076a11afb2c3382eeb8a41f1974/python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py#L205-L217

issues.title: [Feature] Unified JIT / Precompilation Cache Directory
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation


## Summary

**Request:** Unify all JIT and precompilation cache paths under a single configurable root so that users and operators can manage cache location, size, and persistence in one place. The current situation is fragmented across multiple env vars and default paths (including `/tmp`), which makes it hard to reason about where compiled artifacts live and to reuse caches across runs or machines.

## Current State (Fragmented)

### 1. Triton JIT cache

| What | Env var / source | Default / behavior |
|------|------------------|--------------------|
| Direct `@triton.jit` (e.g. allocator, MoE kernels) | `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` (Triton runtime) | Triton default: `~/.triton/cache`; often overwritten by Inductor to a path under `/tmp/torchinductor_*` |
| SGLang override | `SGLANG_TRITON_CACHE_DIR` (if implemented) | e.g. `~/.triton/cache` or `~/.cache/triton` |

- Set only in some entry paths (engine, gRPC launcher, scheduler process); custom/PD launchers may not set it.
- When PyTorch Inductor runs first, it can set `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` to its own subdir, so later Triton JIT (including allocator) writes under `/tmp`.

### 2. PyTorch Inductor (torch.compile)

| What | Env var / source | Default / behavior |
|------|------------------|--------------------|
| Inductor cache | `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` (PyTorch) | `/tmp/torchinductor_<user>` (or similar) |
| SGLang override | `SGLANG_TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` (if implemented) | e.g. `~/.cache/sglang/inductor` |

- Default lives in `/tmp`, so cache is often non-persistent and can conflict with other users on shared nodes.

### 3. DeepGEMM JIT cache

| What | Env var / source | Default / behavior |
|------|------------------|--------------------|
| DeepGEMM cache | `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR` / `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` | `~/.cache/deep_gemm` |

- Set in `layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py`; separate from Triton/Inductor.
- 
## Problems

1. **No single root:** Triton, Inductor, SGLang torch_compile, and DeepGEMM each have their own env or default; some write to `/tmp`, others to `~/.cache/...`.

## Proposal

### 1. Introduce a single JIT cache root

- **New env var:** `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_ROOT` (or `SGLANG_CACHE_ROOT` if we want to align with existing `SGLANG_CACHE_ROOT` in custom_all_reduce_utils).
- **Default:** `~/.cache/sglang` (or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/sglang` when set).
- **Semantics:** All JIT/precompilation caches that SGLang controls should live under this root in fixed subdirs.

### 2. Standard layout under the root

Suggested subdirs (all under `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_ROOT`):

| Subdir | Purpose | Maps from |
|--------|---------|-----------|
| `triton/` | Triton JIT (direct `@triton.jit` and, when possible, Triton used by Inductor) | `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` |
| `inductor/` | PyTorch Inductor (torch.compile) | `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` |
| `torch_compile/` | SGLang torch.compile cache (hash-based, when using SGLangBackend) | `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR` + `torch_compile_cache` |
| `deep_gemm/` | DeepGEMM JIT | `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR` / `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` |

- If we keep backward compatibility, existing env vars (`SGLANG_TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR`) could override the default subdir path when set; otherw

issues.title: [Roadmap] sglang auto tuner
issues.body:
Now we have many kernel backends for moe (e.g., triton, cutlass), attention, and allreduce. For each kernel, we can also tune some configs (e.g., the tile sizes in triton fused moe). Tuning these kernels and choosing dispatching heuristics can be non-trivial. We would like to build a simple command that auto-tune all the kernels and dispatch heuristic for a model.

## Todo
1. Implement a script sglang.auto_tune to tune the kernels and hyperparameters for a specific model. It should dump the optimal tile sizes/dispatching heuristics for all kernels used in this model. Example usage:
    - `python3 -m sglang.auto_tune --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 --tp 8`
    - `python3 -m sglang.auto_tune --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 --tp 4`
2. Start from tuning the triton fused moe https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton
3. Implement a github action workflow that tunes 20 popular models on 5 common platforms.
    - The workflow should take in two arguments: a list of model names, and a list of runner names
    - Our CI has H100, H20, H200, B200, GB200
4. Auto choose allreduce algorithms (custom allreduce, nccl, nccl symmetric memory, torch symmetric memory).
5. Auto choose attention kernel backend and moe runner backend.
6. Auto tune the cutlass gemm kernels (with cutlass profiler)
7. Auto choose speculative decoding parameters for different batch sizes.

tasks.title: [RFC] Full-Duplex Recoverable Unit Failures 中「Unit 生命周期状态机」子项
tasks.source_title: [RFC] [Duplex] [Sessions] Recoverable Unit Failures for Full-Duplex Sessions
tasks.why_core: Full-Duplex 是 SGLang-Omni 的核心会话模型，RFC #2561 提出 Unit 必须按序 commit、失败可恢复的契约。实现 Unit 生命周期状态机是 Full-Duplex 生产化的基础。
tasks.goal: 基于 RFC #2561 的设计，实现 Unit 生命周期状态机（pending → running → committed / failed → retrying），确保单 session 内 Unit 严格有序 commit，跨 session 故障隔离。
tasks.first_action: 阅读 RFC #2561 全文，理解 recovery ladder（fast retry / rollback / reset / session fatal），然后定位现有 session 状态管理代码。
implementation_steps: 定位现有 session 状态管理：sglang_omni/serve/realtime/session.py 或 scheduling/ 相关文件。
设计 Unit 状态机：定义 UnitState 枚举（PENDING, RUNNING, COMMITTED, FAILED, RETRYING）。
实现 commit 顺序保证：每个 stage 维护一个 commit cursor，后续 Unit 不得越过未解决的更早 Unit。
实现 fast retry：若 Unit 失败且未修改持久状态，直接重试。
实现 rollback + retry：若 Unit 可能修改状态，先 checkpoint 再重试。
添加单元测试：模拟 Unit 失败场景，验证状态机行为符合 RFC 契约。
在 Mac 上跑测试确认逻辑正确。
validation: 单元测试覆盖：fast retry、rollback retry、session fatal 三种恢复路径
测试验证跨 session 故障隔离（A session 失败不影响 B session）
测试验证 commit 顺序不变量
questions: RFC #2561 是否已有维护者认领实现？还是仍在设计讨论阶段？
现有 session 状态管理代码在哪个模块？是 realtime/session.py 还是 scheduling/ 层？
是否需要先实现状态机骨架，再逐步添加 recovery 策略？
tasks.risks: RFC 仍在讨论中，实现前需得到维护者对设计方向的确认。
tasks.skill_fit: 分布式训练中的容错与状态机设计经验直接适用于 Unit 生命周期管理。
tasks.engagement: Issue #2561 无 assignee、无 open PR，仍在 RFC 阶段。此卡应先开 Issue 提案（或在 #2561 下留言），得到维护者对状态机设计的确认后再动手实现。

positioning.overview:
SGLang-Omni 是 sgl-project 下的多阶段（multi-stage）推理服务运行时，专门面向 omni 模型、语音 / TTS 模型以及统一多模态模型。它把一次生成拆成多个异构阶段——预处理、编码器、自回归引擎、talker、解码器、vocoder、聚合器——分别匹配不同的调度器与传输后端，对外暴露 OpenAI 兼容的 `/v1/audio/speech`、`/v1/audio/transcriptions`、多模态 chat 等接口。项目明确把自己定位在 SGLang 生态之上：自回归调度与 token 级执行复用 SGLang，而 pipeline 拓扑、阶段生命周期、跨阶段传输、模型族适配层、serving surface 由 SGLang-Omni 自己拥有。

从 README 与提交历史看，项目处于活跃但偏早期的生产化阶段：PyPI 最新 release 为 v0.1.7（2026-09-28），近一周提交热点集中在 Qwen3-Omni 内核级性能优化（MoE kernel compile、predictor 重叠发射、MRoPE 元数据裁剪）、MiniCPM-o HiFT decode compile、CosyVoice3 / MOSS-TTS 的跨阶段零拷贝、以及 XPU / Router 安全修复。README 把 Apple Silicon、Intel XPU 都标为 Experimental，CUDA 为默认完整支持后端。仓库结构上，`sglang_omni/`（739 文件）是主 Python 包，`sglang_omni_router/` 是 Rust+Python 的多 worker 前置路由，`sglang_omni_mlx/` 是 Apple Silicon 适配层，`OmniTyper` 与 `Voxt` 是 Swift / iOS 侧配套项目，`tests/`（610 文件）和 `benchmarks/`（87 文件）提供测试与回归基准。整体是一个正在从研究原型走向多硬件、多模型族产品化的 serving 框架。
positioning.problem: 解决的核心问题是：现代 omni / TTS / 语音模型不再是单一自回归 decode，而是由多个计算模式完全不同、依赖结构各异、资源需求不等的阶段串/并而成（如文本 thinker → 音频 talker → vocoder，或 ASR encoder → LLM → 说话人日志）。现有 serving 框架要么只覆盖纯文本 LLM（vLLM、TensorRT-LLM），要么只覆盖单阶段扩散/解码，无法原生表达这种多阶段 pipeline 的调度、阶段间 tensor 传输、异构硬件后端切换、以及流式 vocoder 输出。SGLang-Omni 的目标用户是：需要把 Qwen3-Omni、MiniMax Music 3、Higgs Audio v3、MOSS-TTS、Fish Speech S2-Pro、Qwen3-ASR 等模型以生产级延迟与吞吐部署在 NVIDIA CUDA、Intel XPU、Apple Silicon、ROCm、NPU 等多硬件上的推理工程师、MLSys 研究者、以及需要 OpenAI 兼容音频 API 的产品团队。典型场景包括：实时语音对话（全双工）、歌词→立体声歌曲生成、批量 TTS、流式语音、上传参考语音克隆、ASR+说话人分离一站式服务。
positioning.users: 1) 推理系统工程师：负责把 omni / TTS 模型部署到 GPU 集群，需要多阶段 pipeline 调度、跨阶段 tensor relay、NCCL/NIXL/Mooncake 传输后端、以及 OpenAI 兼容 API；2) 性能优化工程师：在 Qwen3-Omni、MiniCPM-o 等模型上做 kernel 级调优（MoE compile、HiFT decode、predictor 重叠、MRoPE 裁剪）；3) 多硬件支持工程师：为 Intel XPU、Apple Silicon MLX、ROCm、NPU 等非 CUDA 后端添加适配层；4) 研究者 / 评测工程师：使用 benchmarks/ 与 playground/ 跑回归、对比不同模型族；5) 端侧 / iOS 开发者：通过 OmniTyper、Voxt 把能力带到 Apple 平台。

landscape.difference: SGLang 是纯文本 LLM 的高性能 autoregressive 调度与模型执行引擎；SGLang-Omni 在其之上接管多阶段 pipeline、阶段间传输、vocoder/talker 调度、音频 API。自回归部分复用 SGLang，非自回归阶段由 Omni 自己拥有。
vLLM 聚焦单阶段自回归 LLM serving，无多阶段 pipeline、无 vocoder/talker 调度、无跨阶段 tensor relay、无 OpenAI 兼容音频端点。Omni 在音频/多模态 serving 层面是 vLLM 的上层扩展。
NVIDIA 官方优化，深度绑定 CUDA/TensorRT，单阶段为主；Omni 面向多硬件（XPU/ROCm/NPU/MLX）、多阶段、模型族更宽（TTS/ASR/音乐/Omni），但单卡极致优化深度可能不如 TRT-LLM。
专注 ASR 单任务；Omni 把 ASR、TTS、音乐生成、多模态 chat 统一到一个 serving surface 与多阶段框架下。
专注 TTS 模型本身；Omni 是 serving 运行时，把 TTS 作为多阶段 pipeline 之一，支持 batch/streaming/voice-clone 以及与其他模态组合。

positioning.stage: 活跃开发、早期生产化。PyPI 最新 v0.1.7（2026-09-28），近一周仍有密集性能提交；README 明确标注 Apple Silicon、XPU 为 Experimental；CUDA 为默认完整支持后端。

codemap.layers: SGLang-Omni 在纵向上可以划分为五层。最上层是接入层（Serving Surface），由 `sglang_omni/http/`、`sglang_omni/cli/`、`sglang_omni/client/` 以及前置的 `sglang_omni_router/` 组成，负责把 OpenAI 兼容的 HTTP/WS 请求、CLI 命令、Python SDK 调用转成内部 `StagePayload`，并落到 admission 控制与 scheduler 队列里。第二层是调度层（Scheduling & Pipeline Orchestration），核心在 `sglang_omni/scheduling/`、`sglang_omni/pipeline/`、`sglang_omni/admission.py`，分别承载 OmniScheduler、EngineFactory、Stage 生命周期、跨阶段 KV/tensor 传输策略与准入控制。第三层是执行层（Model Execution），由 `sglang_omni/model_runner/` 与 `sglang_omni/models/<model_family>/` 构成：model_runner 把调度请求翻译成 SGLang 的 `ForwardBatch`/`ScheduleBatch`，每个模型族则提供 `engine_builder.py`、`sglang_model.py`、`model_runner.py`、`stages.py` 把自己的多阶段拓扑注册到框架里。第四层是硬件与传输层（Hardware & Transport），`sglang_omni/platforms/`、`sglang_omni/mps/`、`sglang_omni_mlx/`、`sglang_omni/comm/` 把 CUDA、Apple Silicon MLX/MPS、XPU、NPU 的差异收敛成统一后端，`comm/` 下 `data_ref.py`、`kv_transfer.py`、`relay.py`、`stage_io.py` 提供共享内存、NCCL、NIXL、Mooncake 四种 tensor 传输路径。第五层是工具与支撑层（Tooling & Profiling），`sglang_omni/profiler/`、`sglang_omni/diagnostics/`、`sglang_omni/utils/`、`benchmarks/`、`tests/` 提供性能剖析、硬件诊断、回归基准与端到端测试。整个架构的关键思想是：SGLang 只负责单阶段 AR 调度与 kernel 执行，多阶段拓扑、阶段间传输、模型族适配、API 表面全部由 SGLang-Omni 自己拥有。

codemap.data_flow: 一次典型 `/v1/audio/speech` 请求的生命周期如下。第一步，HTTP 层 `sglang_omni/http/` 把 multipart / JSON 请求反序列化，经过 `sglang_omni/http/admin_auth.py` 与媒体策略校验后，在 `sglang_omni/admission.py` 做准入控制，生成 `StagePayload` 并送入 `sglang_omni_router`（若部署了多 worker）或直连 `sglang_omni/serve`。第二步，`sglang_omni/scheduling/omni_scheduler.py` 的 `OmniScheduler` 收到请求，根据模型族对应的 `stages.py` 把请求分解成多个 `SchedulerRequest`，每个 SchedulerRequest 携带 `ARRequestData` 或对应的 `payload_types.py` 中的强类型数据（如 `CosyVoice3SGLangRequestData`、`DotsTTSSGLangRequestData`），进入对应阶段的队列。第三步，调度器通过 `engine_factory.py` 中对应的 `TtsEngineBuilder`（如 `FunCosyVoice3EngineBuilder`、`HiggsTtsEngineBuilder`、`DotsTTSEngineBuilder`）构造出 `ModelWorker` 与 `ModelRunner`；这些 EngineBuilder 在构造期调用 `customize_server_args`、`generation_defaults` 把自己的阶段需求（关闭 CUDA Graph、调整 mem_fraction_static、设定 max_running_requests）注入 SGLang 的 `ServerArgs`。第四步，进入执行循环：`sglang_omni/model_runner/base.py` 的 `ModelRunner` 把 `SchedulerRequest` 翻译成 SGLang 的 `ScheduleBatch` 与 `ForwardBatch`，由 `sglang_model_runner.py` / `sglang_execution.py` 调用上游 SGLang 的 `GenerationBatchResult` 完成 prefill 与 decode；每个阶段特有的逻辑（如 dots.tts 的 latent recurrence、Fun-CosyVoice3 的 token-hop streaming、FishAudio S2-Pro 的 codebook 输出收集）由对应模型族的 `model_runner.py` 在 `before_prefill`、`post_prefill`、`post_decode`、`custom_prefill_forward` 钩子中实现。第五步，阶段间 tensor 传输由 `sglang_omni/comm/` 处理：`data_ref.py` 做零拷贝引用计数，`kv_transfer.py` 在 AR 阶段之间搬运 KV cache，`relay.py` 与 `stage_io.py` 根据部署选择共享内存、NCCL、NIXL 或 Mooncake 后端，把 talker 的 semantic token、vocoder 的 audio chunk 以 `OutgoingMessage` 形式推到下一阶段。第六步，最终阶段（vocoder / aggregator）把音频帧通过 `streaming_vocoder.py` 或 `streaming.py` 以流式方式经 HTTP WS 或 `client/audio.py` 推回客户端。关键调度点包括：admission 的并发上限、OmniScheduler 的阶段批化策略、SGLang 内部的 radix cache 与 chunked prefill 开关、以及 `generation_batch_policy.py` 中 `CudaGraphBackend` 的 batch size 选择。关键数据结构包括：`StagePayload`、`SchedulerRequest`、`ARRequestData`、`RequestOutput`、`SchedulerOutput`、`ForwardBatch`、`ScheduleBatch`、`GenerationBatchResult`，以及各模型族自定义的 `payload_types.py`。

key_types.name: OmniScheduler
key_types.role: 多阶段调度总控，协调预处理/AR/talker/vocoder 各阶段队列与生命周期

key_types.name: AsrEngineBuilder / TtsEngineBuilder
key_types.role: 模型族接入的核心抽象，每个模型族实现自己的 EngineBuilder 注入 ServerArgs 与 ModelRunner

key_types.name: ModelRunner
key_types.role: 执行层基类，把 SchedulerRequest 翻译成 SGLang 的 ForwardBatch/ScheduleBatch 并驱动 prefill/decode

key_types.name: SchedulerRequest / ARRequestData
key_types.role: 调度器内部的请求与阶段数据载体，贯穿从 admission 到 model_runner 的完整路径

key_types.name: StagePayload
key_types.role: HTTP 入口到调度器的协议请求封装，是 serving 表面的内部投影

key_types.name: ForwardBatch / ScheduleBatch / GenerationBatchResult
key_types.role: 上游 SGLang 的执行原语，SGLang-Omni 通过它们复用 SGLang 的 kernel 调度

key_types.name: current_platform
key_types.role: 硬件后端抽象，统一 CUDA / MLX / MPS / XPU / NPU 差异

key_types.name: DataRef / KVTransfer
key_types.role: 跨阶段 tensor 传输的零拷贝引用与 KV 搬运原语

key_types.name: CosyVoice3SGLangRequestData / DotsTTSSGLangRequestData
key_types.role: 模型族自定义的强类型请求数据，承载阶段特有状态（flow state、speaker embedding、codebook 等）

key_types.name: FunCosyVoice3ModelRunner / DotsTTSModelRunner / FishS2ProModelRunner
key_types.role: 各模型族的执行钩子实现，覆盖 token-hop streaming、latent recurrence、codebook 收集等特有逻辑

key_types.name: CudaGraphBackend
key_types.role: CUDA Graph batch size 策略，控制 prefill/decode 是否走 graph capture 路径

key_types.name: OutgoingMessage
key_types.role: 跨阶段消息封装，承载 semantic token、audio chunk 等流式输出

key_types.name: ServerArgs
key_types.role: SGLang 运行时配置，各 EngineBuilder 通过它注入阶段级参数

key_types.name: resolve_checkpoint
key_types.role: 模型路径解析，处理 CosyVoice-BlankEN 等特殊目录结构

extension_points.how: 在 `sglang_omni/models/<new_family>/` 下新建目录，实现五件套：`engine_builder.py`（继承 `AsrEngineBuilder` 或 `TtsEngineBuilder`，在 `customize_server_args` / `generation_defaults` 注入阶段参数）、`sglang_model.py`（继承 SGLang 的模型基类）、`model_runner.py`（继承 `ModelRunner`，在 `before_prefill` / `post_decode` 等钩子实现特有逻辑）、`stages.py`（描述阶段拓扑与 `StagePayload` 映射）、`request_builders.py`（定义强类型请求数据）。现有最佳参考是 `dots_tts/`、`fun_cosyvoice3/`、`fishaudio_s2_pro/`、`higgs_tts/`、`arkasr/`、`fun_asr/` 这六个族，它们的 engine_builder 都展示了如何把多阶段需求注入 SGLang。

在 `sglang_omni/platforms/` 下扩展 `current_platform` 的判断逻辑，并在 `sglang_omni_mlx/`（Apple Silicon）、`sglang_omni/mps/`（MPS）或新增 `sglang_omni/xpu/` 目录下实现对应的 `ModelWorker` 与权重加载路径。`pyproject_*.toml`（`pyproject_xpu.toml`、`pyproject_npu.toml`、`pyproject_rocm.toml`、`pyproject_musa.toml`、`pyproject_cpu.toml`）已经给出了每种后端的依赖模板，新后端可参照添加条件依赖。`sglang_omni/comm/` 的传输后端扩展需在 `relay.py` / `stage_io.py` 中注册新的 DataRef 传输方式。

kernel 级优化主要发生在两个位置：一是各模型族 `model_runner.py` 中的 `custom_prefill_forward` / `before_prefill` / `post_decode` 钩子，可插入自定义 Triton / CUDA kernel（如 Qwen3-Omni 最近提交 #2599 编译 MoE kernel、#2598 重叠 fused predictor、#2597 裁剪 MRoPE 元数据）；二是 `sglang_omni_mlx/` 与 `sglang_omni/mps/` 下的 Apple Silicon 适配层，可写 MLX 自定义 kernel。若需修改 SGLang 内核本身，应在上游 sglang 仓库贡献，SGLang-Omni 通过 `sglang==0.5.21` 固定版本消费。

extension_points.where: 新调度策略 / 传输策略
extension_points.how: 调度策略扩展点在 `sglang_omni/scheduling/generation_batch_policy.py`（`CudaGraphBackend`、prefill coalesce 策略）与 `sglang_omni/scheduling/engine_factory.py`（`SchedulerExtras`、`GenerationDefaults`）。传输策略扩展点在 `sglang_omni/comm/router.py`（选择 shmem / NCCL / NIXL / Mooncake）与 `sglang_omni/comm/kv_transfer.py`（KV 搬运调度）。准入控制扩展点在 `sglang_omni/admission.py`。

install: # 1. 前置：Homebrew + Python 3.10–3.12（Apple Silicon 要求）
brew install uv
# 2. 克隆仓库
git clone https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni.git && cd sglang-omni
# 3. 一键安装脚本（README Quick Start 明确指向）
# 内部会检测 arm64 + darwin，走 pyproject.toml 的 mlx/mlx-lm 分支，跳过 flashinfer_python[cu13]/flash-attn-4/nixl-cu13/mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13/kernels 等 CUDA-only 依赖
./install.sh
# 4. 失败回退：手动用 uv 创建 venv 并安装 Apple Silicon 子集
# pyproject.toml 中 Apple Silicon 专属依赖：mlx>=0.32.0, mlx-lm；CUDA 依赖通过 sys_platform != 'darwin' or platform_machine != 'arm64' 自动排除
uv venv --python 3.11 .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e . --prerelease=allow
# 5. 验证安装（应看到 torch=2.13.0, transformers=5.12.1, sglang 从源码编译的 all_mps 变体, mlx 已安装）
python -c "import sglang_omni, torch, mlx; print('torch', torch.__version__); print('mlx ok')"
# 6. 跳过/不会装上的依赖（pyproject.toml 中 sys_platform 条件排除）：
#   flashinfer_python[cu13]==0.6.18, flash-attn-4>=4.0.0b18, kernels>=0.14.1,<0.15,
#   nixl-cu13>=1.1.0, mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13>=0.3.10
# 这些是 CUDA relay/attention 后端，Apple Silicon 上 import 会直接报错，不要尝试安装
no_gpu_paths: # 能在 Apple Silicon / MPS / MLX 上真正执行的代码路径：
# - sglang_omni_mlx/ 整个包：Qwen3-ASR 的 MLX 推理路径（README 明确 Apple Silicon 支持 Qwen3-ASR via MLX）
# - sglang_omni/models/*/mlx/ 子模块：arkasr/mlx/, fun_cosyvoice3/mlx/, fun_asr/torch_mps_runner.py —— 这些是 Apple Silicon 专用 runner
# - sglang_omni/model_runner/audio_mlx.py, audio_torch_mps.py —— MLX/MPS 音频执行器
# - sglang_omni/mps/ —— Metal Performance Shaders 后端适配
# - sglang_omni/models/fun_cosyvoice3/engine_builder.py 中 uses_torch_mps() 分支（device.type == 'mps' 时走 Torch MPS 而非 MLX）
# - sglang_omni/models/fun_asr/torch_mps_runner.py —— Fun-ASR 的 MPS 实现
# - sglang_omni_router/ —— Rust+Python 路由层，无 GPU 依赖，纯 CPU 可编译运行
# - tests/unit_test/ —— 纯 Python 单元测试（调度逻辑、配置解析、payload 序列化）
# - sglang_omni/config/ —— 配置系统，CPU 可跑
# - sglang_omni/scheduling/ —— 调度逻辑（除 CUDA graph 相关）
# - sglang_omni/pipeline/ —— pipeline 拓扑定义
# - sglang_omni/profiler/, diagnostics/ —— 诊断工具（部分 GPU 相关功能会降级）
# 只能读代码或必须 Colab T4 验证的路径：
# - 所有 *cuda_graph*.py：encoder_cuda_graph.py, step_cuda_graph.py, vocoder_cuda_graph.py, prefix_cuda_graph.py, whisper_prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py
# - sglang_omni/comm/kv_transfer.py 中 NCCL 路径、relay.py 中 NIXL/Mooncake 后端
# - sglang_omni/models/qwen3_omni/ 的 thinker/talker 内核（MoE compile、MRoPE 优化均为 CUDA 专属）
# - sglang_omni/models/dots_tts/ 的 torch_compile 路径（configure_optimized_kernels）
# - sglang_omni/models/fishaudio_s2_pro/ 的 Fast-AR attention（强制要求 SM89/90/100/120 + flashinfer）
# - sglang_omni/models/higgs_tts/ 的 CUDA graph 路径
# - sglang_omni/platforms/ 中 CUDA 后端的具体 kernel 调用
# - benchmarks/ 下所有 eval 脚本（均需真实 GPU 推理）

test_suite: # 测试框架：pytest（tests/ 目录 610 文件，含 test_ci/, test_model/, unit_test/, utils/）
# 目录结构：
#   tests/unit_test/        —— 纯 CPU 单元测试（调度、配置、payload、序列化）
#   tests/test_ci/          —— CI 专用测试
#   tests/test_model/       —— 模型级测试（多数需 GPU）
#   tests/utils/            —— 测试工具
#   tests/data/             —— 测试数据
# 只跑 CPU 子集（Apple Silicon 推荐）：
pytest tests/unit_test/ -x -v --timeout=120 -k 'not gpu and not cuda and not trt'
# 预估耗时：unit_test 子集在 16GB MacBook Air 上约 5–15 分钟（取决于是否触发模型下载）
# 跳过 GPU 测试的标记（需验证具体 marker 名称）：
# 查看 pytest.ini 或 conftest.py 中是否有 @pytest.mark.gpu / @pytest.mark.cuda
# 若无显式 marker，用 -k 排除关键词过滤
# 注意：tests/test_model/ 下多数测试会尝试 import flashinfer 或 CUDA 相关模块，
# 在 Apple Silicon 上会 collect error，建议只跑 unit_test/
debug_tips: # 日志开关：
#   SGLANG_OMNI_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG —— 全局日志级别（需验证环境变量名）
#   sglang 自身：SGLANG_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG
#   各 model_runner 模块使用标准 logging.getLogger(__name__)，可通过 logging.basicConfig(level=DEBUG) 开启
# 断点入口（关键类和方法）：
#   - sglang_omni/scheduling/omni_scheduler.py:OmniScheduler.schedule() —— 多阶段调度主循环
#   - sglang_omni/pipeline/ 下各 Stage 的 process() 方法 —— 单阶段执行
#   - sglang_omni/model_runner/base.py:ModelRunner.before_prefill/post_prefill/post_decode —— 模型执行钩子
#   - sglang_omni/comm/data_ref.py —— 跨阶段 tensor 传输的共享内存路径（CPU 可断点）
#   - sglang_omni_mlx/qwen3_asr/ —— Apple Silicon MLX 推理入口
# Profiling 入口：
#   - sglang_omni/profiler/ —— 内置性能剖析工具
#   - sglang_omni/diagnostics/gpu.py —— GPU 诊断（Apple Silicon 上部分功能降级）
#   - .claude/skills/omni-gpu-deep-dive/scripts/omni_trace_pair.py —— 提交轨迹追踪脚本
#   - benchmarks/runtime_metrics.py —— 运行时指标采集
# 环境变量（需验证）：
#   SGLANG_OMNI_MLX_DEVICE=1 —— 强制使用 MLX 后端（Apple Silicon）
#   SGLANG_DISABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1 —— 禁用 CUDA graph（CPU/MPS 调试时）
#   Metal/MPS 相关：PYTORCH_MPS_HIGH_WATERMARK_RATIO=0.0 —— 调整 MPS 内存上限
ci: # CI 系统：GitHub Actions（.github/workflows/ 下多个 workflow，.github/scripts/ 含辅助脚本）
# 关键 CI 脚本：
#   .github/scripts/pr_ci_gate.py —— PR 门禁逻辑
#   .github/scripts/verify_omni_installed_pins.py —— 验证依赖 pin 一致性
#   .github/scripts/omni_missing_dependencies.py —— 缺失依赖检测
#   .github/update_ci_permission.py —— CI 权限管理
# 多后端 CI 矩阵（docker/ 目录对应）：
#   Dockerfile（CUDA 默认）、cpu.Dockerfile、musa.Dockerfile、npu.Dockerfile、rocm.Dockerfile、xpu.Dockerfile
#   CI 会分别在这些镜像中跑测试
# PR 会被卡住的检查（推测，需看 workflows 文件名确认）：
#   1. pre-commit：isort、check_if_else.py、check_leading_underscore.py 等代码风格检查
#   2. unit_test 子集必须在 CPU 上通过
#   3. 依赖 pin 一致性检查（verify_omni_installed_pins.py）
#   4. 多后端构建验证（CUDA/XPU/NPU/ROCm 各自有 CI job）
#   5. 可能有的 docs 构建检查（docs/ 含 Makefile 和 serve.sh）
# Apple Silicon 相关 CI：需确认是否有 macOS arm64 runner（README 标 Experimental，可能无专属 CI）
pitfalls: # 坑 1：sglang PyPI wheel 的 CUDA 依赖是 unconditional 的
#   pyproject.toml 注释明确说：'SGLang's PyPI wheel has unconditional CUDA dependencies, so Apple Silicon installs this exact tag from source with the all_mps extra'
#   解决：必须用 install.sh 或从源码编译 sglang 的 all_mps extra，不能直接 pip install sglang
# 坑 2：flashinfer_python[cu13] 的 cubin wheel 问题
#   pyproject.toml 注释：'Do NOT add flashinfer-cubin: PyPI has no matching cubin, and any leftover cubin wheel fails MiniMax DIT import'
#   在 Apple Silicon 上这些会被 sys_platform 条件排除，但如果你手动改 pyproject 或混用 pip install 可能触发
# 坑 3：torch==2.13.0 和 transformers==5.12.1 是硬 pin
#   这是为了匹配 sglang 的 pinned stack，不要随意升级，否则 sglang 内部会 break
# 坑 4：Apple Silicon 上 Qwen3-ASR 是唯一官方支持的端到端推理路径
#   README Hardware Support 表：'Apple Silicon | Experimental | Qwen3-ASR runs through native MLX or Torch MPS'
#   其他模型（Qwen3-Omni, dots.tts, FishAudio S2-Pro 等）在 Apple Silicon 上无法跑推理，只能读代码
# 坑 5：MLX 和 Torch MPS 路径的切换逻辑不透明
#   fun_cosyvoice3/engine_builder.py 中 uses_torch_mps() 依赖 sglang.srt.hardware_backend.mlx.runtime.use_mlx() 的返回值
#   如果 MLX 库存在但 device 是 mps，会走 Torch MPS；否则走 MLX。切换逻辑需要读源码确认，无文档说明
# 坑 6：tests/test_model/ 在 Apple Silicon 上会大量 collect error
#   这些测试会 import flashinfer、CUDA graph 相关模块，在 macOS 上 import 阶段就失败
#   建议只跑 tests/unit_test/，不要跑全量 pytest tests/
# 坑 7：sglang_omni_router 的 Rust 部分需要独立编译
#   sglang_omni_router/ 含 rust/ 子目录，需要 cargo 工具链
#   如果只跑 Python 层，需确认 python/ 子目录的纯 Python fallback 是否完整
# 坑 8：16GB 内存限制对 unit_test 的影响
#   部分 unit_test 可能加载小模型或 mock 权重，16GB 可能紧张
#   建议用 -k 过滤 + --timeout 限制，避免 OOM
# 坑 9：cache-dit==1.3.0 和 addict==2.4.0 是 hard import 不是 optional
#   pyproject.toml 注释：'hard import, not optional'
#   这两个包在 Apple Silicon 上也会被安装，如果它们有 CUDA 依赖可能会 import error（需验证）
# 坑 10：CONTRIBUTING 文件为空字符串（仓库 evidence 中 contributing 字段为空）
#   项目可能依赖 AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md 中的 coding style 指南
#   修改代码前必须读 .claude/skills/code-review/coding-style.md（AGENTS.md 明确要求）

community.process: 仓库没有独立的 CONTRIBUTING.md（根目录、docs/ 下均未见，contributing 字段为空）。从现有证据推断的贡献流程：1）鼓励先开 Issue 讨论——仓库大量使用 `[Roadmap]`、`[RFC]`、`[Tracking]`、`[Runtime Profiling]`、`[Feature]`、`[Bug]` 前缀的 Issue 模板（见 .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE 目录），几乎所有工作都先落到一个 Issue 再开 PR；2）PR 标题沿用 `[Perf]`、`[Fix]`、`[Feature]`、`[XPU]`、`[Apple]`、`[MiniCPM-o]`、`[Router]` 等前缀，与 Issue 标签体系对齐；3）pre-commit 已配置（仓库根有 `.pre-commit-config.yaml`，docs/README.md 明确要求「Run `pre-commit run --all-files` before opening a PR」）；4）CI 权限与代码归属由 `.github/CODEOWNERS`、`CI_PERMISSIONS.json`、`update_ci_permission.py` 管理；5）未发现 CLA / DCO 文件（需验证：仓库根目录仅有 LICENSE，未提及 CLA 或 DCO 签署流程）。
community.review_style: 从近期 PR 与提交推断：响应速度快（10-08 当天密集合入多个 perf PR），review 聚焦具体技术点——如 #2597–#2599 三个 Qwen3-Omni perf commit 是同一工作被拆成三个细粒度 PR 分别合入，说明维护者偏好小而精、可独立验证的 PR；安全类修复（#2581 Router admin key、#2583 profiler routes）同样快速合入。路线图类 Issue（#1754、#1883、#2459）评论数高达 10–27 条，说明设计阶段讨论充分，但一旦进入实现则 PR 拆分很细。整体风格偏「先 Issue 对齐 → 小 PR 快速迭代 → 性能可量化验证」。
etiquette: 得体：1）先开 Issue 对齐方案再写代码，尤其是新模型支持、新硬件后端、架构重构类工作——仓库里 `[RFC]`、`[Roadmap]`、`[Tracking]` 前缀的 Issue 是标准入口；2）PR 标题使用 `[Perf]`/`[Fix]`/`[Feature]`/`[XPU]`/`[Apple]` 等前缀，与现有标签体系保持一致；3）性能类 PR 附带可量化的 benchmark 数据（从 #2597–#2599 等 perf commit 推断，维护者关注具体收益）；4）提交前跑 `pre-commit run --all-files`（docs/README.md 明确要求）；5）小步拆分，避免巨型 monolithic PR。

不得体：1）跳过 Issue 讨论直接提大型重构 PR；2）在 Apple Silicon 上尝试安装 CUDA-only 依赖（flashinfer_python[cu13]、flash-attn-4、nixl-cu13、mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13、kernels）——pyproject.toml 已通过 sys_platform 条件排除这些依赖，强行安装会直接报错；3）在 Issue / PR 中不标注复现步骤或性能数据；4）忽视 CODEOWNERS 与 CI 权限配置。
what_they_want: Runtime Profiling 与性能优化：多个活跃 Issue 明确在招人做模型级 profiling——#1882（Dots-TTS）、#1883（Fun-CosyVoice3）、#1988（Fish Speech S2-Pro）、#2273（MiniCPM-o 4.5）、#2559（Nemotron-VoiceChat P0 pipeline profiling）、#2580（MiniCPM-o 4.5 Video-AMME runtime profiling）。这是当前最密集的需求方向，与候选人 GPU kernel / 训练性能工程背景高度契合。

Apple Silicon 支持扩展：Issue #1967「Apple Silicon support roadmap」有 23 条评论，assignee 为 AkazaAkane，目前仅 Qwen3-ASR 有 MLX 路径（sglang_omni_mlx/qwen3_asr），急需把更多模型族（尤其是 TTS / Omni）迁到 MLX/MPS 后端。候选人目前只有 MacBook Air，这是最现实的切入点。
新模型族集成：#2574（Irodori-TTS）、#2207（LLaDA-Uni）、#1864（Cosmos 3）、#2458（PersonaPlex）、#2459（Nemotron-VoiceChat 11b）均在跟踪新模型支持。
全双工（Full Duplex）会话：#1909、#2559、#2561（Recoverable Unit Failures for Full-Duplex Sessions）显示这是架构级优先事项。
多硬件后端：#1588（Intel XPU H2'26）、#1598（MUSA）、#2076（Ascend NPU）、#2416（AMD ROCm）——项目在积极扩展非 CUDA 后端。
代码质量与风格治理：#2195「Roadmap: Coding Style」显示维护者在推动统一编码规范。

gaps.gap: Apple Silicon / MLX 后端覆盖严重不足，只有 Qwen3-ASR 一条完整路径
gaps.evidence: README 表格明确标注 Apple Silicon 为 Experimental，仅列出 Qwen3-ASR；sglang_omni_mlx/ 只有 8 个文件且仅含 qwen3_asr；models/ 下虽有 fun_asr/torch_mps_runner.py、fun_cosyvoice3/mlx/ 等零星 MLX 适配，但 README 未宣称任何 TTS/Omni 模型在 Apple Silicon 上端到端可用。
gaps.why_you: 你擅长扩散模型推理加速与端侧部署（TensorRT/量化），把 TTS 模型（如 Fun-CosyVoice3、dots.tts、FishAudio S2-Pro）移植到 MLX/MPS 正是把端侧经验迁移到 Apple Silicon 的工作，且全程可在 MacBook Air 上开发与验证，无需 GPU。

gaps.gap: Apple Silicon 上缺乏系统性的性能基准与回归测试
gaps.evidence: benchmarks/ 有 87 个文件，但目录结构与文件名中没有任何 mlx/mps 相关基准；benchmarks/tasks/ 含 tts.py、asr.py 等通用任务，但没有 Apple Silicon 专属的 runtime_metrics 或 parity 测试；tests/ 下 610 个文件中未见 MPS/MLX 后端的单元测试或数值 parity 测试。

risks.risk: Apple Silicon 上某些 CUDA-only kernel（如 flashinfer、fa3、nixl）无法运行，导致 TTS 模型移植卡住
risks.mitigation: 优先选择已有 MLX/MPS 后端的模型族（如 fun_cosyvoice3、fun_asr）作为第一个移植目标；对 CUDA-only 路径写 platform guard 并开 Issue 跟踪

risks.risk: 仓库迭代快（周级发版），你的 PR 可能因冲突需要频繁 rebase
risks.mitigation: 保持 PR 小而专注；在 Slack 与 maintainer 同步开发意图；优先做文档/测试类 PR 减少冲突面

risks.risk: Apple Silicon Experimental 状态可能意味着 maintainer 暂时无意投入资源
risks.mitigation: 先用文档+测试+基准证明价值；在 Issue #1967（Apple Silicon support roadmap）下持续交付可见产出

risks.mitigation: 把 ownership 范围扩大到 models/*/mlx/、Apple Silicon 测试与基准，形成更大的责任面

risks.mitigation: 先用小模型（Qwen3-ASR、Fun-ASR）建立流程；对大模型只跑 request_builders 和 model_runner 的 CPU 单元测试

risks.risk: 社区沟通以英文为主，时区差异可能延迟反馈

issues.title: [Roadmap] Optimization for PersonaPlex
issues.body:
Optimize the PersonaPlex offline inference pipeline, including streaming speech output, for lower first-audio latency, faster full-recording processing and higher single-GPU throughput while preserving audio quality and request isolation.

## P0 — Baseline and profiling

- [ ] 1. Establish short/medium/long audio and concurrency baselines for TTFA, total latency, RTF, throughput and peak memory. @LiuYuHui
- [ ] 2. Separate Temporal Transformer, Depformer, Mimi, host launch, queueing and transfer costs to identify the critical path. @LiuYuHui #2506

## P1 — Depformer CUDA Graph and kernel fusion

- [ ] 1. Capture the fixed eight-codebook generation loop with CUDA Graphs, using batch-size buckets and reusable input/output and KV scratch buffers to reduce launch and allocation overhead. @lijrjyan 
- [ ] 2. Combine the eight independent temporal-hidden projections into a larger linear operation, then select each projection inside the depth loop to reduce small GEMMs and repeated input reads. Codebook generation remains sequential. @kalebguo #2469
- [ ] 3. Evaluate `torch.compile` or targeted fusion for FP32 RMSNorm and SiLU/gate pointwise operations to reduce intermediate tensors and kernel launches while preserving the normalization formula and dtype behavior. @LiuYuHui

## P2 — Cross-request Depformer batching

- [ ] 1. Combine per-request `spell_frame()` calls for compatible requests already in the LM batch, then scatter generated codes back to each request. @kalebguo #2478 
- [ ] 2. Support compatible sampling groups with request-specific RNG and forced codes; handle batch reordering, mixed-length completion and cancellation without adding a singleton batching wait. @yaourt137

## P3 — GPU-resident audio codes

- [ ] 1. Remove the LM → Code2Wav `.cpu()` → GPU round trip for the existing same-process placement using the supported transport path, with correct buffer lifetime and CUDA stream ordering. @guozhihao-224 
- [x] 2. Evaluate device-resident Mimi encoder → LM handoff separately, accounting for cross-process transport and timeline construction costs; retain a fallback for unsupported placements. @WilsonZheng0327 #2536 

## P4 — Mimi decode CUDA Graph and chunk batching

- [ ] 1. Capture fixed-frame-count `decode_step()` shapes with CUDA Graphs, using stable addresses for per-request convolution and Transformer state and correct refresh/reset on slot reuse. @lijrjyan 
- [ ] 2. Evaluate a small first chunk followed by larger decode chunks to amortize decoder launches and PCM transfers, balancing TTFA, chunk gaps and throughput. @nightdecode #2554
- [ ] 3. Batch ready, shape-compatible chunks across requests while gathering and scattering decoder state independently. Preserve causal context, output sample counts, final trimming and waveform continuity. @nightdecode

## P5 — Selective Mimi loading and length-bucketed encoding

- [ ] 1. Load only encoding components in the Mimi encoder stage and decoding components in Code2Wav, retaining each path's required quantizer weights to reduce resident memory and startup cost. @LiuYuHui
- [ ] 2. Batch similar-length caller audio using length buckets and a padding budget, with correct valid-length handling and output trimming; compare padding and queueing overhead against single-request encoding. @WilsonZheng0327 

Leave a comment with its number (e.g., **P2-1**) and link your issue or PR if you are interested with open tasks. Concurrent implementations will be credited as co-authors when merged

issues.title: [Roadmap] Optimization for Nemotron-VoiceChat 11b
issues.body:
Optimize the Nemotron VoiceChat-11B offline inference pipeline, including streaming speech output, for lower latency and higher throughput while preserving output quality.

## P0 — Pipeline profiling
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/2559 by @Lushali
- [ ] 1. Establish short/medium/long recording and concurrency baselines for TTFA, total latency, RTF, throughput and peak memory. 
- [ ] 2. Separate Perception, Thinker, Talker, RVQ, Code2Wav, host launch, queueing and transfer costs to identify the critical path.

## P1 — Perception graph coverage and length-bucketed batching

- [ ] 1. Measure replay coverage and eager fallback in the existing Perception CUDA graph path from [#2403](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/2403); extend capture to measured hot shapes where needed. @JINO-ROHIT
- [ ] 2. Evaluate length-bucketed cross-request audio encoding with a padding budget, independent causal state and valid-length handling. Preserve caller-channel selection, the seed frame and 80 ms frame alignment. @ChoHee15
- [ ] 3. Evaluate CPU worker parallelism for audio decoding/resampling and prepare contiguous input tensors once before device transfer. @JINO-ROHIT #2521

## P2 — Request-owned acoustic tensors and batched Thinker fusion

- [ ] 1. Deserialize acoustic input state once per request and retain a device-resident acoustic tensor, replacing repeated full-state reconstruction and per-frame transfers with indexed reads. @Kokoro2336
- [ ] 2. Pack text/function token IDs across the active batch, perform embedding lookup and acoustic fusion in batches, and reuse input buffers instead of constructing per-request GPU tensors each step. @Kokoro2336
- [ ] 3. Consolidate text/function output extraction and host transfers at the existing result boundary; reduce redundant argmax or synchronization where the sampled result can be reused without changing hook ordering or frame alignment. @yaourt137

Preserve retract behavior and release request-owned buffers on completion or cancellation.

## P3 — Token-to-character lookup and ready-request scheduling

- [ ] 1. Precompute tokenizer-derived token-to-character IDs and lengths, then use indexed lookup instead of repeated token conversion and small tensor construction in the Talker input path. @jiangLLM #2486
- [ ] 2. Schedule requests with available text independently of requests waiting for Thinker output, avoiding whole-batch stalls and repeated decode-preparation rollback through the shared scheduler. @XinhaoTheo

Preserve token ordering, KV accounting and terminal delivery, including cancellation while waiting for input.

## P4 — Talker RVQ precomputation, batching and CUDA Graph

- [ ] 1. Precompute the fixed generation schedule for each supported iteration/exponent configuration, removing per-call schedule tensor construction and `counts.tolist()` synchronization. @nagisa-kunhah #2503
- [ ] 2. Precompute codebook squared norms and padded codebook tables when weights are loaded; evaluate gather/reduction fusion for `depth_sum` without changing residual updates or FP32 quantization semantics. @Zheyuan-Lin #2461
- [ ] 3. Combine compatible per-request `generate_codes()` calls into batched execution, retaining request-to-row mapping and explicitly validating stochastic sampling behavior as batch composition changes. @nagisa-kunhah
- [ ] 4. Capture supported sampling/RVQ shapes with CUDA Graphs after removing host-side schedule work; evaluate `torch.compile` for remaining point

issues.title: [Tracking] MiniCPM-o4.5 end-to-end inference optimization
issues.body:
Related work: #2283 — mixed-reference / mixed-length Code2Wav batching and speaker-prompt caching.

Track candidate performance improvements across the MiniCPM-o4.5 inference pipeline. These are directions to investigate; applicability and end-to-end gains must be established by profiling and numerical validation before changing defaults.

- [ ] **Preprocessing:** reduce repeated media decoding/resampling and tensor construction; investigate CPU worker concurrency and reusable preprocessing, comparing Qwen3-Omni preprocessing and Qwen3-ASR pre-LM caching. Follow-up: #2356 moves speaker conditioning into preprocessing with bounded caching and same-reference deduplication; final-head validation pending.
- [ ] **Image/video encoder:** tune slice batching and resampler padding/shape buckets. MiniCPM-o already packs vision attention; investigate the remaining packing, transfer, and resampler costs.
- [ ] **Audio encoder:** investigate length-aware and cross-request batching, padding reduction, and layer CUDA graphs, borrowing from Qwen3-Omni audio graphs and Qwen3-ASR encoder scheduling while preserving chunk-causal masks.
- [ ] **Encoder caches:** evaluate CPU/GPU cache placement and capacity against transfer cost, hit rate, and colocated memory pressure.
- [ ] **Thinker:** profile prefill/decode scheduling, hidden-state capture and per-token copies; tune existing SGLang batching/graph/async-decode capabilities where measured.
- [ ] **Thinker → talker:** reduce hidden-state serialization and CPU/GPU round trips; investigate staged conditioning transfer using Qwen3-Omni's streaming handoff as a reference.
- [ ] **Talker:** investigate windowed repetition-penalty overhead, codec sampling, prefill construction and batch policy. Follow-up: #2353.
- [ ] **Code2Wav batching:** continue #2283; investigate length extraction synchronization, padding-aware batching/cost limits, prompt-cache policy and queue-wait settings. Follow-up: #2356 consumes preprocessed speaker conditioning and packs waveform output transfers; final-head quality and concurrency validation pending.
- [ ] **Flow / DiT:** investigate device-only CUDA graph boundaries, repeated per-step preparation, fused projections and variable-length execution, comparing Qwen3-Omni graph runners and CosyVoice packed DiT.
- [ ] **HiFT:** fold inference weight normalization (#2287); investigate padded work, output transfer and suitable graph shapes, validating stochastic excitation and per-row output boundaries. Follow-up: #2356 adds padding-budget batching with per-row masks and STFT/ISTFT boundaries; checkpoint-backed numerical equivalence and final-head GPU validation pending.
- [ ] **Streaming speech:** evaluate incremental thinker/talker/vocoder overlap only after establishing context requirements and quality impact; compare CosyVoice and the shared streaming vocoder machinery.
- [ ] **Runtime / placement:** investigate queueing, IPC, compute/transfer overlap, per-stage memory budgets and colocated versus split placement across concurrency levels.

Validated follow-up PRs will be linked to the corresponding items here. Keep numerical semantics, audio quality, tail latency and memory use in scope alongside throughput.

issues.title: [Runtime Profiling] MiniCPM-o 4.5 Video-AMME: video plus spoken question in, text and speech out
issues.body:
Sub-issue of #1798.

Related: #2284 (optimization tracker), #2399 (text to speech) and #2273 (voice cloning). Prior work on the same paths, with text output: charliechenye/sglang-omni#59 (preprocessing slot) and charliechenye/sglang-omni#62 (image encoder). wirybeaver/sglang-omni#13 covers audio input on MMAU.

## Goal

Profile `openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5` on the Video-AMME CI workload, rank what limits throughput and latency, and map each hotspot to open work.

## Scope

- Workload: `zhaochenyang20/Video_AMME_ci`, 50 spoken questions over 17 videos, CI request fields (fps 2, at most 128 frames and 401,408 px, `max_tokens` 256, temperature 0, no streaming, speech on) plus `seed` 0, which CI does not send.
- Load: c1 on one server and c8 on two fresh servers (A/A), each with a first pass (16 of 50 requests miss the image encoder cache) and a repeat pass (all hit).
- Layers, graded with the METHODOLOGY section 3 item 8 rubric:
  - Layer 1, strong: GPU busy (both processes) is 15.6 percent in the c1 cold trace and 17.1 to 27.6 percent in the c8 traces, so the limit is on the CPU side.
  - Layer 2, strong: py-spy (8 captures), traces and server timestamps agree that the slot spends its time in the first resize and the HF image loop, and that its two threads never overlap.
  - Layer 3, strong: c8 holds 0.330 to 0.333 qps on two servers, with an A/A band of 0.7 to 1.0 percent in qps and 0.8 to 1.0 percent in mean latency (derived from unrounded qps). nvidia-smi averages 10.8 to 12.7 percent at c1 and 15.4 to 19.6 percent at c8. Only c1 and c8 ran, since c8 already keeps the slot 99 percent busy.
  - **Layer 4 not run.**
  - Layer 5, strong for text: 50 of 50, accuracy 0.68 and identical text in every pass. No WER.

## Done when

- [x] Baseline, workload and reproduction commands are recorded.
- [x] Hotspots are ranked and graded.
- [ ] Each "no open PR" item below is picked up or ruled out.
- [ ] If the maintainers want it, an A/B of #2316 after its rebase, here with speech output (charliechenye/sglang-omni#59 ran it with text output).

---

## Baseline environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| sglang-omni | `5ed8a8d` (main, clean), plus the #2419 source change on the capture server. Main through `4a3e962` leaves this path unchanged |
| sglang / torch / transformers | 0.5.21 (the repo pin, over the image's 0.5.19) / 2.13.0+cu130 / 5.12.1 |
| Hardware | 1x H200 (143,771 MiB, driver 595.71.05) on an SGLang community node, Omni CI image. Server on 28 logical CPUs (Xeon Platinum 8480C) of the GPU's NUMA node, client on 4 others |
| Checkpoint | `openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5` @ `503e754` |
| Server flags | as in CI: `--thinker.factory.max_seq_len 32768 --thinker.engine.mem_fraction_static 0.55 --talker.engine.mem_fraction_static 0.15` |
| Layout | pipeline process (preprocessing, encoders, thinker) and talker process (talker, code2wav), one thread per stage |
| Data | `Video_AMME_ci` @ `7a37507` over the `Video_MME_ci` @ `833bd81` videos (16 at 640x360, one at 634x360), mean prompt 8,808 tokens |

qps is completed requests per wall second. e2e is the client latency, also the time to first audio since the client does not stream. Labels: est is not measured, derived is arithmetic on measured numbers (all shares and sums), external comes from another PR or issue.

## Headline

| Pass | qps | e2e mean / p50 / p95 (s) | Preprocessing service (ms) | Preprocessing busy share |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| c1, first | 0.208 | 4.819 / 4.712 / 6.261 | 3,000.0 | 0.623 |

issues.title: [Roadmap] Runtime Profile Agent for SGLang Omni
issues.body:
## Goal

Renamed on 2026-09-09 from Kernel Development Agents (KDA) to Runtime Profile Agent. Current scope: profile each model's runtime first, optimize at the scheduling and orchestration layer while the GPU is still idle, and enter kernel work only once the GPU is busy. The kernel stage keeps the adjudication protocol below.

Make agent-driven runtime optimization a repeatable, adjudicated pipeline for SGLang Omni. A generated change is cheap. A trusted change is expensive. The pipeline spends its effort on the second part.

Founding case study: #1608 by @junliu-mde. External references: the [agent assisted SGLang development write-up](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-02-agent-assisted-sglang-development) and [PolyArch humanize](https://github.com/PolyArch/humanize).

## Evaluation protocol (v0, comments welcome)

Every candidate passes the same protocol before any gain is claimed:

1. A correctness gate declared up front: bitwise identity under a controlled batching protocol, or for ASR possibly token identity plus a bounded WER regression, see the open question below.
2. An isolated benchmark against a functionally equivalent baseline under the same inputs, launch path, and compile flags. Control for warm-up and temporal drift, for example interleaved A/B or A-B-A with the first round discarded, and require the effect to clear the measured noise band.
3. Positive evidence the new code path actually executed, from counters or traces. Absence of errors is not evidence.
4. An end-to-end measurement on the target workload. Isolated wins that do not translate end-to-end are retained as optimization inventory but are not counted as delivered gains (#1608 documents this in detail). Match workload size to the effect being measured. In the #1620 reproduction, a 64 sample quick gate could not resolve a c16 effect that a 1088 clip run resolved (see comments). When the noise band is wider than the expected effect, an inconclusive measurement is a rerun trigger rather than evidence of no gain (see finals comment).
5. Independent reproduction before a merge recommendation.

Distilled from #1608, #1418 and the MTD kernel sweep. Corrections welcome, especially from anyone who has hit cases this does not cover.

## Stage 0: calibration (first, about one week)

Run candidate models through tasks with known answers, so the grader is validated against ground truth before we trust it on open problems.

- [x] Main task: reproduce the fused seeded sampling kernel adjudicated in #1608. Network disabled, repository pinned to a fixed commit, graded automatically on the correctness gate and the isolated benchmark.
- [x] Judgment task: predict and explain the end-to-end effect of that kernel. The reference answer is in #1608.
- [x] Finals, top candidates only: reproduce #1620 from its pre-merge base and validate the full chain including end-to-end, since that PR has verified gains of 3.3 to 6.4 percent.

Output per candidate model: pass rate at each gate, accuracy of the end-to-end judgment, and cost per adjudicated task. Plus a grading harness hardened on known answers.

## Stage 1: target qualification

Targets enter the hunt list only with quantified headroom in a regime where kernel gains can cash.

Current candidates:

- [ ] #1259 Fun-ASR encoder: launch bound, not compute bound. On current main, the bucketed CUDA graphs from #1369 are enabled by default and outperform torch.compile by 2.6x at B1 (eager 19.1 ms, compile 13.6 ms, graph 5.2 ms). The earl

# Goal

Support Cosmos 3 Nano, Edge, and Super in SGLang-Omni through native SGLang execution and reusable adapters. Native SRT and multimodal_gen own model loading, preprocessing, scheduling, KV management, and parallelism. Omni owns serving integration and interleaved orchestration.

Qualify each checkpoint, feature, and topology independently.

# Roadmap

### Phase 1: Shared foundations and Nano visual serving

RFC: #2183

- [ ] Establish native runtime and generation prerequisites.

  - [ ] Settle native runtime startup, rollback, and shutdown ownership. Planned SGLang PR.
  - [ ] Settle generation cancellation, media-job lifetime, and worker-failure propagation. Planned SGLang PR.
  - [ ] Pin an SGLang release with these prerequisites so Cosmos 3 generation starts from published packages.

- [ ] Integrate Nano visual serving through native SGLang.

  - [ ] Add T2I, T2V, and I2V generation through native DiffGenerator. #2050
  - [ ] Compose native image, video, and action HTTP routes with shared SDK execution. #2048

### Phase 2: Nano full Omni

- [ ] Integrate shared interleaved reasoning, generation, and generated-media re-ingestion.

  - [ ] Add the reusable UMM controller, continuation routing, and ordered output. #2204
  - [ ] Integrate Nano native stages, image/video feedback, and HTTP/SDK delivery. #2205

- [ ] Complete Nano modality support.

  - [ ] Complete V2V conditioning and quality qualification.
  - [ ] Add 48 kHz stereo sound with audiovisual synchronization.
  - [ ] Add action forward and inverse dynamics, then qualify Nano Policy DROID independently.

### Phase 3: Edge support and low latency

Edge development can proceed alongside Nano full-Omni work after the shared foundations.

### Phase 4: Super and specialized checkpoints

Super integration reuses the shared adapters and requires independent modality and topology qualification.

issues.title: [RFC] [Duplex] [Sessions] Recoverable Unit Failures for Full-Duplex Sessions
issues.body:
## Summary

Full duplex sessions are long lived and stateful. Today, an unexpected Unit-processing exception is effectively session fatal. That is safe, but too coarse.

We propose a stricter and more useful contract:

> **Units must commit successfully in order. Execution may be retried, but a failed Unit must not create a hole in persistent session state.**

For one session:

```text
U0 success
U1 success
U2 fail
   ↓
retry U2
   ↓
U2 success
U3 success
```

Not:

```text
U0 success
U1 success
U2 dropped
U3 success
```

For stateful Full Duplex, skipping a Unit can make later state ambiguous and produce incorrect responses.

---

## Goals

### 1. Isolate failures across sessions

Batching is an execution optimization, not a failure domain.

If one row fails:

```text
[A/U8, B/U3, C/U19]

A/U8  success
B/U3  fail
C/U19 success
```

A and C must commit normally. Only B/U3 enters recovery.

A failure in one session must never fail unrelated sessions in the same batch or pipeline.

### 2. Preserve strict in-order commit within a session

For each stateful stage:

```text
commit(U0) < commit(U1) < commit(U2) < ...
```

A later Unit may already be resident elsewhere in the pipeline, but it must not commit past an unresolved earlier Unit at the same stage.

### 3. Recover the failed Unit instead of skipping it

The preferred recovery ladder is:

```text
fast retry
  ↓
rollback + retry
  ↓
reset/reconstruct state + retry
  ↓
session fatal
```

Session failure is the final fallback, not the first response to a Unit failure.

---

## Recovery Model

### Fast retry

If a failed attempt did not change persistent state:

```text
state = S2

run U3
→ fail
→ state still S2

retry U3
→ success
→ commit S3
```

This should be the cheapest recovery path.

### Rollback + retry

If the attempt may mutate state, restore the pre-Unit state first:

```text
checkpoint S2
→ run U3
→ partial mutation
→ fail
→ restore S2
→ retry U3
```

The checkpoint can be model-specific, for example:

- retained KV length;
- staged metadata committed only on success;
- cache/state cursor;
- small per-session state snapshot.

### Reset/reconstruct + retry

If rollback is unavailable but the stage can rebuild from committed history:

```text
U0 U1 U2 committed
U3 corrupts live state
→ reset stage state
→ rebuild through U2
→ retry U3
```

Only when the stage cannot restore a known-good state should the whole session fail.

---

## Exactly-once Commit, Not Exactly-once Execution

A Unit may execute more than once:

```text
U3 attempt 1 → fail
U3 attempt 2 → success
```

but it must commit only once.

Any externally visible output from a failed attempt must not leak.

Conceptually:

```text
run U3
→ buffer attempt-local outputs/state
→ success
→ publish outputs + commit state
```

On failure:

```text
discard attempt-local outputs
restore known-good state
retry
```

---

## Latency and Backpressure

Recovery must remain bounded for realtime use.

We should prefer a small retry budget, for example:

```text
1 fast retry
then
1 reset/rebuild retry
then
fatal
```

No long exponential backoff.

If one session is retrying:

- that session may temporarily stop advancing;
- its bounded in-flight window may fill and apply backpressure;
- unrelated sessions continue normally.

Temporary per-session backpressure is preferable to creating a semantic hole.

---

## Interaction with Batching

For a batched append:

```text
[A/U8, B/U3, C/U19]
```

if B/U3 fails:

```text
A/U8  commit
C/U19 c

issues.title: [Nemotron-VoiceChat] P0 — Pipeline profiling
issues.body:
# VoiceChat 11B Performance Benchmark & Critical Path Analysis

## 1. Summary

### 1.1 Key Takeaway
VoiceChat 11B runs on a single H100 80GB, but the offline pipeline is only slightly faster than real time (**RTF 0.80–0.92**). The end-to-end critical path is **Perception + Talker**. Nearly all Talker and Thinker time is **CPU launch overhead (host launch-bound)**.

### 1.2 Model & Resources
* **Model**: NVIDIA NemotronLabs VoiceChat 11B, an end-to-end full-duplex speech-to-speech model (11B params). Checkpoint is a single fp32 `model.safetensors` (44.38 GB). Runs frame-locked at 12.5 Hz: each 80 ms of input audio advances one frame, emitting 1 text token + 1 function token; Talker converts these to 31 RVQ codes, and the Codec renders 22.05 kHz audio.
* **Memory & hardware constraints**:
  * **Fits on one card, no headroom**: 66.0 GB after load; single-request peak 69.7–76.4 GB; concurrency 4 peaks at 80.8 GB (full).
  * **No multi-GPU speedup**: all 4 stages are pinned to `gpu=0` and requests are serialized, so extra GPUs don't reduce latency. Concurrency requires independent replicas (1 GPU each).

---

## 2. P0-1: Baseline Benchmarks (Short / Medium / Long Audio & Concurrency)

> **Note**: All input lengths include 3 s of trailing silence.

### 2.1 Single-Stream Baseline: Latency, TTFA, RTF, Streaming Stability

| Input | Total latency p50 (range) | p95 / p50 | TTFA p50 | RTF p50 | Chunk interval p50/p95/p99 | GPU util | Peak mem | ASR WER |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **8.0 s** | 7.36 s (7.28–7.57) | 1.02–1.07 | 1.69 s | 0.920 | 63 / 83 / 92 ms | 47.3% | 69.7 GB | 0.0 |
| **13.0 s** | 11.59 s (11.08–12.18) | — | 1.92 s | 0.891 | — | — | — | — |
| **23.0 s** | 19.11 s (18.61–19.71) | 1.03 | 2.33 s | 0.831 | 63 / 79 / 91 ms | 53.7% | 71.9 GB | 0.0 |
| **33.04 s** | 26.43 s (26.15–26.64) | — | 2.72 s | 0.800 | — | — | — | — |
| **44.08 s** | 35.60 s (34.96–36.80) | 1.01 | 3.19 s | 0.808 | 64 / 82 / 91 ms | 54.9% | 76.4 GB | 0.0 |
| **87.46 s** | 72.79 s (70.66–73.11) | — | 5.36 s | 0.832 | — | — | 76.4 GB | — |

* **Latency & stability**:
  * Max spread across 5 runs per config is under 10% (largest: 13 s group, ~9.5%).
  * TTFA grows roughly linearly with input length (1.69 s → 5.36 s). For 8 s inputs, TTFA dominates, so RTF varies 0.92–1.06 across runs.
* **Streaming cadence**: each chunk is 80 ms; median chunk interval is 63 ms (~1.2× faster than real time). A ~0.25 s playback buffer prevents underruns for nearly all requests. **Caveat**: the pipeline is offline (processing starts after the full recording arrives), not true real-time full duplex.
* **Startup & environment variance**: pipeline takes ~10.5 min to become ready (~7 min with warm cache). Environment changes introduce ~10% systematic variance; only compare within the same config and pod batch.

issues.title: [Tracking][Qwen3-Omni] Serving Reform and Default Configuration Roadmap
issues.body:
## Goal

This issue tracks the Qwen3-Omni serving reform.

The goal is to establish a **validated, explainable, and robust default serving configuration** across different hosts and workloads, while improving performance without regressing correctness, streaming continuity, or serving stability.

Related:

* #1022
* #907
* #1466

## Motivation

Qwen3-Omni currently has three related problems:

1. **Host sensitivity.**
   Performance can change significantly with `OMP_NUM_THREADS`, CPU affinity, NUMA placement, and replica topology. The runtime does not yet have a node-wide CPU resource policy.

2. **Optimization interaction.**
   Individually beneficial optimizations may not compose into the best end-to-end configuration because CPU, CUDA Graphs, KV cache, chunking, batching, and admission control share resources.

3. **Limited observability.**
   When serving regresses, it is difficult to tell whether the bottleneck is queueing, CPU scheduling, batch formation, KV pressure, graph fallback, or downstream stages without running an external profiler.

## Scope

* Qwen3-Omni Thinker / Talker / Code2Wav
* CPU resource allocation and NUMA affinity
* CUDA Graph and cache policies
* KV / admission / batching configuration
* Streaming chunk configuration
* Serving profiles
* Runtime observability

## Roadmap

design doc: https://plarkustnig5c8p6.usttp.larksuite.com/wiki/CBoawro26i14K1k43CLuaPX8t1f

### O-PR0: Add serving observability @AkazaAkane 
* #2378 

Expose enough runtime state to explain performance without requiring a profiler:

* per-stage queue time
* effective batch size
* running / waiting requests
* KV utilization
* CUDA Graph hit / fallback rate
* CPU scheduler busy time
* GPU wait / idle time

This telemetry should later support traffic-aware admission, batching, and resource policies.

### O-PR1: Land and qualify existing optimizations @Ratish1 

Review and independently qualify:
* #2358 
* #2374 
* #2380 
* #2413 
* #2073
* #1320
* #1999
* #1965
* #2395 
* #2545 
* #2546 
* #2547 
* #2548 

### O-PR2: Add generic CPU resource planning
* #2439 
Introduce a node-wide planner that sees the complete local process topology before workers are spawned:

```text
CPU topology
    ↓
stage / replica / GPU placement
    ↓
node-wide CPU budget
    ↓
per-process cpuset + thread budget
```

Initial work:

* CPU topology / cgroup / cpuset discovery
* node-wide process accounting
* static per-process thread budgets
* startup vs runtime thread limits
* GPU-local NUMA affinity

Invariant:

> Auto-managed stages must share one node-wide CPU budget; no stage or replica should independently assume it owns the full host.

### O-PR3: Validate default configurations


Benchmark representative workloads across:

* short / long generation
* ref / no-ref audio
* English / Chinese
* c1 / c8 / c32

Evaluate key interactions such as:

* CPU threads / affinity
* first-audio chunk schedule
* prefill CUDA Graph
* projection cache
* KV budget / admission

Classify optimizations as:

* default
* low-latency profile
* throughput profile
* opt-in

### O-PR4: Add named serving profiles

Build on the existing config system from #1466 rather than introducing another configuration layer.

Example:

```yaml
profile: balanced
```

Initial profiles:

* `balanced`
* `low_latency`
* `throughput`

Profiles should resolve into validated canonical configuration rather than exposing model-specific tuning knobs directly to users.

issues.title: [Tracking] MOSS-TTS Optimizations
issues.body:
## Motivation

MOSS-TTS Delay still has significant room for performance improvement. We have implemented a series of optimizations, and this issue tracks their progress as separate PRs.

## Tracking

All items listed below **have already been implemented**. The checkbox tracks whether the corresponding PR has been merged, not whether implementation is complete.

The optimizations are submitted as separate PRs so that each change, performance gain, and quality impact can be reviewed and validated independently.

The performance numbers below come from different points in the development stack. They are useful directional evidence, but they are not cumulative. Each PR will be rerun against its immediate parent before submission.

### Codec ownership and preprocessing

- [x] **Decouple the MOSS-TTS Delay codec and run reference encoding on GPU** — #1222
  - Load the processor with `audio_tokenizer=None` and give preprocessing and vocoder standalone codec ownership.
  - Preserve checkpoint codec metadata, explicit codec overrides, `PathLike` references, and unified path/URL/data-URI audio loading.
  - Rename `codec.py` to `delay_pattern.py` because it contains Delay-pattern logic rather than neural codec execution.
  - Derive the codec device from stage placement while preserving an explicit CPU fallback.
  - Update MOSS-TTS process resource accounting so opt-in stage isolation does not require a manual preprocessing memory-fraction workaround.
  - Full SeedTTS result: `2.9958 -> 4.4395 QPS` (`+48.19%`).

- [x] **Batch and cache reference encoding** — #1348 
  - Route MOSS-TTS Delay reference encoding through the shared `ReferenceEncodeService`, with waveform-content cache identity, same-key single-flight deduplication, byte-bounded LRU caching, and caller-isolated cached tensors.
  - Batch prepared GPU waveforms across different cold references while keeping audio loading and resampling outside the codec worker; retry failed batches per item and close the worker with the preprocessing lifecycle.
  - Five-run full SeedTTS EN result on a single NVIDIA H200 at concurrency 16 (`1088/1088` samples per run): throughput `6.8686 -> 9.0000 QPS` (`+31.03%`); mean latency `2.3228 -> 1.7698 s` (`-23.81%`); P95 latency `2.9000 -> 2.1930 s` (`-24.38%`); mean RTF `0.54038 -> 0.41056` (`-24.02%`).

- [x] **Run MOSS-TTS Local reference encoding on a dedicated CUDA stream** — #2193
  - Give the existing reference encoder worker a persistent CUDA stream, reducing interference with AR generation on reference-cache misses.
  - Establish a one-time dependency on the model-loading stream and complete the CPU-code conversion before resolving each request's future.
  - Five-round full Seed-TTS-Eval EN A/B on one NVIDIA H200 at concurrency 16, with CPU quota limited to 1/8 of the host, 1,088 requests per round, and a fresh server each round. Results use arithmetic means:
    - Local streaming: throughput `12.8234 -> 13.1002 QPS` (`+2.16%`); mean TTFA `326.54 -> 265.84 ms` (`-18.59%`); P95 TTFA `501.44 -> 390.08 ms` (`-22.21%`).
    - Local non-streaming: throughput `15.1102 -> 15.7866 QPS` (`+4.48%`); mean latency `1.0524 -> 1.0076 s` (`-4.26%`).
  - Streaming mean per-request maximum playback underrun decreases from `0.700 -> 0.080 ms`; requests with underrun above 50 ms decrease from `31/5,440 -> 4/5,440`.

### AR sampling

- [x] **Restrict audio-state text sampling to the two valid control tokens** — #1158
  - Preserve global token IDs, seeded sampling behavior

issues.title: [Bug] /v1/realtime history transcription inherits the reply's token limit
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

For every committed turn, the realtime conversation session sends a second request that transcribes the user's audio for the conversation history (`run_turn` calls `run_transcription`). `build_transcription_request` uses `self.sampling()`, which is the sampling of the reply, so the transcript inherits `max_response_output_tokens`. That causes two problems.

First, a client that sets `max_response_output_tokens` to keep replies short also gets a cut-off history transcript. With a limit of 8 tokens, the sentence "My name is Alice, and my favourite drink is green tea. Please remember that." was stored in my run as "My name is Alice and my favourite drink", so later turns lose what the user said.

Second, with the default `"inf"` the session sets no limit, so the request falls back to the model's default, 2048 new tokens for MiniCPM-o. Turns run one at a time from `response_queue`, so the next turn waits until this request finishes. If the model answers the audio instead of transcribing it, the session stalls. I hit this with MiniCPM-o-4.5 and a spoken request for a long story. In five runs (three with the script below, two in a longer test that also asks a follow-up question) the "transcript" came back as 1180 to 1536 words of story and finished 29 to 39 s after the reply. In those two longer runs, a short question asked right after the reply waited 31 and 34 s for its answer. The whole story is then kept in the history as the user's message.

Code at 9d3bf44:
- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/9d3bf443/sglang_omni/serve/realtime/session.py#L1126-L1132
- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/9d3bf443/sglang_omni/serve/realtime/session.py#L1165-L1177

The model-side reason MiniCPM-o answers instead of transcribing is a separate issue (#2462). Either way, the reply's limit is the wrong limit for this request. This is also separate from #2208, which proposes bounding how many turns stay in history.

```bash
sgl-omni serve --model-path openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5 --port 8000 --enable-realtime
```

issues.title: [Tracking] Qwen3-TTS Optimization Follow-Up Roadmap
issues.body:
## Goal

Improve Qwen3-TTS streaming first audio, continuity, throughput and high-concurrency serving without regressing output quality, deterministic inference, request lifecycle correctness or streaming behavior. Related: #1418.

**Bar for performance work:** a change is worth making when one tracked metric (first playable or audible first audio, underrun, throughput, RTF) improves by at least 5% end to end at an operating point we serve, and no other tracked metric, quality included, gets worse. Measure with paired runs on the harness below. Changes under the bar, or that only trade one metric for another, are not pursued. Everything tried and dropped, and everything under the bar, is in [one comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/1754#issuecomment-5824501257).

## Scope

Qwen3-TTS Base and CustomVoice: Talker and Code Predictor, reference encoding, streaming vocoder, CUDA graph coverage, scheduling and batching, serving profiles and admission.

## Where it stands

**Streaming first audio.** One H100 80GB, CustomVoice 1.7B, seed-tts-eval EN, open-loop Poisson arrivals, 30 s warmup, 60 s measurement, three client seeds, all three stages in one process. Main with #2216 and #2217, 2026-09-19:

| | 1 rps | 20 rps |
|---|---|---|
| first playable p50 | 28.4-28.7 ms | 36.9-37.2 ms |
| audible first audio p50 | | 38.1-38.7 ms |
| underrun | 0-0.2% | 0-0.2% |

A stronger reference implementation on the same host and harness reaches about 26 ms audible first audio at 20 rps with about 0.5% underrun. With #1998 landed, 1 rps reaches the reference's first-audio level; the gap left is under load, about 12 ms audible at 20 rps.

**Throughput.** The TTS CI stages carry it. Base at concurrency 16 on the CI runners, worst of five runs on 2026-08-30: 21.1 req/s non-streaming (RTF 0.186) and 19.5 req/s streaming (RTF 0.199). The code has moved since, so these are floors rather than today's medians.

Two things these numbers do not show:

- Running the vocoder in its own process, as the CI presets and the cookbook benchmark table do, costs 14 ms first playable and 26 ms audible first audio at 20 rps (2.4 ms at 1 rps). MPS wins back about half.
- Base voice cloning with a reference transcript (ICL) reaches first audio much later than CustomVoice: 57-60 ms at 1 rps and 104-122 ms at 20 rps on the CI runners, against 20-22 and 33-35 ms for CustomVoice there. Profiled on one H200, vocoder in its own process, cached references, 1 rps, admission to first PCM: ICL 46 ms, x-vector cloning 21 ms, CustomVoice 20 ms. Prefill is about 6 ms for all three; the ICL excess is the vocoder's first chunk (30 against 9 ms), which decodes every reference frame with the first generated frame. With the vocoder in the engine process the same ICL path is 38 ms at 1 rps and 63 ms at 20 rps, and that first decode is still 18 of it. An uncached reference adds 4 to 6 ms of encoding.

**Where one decode iteration goes, 20 rps:** talker and code predictor CUDA graphs 6.69 ms (2.30 + 4.09 ms of GPU), `get_next_batch_to_run` 1.02 ms (upstream SGLang), `process_batch_result` 0.62 ms, stream emission 0.56 ms, inbox and admission 0.14 ms; 9.09 ms in all. The GPU is neither saturated nor issuing well, but each kernel item left in the predictor and vocoder is under the bar for first audio. Profile: `docs/benchmarks/qwen3_tts_profiler_headroom_20260914.md` on branch `qwen3-tts-align-followup-windows`.

issues.title: [Roadmap] Coding Style
issues.body:
## Goal

Gradually bring the main code and tests into alignment with the [code style guide](https://github.com/zhaochenyang20/sglang-diffusion-routing/issues/32), with automated checks for requirements that tooling can express directly.

Start with basic lint checks, introduce type checking to support annotation changes, then expand coverage to tests once the rollout for the main code is established.

## Roadmap

### Phase 1: Coding style guidance and basic Ruff checks

- [x] Establish the initial Ruff configuration, fix existing non-annotation findings outside `tests/`, and enable the checks in pre-commit and CI. #2184
- [x] Add coding style guidance for coding agents and contributors. #2181

### Phase 2: Type checker selection and integration

Ruff can flag missing annotations and some uses of `Any`, but validating annotations against implementations and callers requires a type checker.

- [ ] Evaluate type checkers on representative repository code, considering dependency typing support, diagnostic quality, and incremental adoption.
- [ ] Select a checker and define the initial coverage and strictness, including how untyped dependencies and implicit `Any` are handled.
- [ ] Establish a checked scope in the main code and integrate the check into local development and CI.

### Phase 3: Annotation cleanup in main code

Use the configured type checker to validate annotation changes, migrating module by module.

- [x] Replace `Any` annotations with types that match the code's actual inputs, outputs, and usage. #2213
- [ ] Add missing parameter and return annotations, and type arguments for bare containers.
- [ ] Resolve type inconsistencies exposed by the checker and review annotation changes against callers.
- [ ] Enable individual Ruff `ANN` rules supported by the guide, including `ANN401`, as the corresponding findings are resolved.

### Phase 4: Extend coverage to tests

Once the checks for the main code are established, apply the same process to `tests/`.

issues.title: [Roadmap] LLaDA-Uni Model Support, Inference Optimization and Serving
issues.body:
## Goal

Complete LLaDA2.0-Uni's core generation capabilities in SGLang-Omni before expanding inference and scheduling optimizations. Shared runtime components should be reusable where their contracts apply, while prompts, CFG semantics, numerical behavior, and model adapters remain explicitly model-specific.

This roadmap continues the work tracked in #445. LLaDA2.0-Uni is the current implementation target; future members of the LLaDA-Uni family require their own model integration.

## Phase 1: Core generation capabilities

- [ ] **A — Thinker CFG and numerical correctness:** #2257. Multi-way CFG, padding-aware attention, shared dLLM admission/cleanup, MoE numerics, and understanding preprocessing.
- [ ] **B — Native image generation and editing:** #1499. Non-thinking T2I and raw-image editing, native image endpoints, chat image output, and Diffusers/default or optional SGLang decoder backends.
- [ ] **C — Thinking-mode image generation:** #1500. Two-pass T2I with a 2048-token thinking budget, an image-generation transition, and two-pass token accounting.
- [ ] **E — Interleaved generation:** #1502. Ordered multi-frame text/image output, generated frame dimensions, and the shared self-route/multi-inflight relay needed by the pipeline.

The image contracts are intentionally distinct: native image endpoints return `data[]`; single-image chat generation returns `message.image`; interleaved chat generation returns ordered `message.segments` with inline PNG media and a concatenated plain-text `message.content`. Normal and `decoder-turbo` decoding are supported by the image stack.

## Phase 2: Inference optimization

- [ ] **F — Thinker TP and opt-in CFG CUDA graphs:** #1486. TP execution, FP32 expert combine/reduce, SGLang routing reuse, and eligible graph replay. Eager execution remains the default. Optional H20 TP2 settings configure existing MoE kernels and are hardware/version-specific.
- [ ] **H — Image-decoder SP and generic stage-SP runtime:** #1501. SGLang-backed Ulysses/Ring decoder integration, global token ordering, and leader/follower lifecycle.
- [ ] **Planned:** thinker and image-decoder quantization.

These optimizations are not prerequisites for merging basic T2I/edit support.

## Phase 3: Scheduling and serving optimization

The following are planned work, not capabilities established by the interleaved relay:

- [ ] Diffusion continuous batching.
- [ ] Dynamic batching in the LLaDA-Uni thinker.
- [ ] Cross-node and cross-stage scheduling.

## Dependencies and PR ownership

The implementation stack is:

```text
main
└── A #2257 — thinker correctness
    └── B #1499 — native T2I/edit
        └── C #1500 — thinking T2I
            └── E #1502 — interleaved generation + shared relay
                ├── F #1486 — thinker TP + opt-in CUDA graphs
                └── H #1501 — decoder SP + generic stage SP
```

These arrows describe the code stack, not a claim that every optimization conceptually requires every earlier feature. Review incremental changes against the immediate prerequisite and rebase the remaining stack as prerequisites merge. F and H are siblings; neither depends on the other.

The older shared-relay proposal #1487 is superseded by E/#1502. The older generic stage-SP proposal #1490 is superseded by H/#1501. They are no longer active work items or separate prerequisites, and their code should not be applied a second time.

issues.title: [Feature] Qwen3-TTS: support configurable output sample rate in the Speech API
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. If the issue you raised is not a feature but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 2. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Motivation

### Motivation

Every TTS pipeline served by SGLang-Omni returns audio at its own native sample rate, and the Speech API provides no way to ask for a different one. `POST /v1/audio/speech`, `POST /v1/audio/speech/batch` and `WS /v1/audio/speech/stream` all return whatever the model produced, and the Python client (`Client.speech`) has no knob either. The native rate differs per model — Qwen3-TTS, Higgs TTS, CosyVoice3 and MOSS-TTS generate at 24 kHz, ZONOS2 and Ming-Omni-TTS at 44.1 kHz, MiniMax-Music3 at 32 kHz — so any caller that needs 8 kHz (telephony/IVR, SIP or G.711 trunks, 8 kHz voice agents) has to resample the payload itself.

Client-side resampling is a poor fit for the streaming API:

1. **Streaming filter state.** A correct anti-aliasing filter must keep state across chunk boundaries. Resampling each chunk independently clicks at the boundaries and folds high-frequency content back into the band; most clients do not implement this at all.
2. **Metadata drift.** Once a client rewrites the PCM, the WAV header and the streaming sample-rate metadata still advertise the native rate, so playback runs at the wrong speed. This failure mode is not hypothetical in this repo: it was reported for the completion audio path in #556 and fixed in #728.
3. **Bandwidth.** Uncompressed 24 kHz PCM is 3x the egress of 8 kHz, which matters most for exactly the telephony deployments that need it.
4. **Abstraction leakage.** Callers must know the native rate of every checkpoint they route to, which breaks the "one OpenAI-compatible speech API for all models" story.

Requested feature: an optional `sample_rate` on the speech APIs, resampled on the server with a stateful, alias-suppressing filter and reflected consistently in headers and metadata.

issues.body:
## Objective

Bring Qwen3-ASR inference to Ascend in small, independently reviewable
increments. Community support is claimed only for merged code and exact-head
hardware evidence.

## Current baseline

| Item | Current state |
|---|---|
| SGLang dependency | `sglang==0.5.19` |
| SGLang candidate | Pure `v0.5.19` commit `0bcd822377da7b5718e674eaf9c870d349424dd1`; no fused-op or Qwen3 model patch |
| SGLang-Omni baseline | [#2084](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/2084) is merged; [#2160](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/2160) is open at `8fe0e163` and awaits current-head qualification |
| Runtime mode | Encoder, breakable prefill and full decode graphs are enabled in the candidate; Torch Compile is outside the qualified NPU scope |
| NPU Host queues | #2160 defaults `PER_STREAM_QUEUE=1` before NPU worker startup while preserving explicit environment overrides |
| Realtime implementation | Existing `/v1/realtime?intent=transcription` and `Qwen3ASRStreamingStrategy`; no NPU-specific realtime production fork |

The SGLang fused-op patch is not required for the functional path. Torch
Compile and compile-plus-graph are deferred.

## Feature status

### Serving and runtime

- [x] [Ascend installation manifest and helper](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/1577)
- [x] Offline transcription on the NPU graph path
- [x] [Encoder private device stream](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/2084)

- [x] Cold concurrency-8 liveness and 140-request functional correctness on
  predecessor candidates
- [ ] NPU encoder graph delivery through [#2160](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/2160)
- [x] Bounded realtime ASR qualification with server VAD and manual commit
- [ ] Realtime cancel/clear hardware qualification
- [ ] Forced alignment and timestamp output

### #2160 implementation update

The current #2160 implementation:

- captures one encoder graph per token bucket;
- updates every captured FIA task with the current request's cumulative window
  boundaries;
- gives each encoder graph runner its own update stream;
- submits FIA updates on a short-lived Host thread concurrently with replay;
- defaults `PER_STREAM_QUEUE=1` before NPU worker startup;
- retains the existing caller-thread cache-hit attach and completed-Future path;
- leaves a bucket on the eager path when its graph capture fails.

The PR does not add a cached-transfer worker path, a terminal graph-failure
state, multiple encoder workers, or an SGLang patch. Earlier all-graph and
per-stream-queue experiments are predecessor evidence, not qualification for
the current `8fe0e163` head.
