## Goal

Profile `fishaudio/s2-pro` on one exact H100 using the repository's layered runtime-profiling methodology and the additional safeguards from [#1798 comment 5517542877](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/1798#issuecomment-5517542877).

The #1798 discussion already covers recent saturation work for MOSS-TTS delay and MOSS-TTS-Local. To avoid duplicating that work, this investigation selected Fish Speech S2-Pro.

> **Status: open.** Layers 1 and 2, the Layer 3 single-process contention diagnosis, Layer 4 Candidate A, and the DAC/reference-preprocessing Layer 4 follow-up are complete. The full Layer 3 concurrency sweep has not run. A standalone Layer 5 regression remains conditional on a selected production implementation/default change.

## Reproducibility fingerprint

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Repository | `sgl-project/sglang-omni` |
| Commit | `50db4a550374239400139841451cc7b48a3e85c2` |
| Image | `hongccc/sglang-omni@sha256:02a85f00438c901c72a2eb2ef738974a807f63af3d13084445604f3344067b19` |
| Model | `fishaudio/s2-pro` |
| Model revision | `1de9996b6be38b745688de084d87a5633f714e4e` |
| Dataset revision | `27f4c1adee83b5b29b7c4b375f6b976324bda308` |
| Config | `examples/configs/s2pro_tts.yaml` |
| Benchmark | `benchmarks/eval/benchmark_tts_seedtts.py` |
| Provider | Modal classic Sandbox |
| Hardware | Exactly one H100 80 GB, 16 physical CPU cores, 65,536 MiB RAM |
| GPU/driver/CUDA | H100 80 GB / 580.95.05 / 13.0.3 |
| Key packages | torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1, sglang 0.5.18, flashinfer 0.6.17, py-spy 0.4.2 |
| Cost constraint | Credits only, confirmed before allocation |
| Local raw evidence | `.profiling-runs/fishaudio_s2_pro/` (gitignored) |

Preflight started at 0% GPU utilization, 4 MiB memory, and zero compute rows. Repository/network/Volume access, launch-mode py-spy, server readiness, and a real one-sample voice-cloning request all succeeded. Direct post-hoc py-spy attach is forbidden by Modal isolation, so profiling servers were launched underneath py-spy.

The benchmark regime was warmed, disjoint-shard traffic with natural duplicate-reference reuse. Each mode received an uncounted 32-request load with 16 script warmups before discovery measurements.

## Layer 1 — GPU busy ratio

Headline load: 128 requests at concurrency 16 per mode, tightly bracketed by 0.2-second `nvidia-smi` sampling. A separate torch trace measured the union of kernel/memcpy/memset intervals.

| Metric | Non-streaming | Streaming |
|---|---:|---:|
| Completed / failed | 128 / 0 | 128 / 0 |
| Mean latency | 7.187 s | 7.212 s |
| p95 / p99 / max latency | 10.142 / 10.984 / 11.850 s | 10.341 / 10.989 / 11.611 s |
| Throughput | 2.107 req/s | 2.130 req/s |
| Mean / max RTF | 2.183 / 6.4338 | 1.861 / 4.2993 |
| Mean / p95 / max audio TTFP | n/a | 6.3627 / 9.3884 / 10.0953 s |
| `nvidia-smi` samples | 257 | 247 |
| Mean / median / max GPU utilization | 51.92% / 73% / 95% | 54.02% / 77% / 90% |
| GPU activity interval union | 48.55% | 48.89% |
| Max GPU memory | 80,149 MiB | 77,773 MiB |

**Finding:** both measurement methods agree that the H100 is materially unsaturated at concurrency 16. This does not support GPU-kernel-first optimization. Evidence strength: **medium**, because each method has one clean directional run.

The latency distributions contain no runaway single request: maximum latency stays close to p99 in both modes. Streaming had zero maximum underrun among 127 continuity-eligible requests.

## Motivation Cosmos 3 needs a shared serving architecture for multimodal understanding, generation, and requests that alternate between the two. That architecture must extend across Nano, Edge, Super, and specialized checkpoints while keeping qualification specific to each model, modality, and deployment topology. This RFC proposes native SGLang execution behind reusable SGLang-Omni adapters. Native runtimes own model loading, preprocessing, scheduling, parallelism, and caches. Omni owns serving integration and interleaved request orchestration. #1864 tracks the rollout. The submitted Nano path combines visual generation and Reasoner foundations with shared interleaved orchestration in #2204 and Nano integration in #2205. Edge support in #2107 and Super support in draft #2201 extend the same foundation. Full Omni modalities, performance, and scale remain part of the design and rollout, with checkpoint-specific qualification. ## Proposed design ### Architecture A deployment selects standalone generation, standalone understanding, or interleaved execution. Each path uses the same native execution components. ```mermaid flowchart TB Client["SDK / HTTP clients"] subgraph Omni["SGLang-Omni"] API["Serving entrypoints"] UMM["Interleaved controller
history, turns, segments
[#2204]"] R["Reasoner adapter
[#2049]"] G["Generation integration

Media app composition [#2048]"] API --> UMM API --> R API --> G UMM --> R UMM --> G end subgraph Native["Native SGLang"] SRT["SRT Engine
OpenAIServingChat"] GEN["multimodal_gen

Native image, video, and action routes retain their request validation, job lifecycle, and content-delivery behavior. Route availability and supported operations follow checkpoint capabilities. The Nano integration in #2205 connects the shared controller to native generation and Reasoner stages through the Cosmos adapter. The initial interleaved deployment uses a CPU controller, a generation GPU, and a separate Reasoner GPU. issues.title: [ASR Streaming] Realtime Input Streaming Roadmap and PR Tracker
issues.body:
This is the tracker for **input streaming (live audio in) for ASR models**. New PRs should use the title prefix `[ASR Streaming]` and link this issue in the PR body.

Related trackers: #1267 (ASR refactor, shared mechanics this work builds on), #1754 (TTS roadmap, same tracking format; TTS input streaming is explicitly out of scope there and here).

## Goal

Let clients push audio incrementally over a WebSocket session and receive transcript events while the audio is still arriving, for every ASR model we serve, through **one fixed protocol**. Today `/v1/audio/transcriptions` only accepts a complete file (optionally with SSE output streaming); live captioning, voice agents and telephony need to send audio as it is captured.

## Design principles

1. **Protocol first.** Models adapt to the protocol, not the other way around. A model that can't do something natively declares it; we never bend the wire contract for one model's limitation.
2. **Target OpenAI Realtime GA (transcription intent).** Beta was retired in May 2026 and no current SDK speaks it. The existing `/v1/realtime` conversation session (#385) migrates to GA in the same change.
3. **OpenAI is the baseline, not the whole spec.** Anything it doesn't cover goes in explicit, documented extension fields.
4. **Shared code owns session/transport/events/capabilities; model dirs own encoder feeding and partial/final production.** No model-name branching in shared code (same rule as #1267).

## Requirements gathered from early users

These came from discussions with teams already building streaming STT servers on top of inference backends. They are recorded here in generalized form as design input.

**Transport and audio**
- One WebSocket per stream; PCM16 mono 16 kHz as the default input.
- Audio format is a negotiated session parameter, not a hard constant. Sample rate (8/16/24/48 kHz) and encoding (pcm16, µ-law, A-law) should be declarable; **8 kHz µ-law is a real need for telephony**, not a nice-to-have.
- Deployment topologies to support: co-located (server + model on one GPU box) and split (session/transport layer on CPU, model backend on separate GPUs). The protocol layer must not assume it lives in the same process as the model.

**Capability negotiation**
- On connect / `session.update`, the server declares what the loaded model can actually do, e.g. `partial_style`, `max_decode_window_s`, supported `input_format`s, `languages`, `segmentation_modes`, `concurrency`.
- `session.updated` reports **what was granted**, not an echo of the request. Clients cannot guess per-model behavior from outside, so this is the mechanism that makes "protocol first" work across a heterogeneous model set.

**Partial transcript semantics**
- `partial_style` must be declared explicitly (e.g. `append_only` vs `revising`). Several models (Whisper-style and Qwen3-ASR among them) revise earlier words as more context arrives; treating their output as append-only deltas is silently lossy. Clients need to know whether a delta may replace previously emitted text.

**Long input / buffer limits**
- Buffer overflow must not close the connection (no WS 1009 as the overflow response). A long turn should be split into multiple finals correlated by a turn id, so a session stays alive across arbitrary utterance lengths.

**Division of labour**
- VAD, turn policy, diarization and session admission are per-customer policy and typically live above us; we should make them optional / pluggable, not mandatory.
- What can

issues.title: [Bug] MOSS-TD: batch-order nondeterminism splits one speaker on AISHELL4 long audio (delta_cer 0.23% to 1.15% in ~1 run in 5)
issues.body:
## Summary

On AISHELL4 long audio, MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize produces two stable outputs for the same input. In about one run in five it inserts an extra segment boundary and opens a new speaker id partway through a segment, which splits one reference speaker across two hypothesis speakers. The transcript text is unaffected, but cpCER for that sample goes from 4.9% to 25.1%, and the 20 sample stage aggregate `delta_cer` goes from about 0.23% to about 1.15%.

Decoding is greedy (temperature 0, set by #969). #959 measured 792/800 identical outputs across identical runs after that change, so roughly 1% residual nondeterminism was already known. This is that residual, landing on a sample where the diarization metric amplifies it.

## Evidence

One H100 pair, single MOSS-TD server per round, AISHELL4 long (20 samples), client concurrency 32, model revision unchanged across rounds. 15 consecutive rounds:

| rounds | AISHELL4 `delta_cer` | cpCER | DER |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 rounds | 0.175% to 0.236% | 14.06% to 14.08% | 9.59% to 9.84% |
| runs 5, 7, 14 | 1.138% to 1.149% | 14.98% to 15.00% | 10.17% to 10.38% |

A further 4 rounds on a later build produced no flip, so the observed rate is 3/19.

## What changes

Every flip is the same sample (`sample-000004`, a 38 minute meeting recording) at the same position, t = 34s. The text is nearly identical, `cer_no_spk` 4.87% against 4.85%; only the segmentation differs.

```
normal: ...明显的客流量也呃客流量也多了，呃咱这个销售这个呃营业额儿也上去了。[39.58][40.44][S01]
flip:   ...明显的客流量也[34.21][34.14][S06]呃客流量也多了，呃咱这个销售这个呃营业额儿也上去了。[39.54]
```

Because generation is autoregressive, every later segment that belonged to `S01` is then emitted as `S06`, and `S04` likewise becomes `S07`. Speaker count goes from 5 to 7. cpCER maps each reference speaker to exactly one hypothesis speaker, so the whole tail of that speaker scores as wrong.

## Root cause

Greedy decoding is deterministic given identical logits, but batch composition differs between rounds, so kernel shapes and reduction order differ and the logits carry small floating point differences. At t = 34s the two candidates, continue the current segment or emit a boundary plus a new speaker, are close enough that this is sufficient to flip the argmax. Timestamp values differ in their last digits throughout the output, from the same source.

## Why this matters

The ASR CI stage gates `AISHELL4_LONG_DELTA_CER_PERCENT_REF`. Any reference calibrated on non flipped rounds, including the current 0.318 on main, fails on a flipped round: the derived gate is 0.382 against an observed 1.15. Calibration cannot make this gate both meaningful and stable while the flip exists, which currently blocks the threshold work in #1896.

## Options

1. Set the reference high enough to cover the flip, about 1.15. The gate stays green but loses most of its power to detect a real diarization regression.
2. Replace `sample-000004` in the AISHELL4 CI subset. Cheapest path to a tight gate, but it hides a real behavior and another sample may do the same.
3. Make the segmentation decision robust, for example by not letting a near tie between a text token and a boundary token depend on batch shape. This is the real fix and the largest.

Reproduction: run the ASR CI stage 1 AISHELL4 long dataset repeatedly on one host and compare `per_sample` entries for `sample-000004` across rounds.

issues.title: [Runtime Profiling] MiniCPMo-4.5
issues.body:
## Goal

This issue records **profiling discovery results and follow-up investigations**. 

## Related work

Related context: [MiniCPM benchmark work #2252](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/2252).

## Scope and measurement setup

- **Measured workload:** original `zhaochenyang20/seed-tts-eval`, all 1,088 English rows, concurrency `1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32`, **one measured run per point**. Additional repetitions and the full Chinese sweep were explicitly removed from the requested scope.
- **API:** non-streaming `/v1/chat/completions`, MiniCPM-o voice cloning, each sample's own reference in `audio.ref_audio`. `max_new_tokens=256`, `temperature=0.7`; per-request generation RNG seeds were not fixed.
- **Client timing:** retain dataset sample ID and a unique server request ID; record send start, complete HTTP body, and decoded WAV readiness. Preload reference data before measurement. Keep full target text in the raw records.
- **Server events:** ASGI ingress/body/send boundaries, conversion, pipeline result, audio encoding and JSON serialization. Event collection requires an active recorder. Module ranges require `SGLANG_OMNI_MINICPM_PROFILE=1`; no new device synchronization is added by those ranges.
- **Detailed captures:** concurrency 1 and 16, 32 English requests each, Nsight CUDA/NVTX with graph-node tracing and request events. No Torch-profiler capture or py-spy CPU sample is claimed.

### Baseline fingerprint

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| SGLang-Omni source | `2d0b48ff4f00b3673c5ba94505ac2564bcc887c7` + saved profiling patch/new files; not a clean-main run |
| Tracked patch SHA-256 | `0413ff7a7210021c33925b9820fac6b42cdb73bab870fdf08b94c22278ee6fc3` |
| Runtime | Python 3.12; SGLang 0.5.19; Torch 2.13.0 with CUDA 13.0 build; Transformers 5.12.1; ONNX 1.23.0 |
| Hardware | 1× H100 SXM 80 GB; driver 580.159.04; 26 allocated vCPUs; DP1, all stages on GPU 0 |
| Model | `openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5`, revision `503e754207c94da6bb26850b4469f367c9ea3582` |
| Dataset | Original `zhaochenyang20/seed-tts-eval`, revision `8f5e1aa2a35d42f42e940074c1983358b9491f89`; not the arrow variant used by ARK-ASR |
| Runtime configuration | Thinker max sequence length 8,192; Thinker `mem_fraction_static=0.55`; Talker `mem_fraction_static=0.15`; `OMP_NUM_THREADS=4` |

The saved tracked diff and both added source files were compared against the current working tree during this review and match. Full dependency pins and exact commands are retained in the evidence bundle.

## Benchmark & Profiling

### Method and timing definitions

The closed-loop client holds the requested concurrency and sends the next request when one completes. All six full-data points use the same sample IDs, text and deterministic input order. Sixteen independent ZH hardcase requests are used **only as warmup**, never in the English statistics; this warmup set was retained when the measured scope was reduced to English. Warmup finishes and its writer drains before measurement.

- **HTTP E2E:** immediately before the client POST through receipt of the complete response body, before JSON/base64/WAV decoding. This is a colocated client over loopback, not an internet RTT benchmark.
- **Audio-ready TTFA:** the same start through decoding the returned WAV. Since this endpoint is non-streaming, this is full-response audio readiness, **not streaming first-chunk latency**.
- **Request throughput:** successful measured requests / measured runner wall time, including fill/drain of the request coh

issues.title: [Feature] Qwen3-TTS: accept a precomputed speaker embedding instead of ref_audio for Base cloning
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. If the issue you raised is not a feature but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 2. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Motivation

In our deployment the speaker embedding for each voice is computed once, offline, and stored in our own voice registry. At synthesis time we already have the exact vector the talker needs. Today, to use SGLang-Omni we have to go the other way round and hand the server a reference audio again, which means on every request:

the reference audio has to be transferred to the server (or be reachable by it), and
the server has to re-derive the speaker representation from that audio before synthesis can start.

That's measurable work on the critical path of a latency-sensitive streaming TTS call, and it's work whose result we already have. It also forces us to keep reference audio available to the serving tier purely as an input format, when the embedding is the thing that actually matters.

Qwen3-TTS itself supports using the speaker embedding alone (x-vector only, skipping the in-context transcript path), so the capability exists in the model — only the serving API has no way to express it.

Proposed API
```
POST /v1/audio/speech
{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base",
  "input": "SGLang-Omni is a great project!",
  "voice": "default",
  "speaker_embedding": [0.0123, -0.0456, ...]   // float list, model's x-vector dim
}
```
**Suggested semantics:**

Type: non-empty list of floats, validated against the model's expected embedding dimension, 400 on mismatch.
Mutually exclusive with references / ref_audio — supplying both is a 400.
Implies x-vector-only mode (no ICL), so ref_text is neither required nor used.
Scoped to the Base/cloning task; 400 for models or task types that can't use it.

If it fits the existing schema better, an equivalent shape would be an embedding key inside the references array, as a third alternative next to audio_path and text. We have no strong preference on the spelling — speaker_embedding is suggested only because it matches the field name already used elsewhere in the ecosystem.



### Related resources

vllm-project/vllm-omni already implements exactly this for Qwen3-TTS. Its adapter (vllm_omni/entrypoints/openai/tts_adapters/qwen3_tts.py) accepts a speaker_embedding request field, restricts it to the Base task, validates it's a non-empty float list of the right dimension, and has it imply x-vector-only mode so ref_text is unnecessary. Why the existing caching paths don't cover this

We're aware of the uploaded-voice / speaker-artifact caching work (create_voice_clone_prompt + SpeakerArtifactCache, and the dedup/single-flight efforts in [sgl-project/sglang-omni#1625](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/1625) and [sgl-project/sglang-omni#925](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/925)). Those are valuable, but they solve an adjacent problem:

They still require the reference audio to reach the server at least once, and require the voice to be registered server-side ahead of use.
The resulting artifact is per-replica state on local disk. Our serving tier is stateless and autoscaled with no shared volume, so a cached voice

### Checklist

- [x] This is a documentation tooling bug, not a question.
- [x] This issue is written in English.

### Problem

The local documentation instructions and preview script depend on the caller already being inside `docs/`, but the documentation does not state that requirement.

From the repository root, the documented commands fail:

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
bash serve.sh
```

The repository root has neither `requirements.txt` nor `serve.sh`; both files live under `docs/`. Calling the script explicitly from the root also fails because it runs `make` in the caller's working directory:

```bash
bash docs/serve.sh
# make: *** No rule to make target 'clean'. Stop.
```

### Expected behavior

The README commands should work from the repository root, and `docs/serve.sh` should run its Make targets from the `docs/` directory regardless of the caller's current working directory.

### Proposed fix

- Document the repository root as the working directory and use `docs/requirements.txt` and `docs/serve.sh` in the examples.
- Make `docs/serve.sh` change to its own directory before invoking `make`.
- Stop immediately if the clean step fails.

I would like to implement this small fix.

issues.title: [RFC] Rust Router for SGLang-Omni — Phased Roadmap
issues.body:
## Goals & context

**Parent roadmap:** [#921](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/921) (Router & Same-GPU DP) — Router Phase 2

**This RFC proposes replacing the data plane with Rust first, and treating the control plane as a separate, later, and independently-justified decision.**

# Why a Rust router

**Because the router's cost is per-request, and we have only been dividing it.**

Phase 0 removed response buffering. Phase 1 split one router process into a control plane plus N stateless relay workers. Both helped, and neither touched the thing that actually sets the ceiling: **what a single request costs to relay.** Roughly three quarters of that cost is fixed — asyncio, httpx, and FastAPI overhead that a request pays whether it carries 4 KB or 4 MB. Sharding it across N processes buys N times the same expensive unit. That is a workaround with a price tag, not a fix.


---

## Open questions

1. **One multi-threaded Rust DP, or N SO_REUSEPORT Rust DPs?** One process deletes the shared-memory seqlock and its x86-64-only restriction, and makes session-count-aware steering (2a) trivial. N preserves Phase 1's blast-radius isolation and slot-reclaim model. Recommendation: start with one, keep the SHM layout documented as a fallback.

2. **Packaging.** PyO3/maturin wheel so `pip install` just works, or a separate binary the supervisor spawns? The wheel is friendlier and adds a Rust toolchain to the release pipeline.

3. **Config parity.** Does the Rust DP re-parse the router YAML/CLI, or does the CP hand it a resolved config? Resolved config means less drift.

4. **Verify upstream internals before fixing the port strategy.** The gateway's HTTP framework and streaming-body implementation are *inferred* from its published interface — the old source paths 404'd during research. Confirm first.

5. **Do we accept x86-64-only for the DP?** A single-process Rust DP would remove today's restriction — worth stating as a deliberate improvement.

---

## Phase 1: Python data plane → Rust (parity)

**Goal: byte-for-byte behavioural parity with the Python DP, at a fraction of the per-request cost.** Reuse SGLang model gateway modules wherever they port cleanly; write the omni-specific parts ourselves, because they exist nowhere upstream.

Scope boundary to avoid ambiguity: **anything the Python DP does today is Phase 1, including the omni-specific parts.** Voice-owner pinning, WebSocket TTS relay, and capability routing are *parity requirements*, not enhancements — a Rust DP without them cannot serve production traffic. Phase 2 is strictly *new* capability.

### 1a. Relay core

- [x] Rust binary on tokio; HTTP relay with SSE and chunked-binary streaming
- [ ] Snapshot reader for the v1 JSON contract (`seq` monotonicity, last-good on torn read, stale-timeout shed + `/ready` flip)
- [x] Capability-filtered selector — port `selector.py` + `route_metadata.py` semantics (7 capabilities; inference from path, body fields, and `X-SGLang-Omni-Route-*` hint headers)
- [x] Policies: `random`, `round_robin`, `power_of_two`
- [x] Admission control (in-process atomic if single multi-threaded process; see open question 1)
- [ ] Diagnostic response headers preserved: `X-SGLang-Omni-Worker`, request ID, route attempt
- [ ] DP→CP internal channel: registration, heartbeat with `last_applied_seq`, hot-path worker-failure reports, `409` fencing on stale generation

### 1b. Full route surface (omni parity)

- [x] Voice-owner pinning — port `voice_routing.py`:

issues.title: [RFC] Full-Duplex Session Infrastructure
issues.body:
## Motivation

Full-duplex interaction can be modeled as a sequence of incremental short requests(Unit). Each unit goes through multiple stages, possibly on different workers. must retain state across units: KV cache, token history, and encoder/codec state. Currently, every request releases its state when it finishes.

This RFC introduce `session`, a long-lived context that holds stage state across units. It is implemented by the realtime layer and the Coordinator on top of the existing pipeline. A session is used to:
- Retain and reuse perception, AR, and codec state across units;
- Release resources on close.

## Proposed design

### 1. How state is retained

A session ID will be used to identify long-lived state and each unit is a short request issued under that ID. The Coordinator assigns each stage of a session to a fixed worker, keyed by the session ID, and every unit of that session runs its stages only on those workers. 

When a unit finishes, each stage releases that request's own resources without releasing the session state:
- AR stages reuse SGLang streaming sessions for KV and token history;
- encoder and codec stages keep their own state across units.

### 2. How state is reused

The Coordinator routes each unit by its session ID to the same workers. Units are dispatched one at a time in sequence order. Each unit does incremental computation on the retained state from the previous unit. Overlapping between units is followup optimization.

### 3. How interruptions are handled

A native full-duplex model receives the user's audio in every unit and decides in each unit whether to speak. When the user interrupts, the model stops speaking in the next unit. The session keeps its state and accepted input, and no session command is involved. 

### 4. How resources are released
The session ends on close, from the client or on disconnect:
- The realtime layer stops accepting input, discards queued input that has not been dispatched, and drops any output that still arrives.
- The Coordinator waits for the in-flight unit to complete. After that, it asks each stage to release the session's state. The session's capacity is returned once every stage has confirmed.

## Phase 1 implementation plan

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P["Pipeline sessions · #2035"]
    C["AR session bridge · #2069"]
    D["Realtime layer · #2070"]
    P --> C
    P --> D
```
- **Pipeline sessions**: #2035
  - Stage side: add `SessionHooks` (open, append, close) for a stage to keep session state, and `SessionScheduler` to run one unit of a session at a time under capacity limits.
  - Coordinator side: add `CoordinatorSessions` to bind workers by session ID, dispatch units in order, and release stages on close.

- **AR session bridge**：#2069
  - Add `ARSessionBridge` in the SGLang backend to map a pipeline session to a SGLang streaming session, so KV and token history stay in the core scheduler across units.

- **Realtime layer**: #2070
  - Add `SessionRuntime` behind `/v1/realtime` in OpenAI Realtime GA shape; it cuts the input stream into units at the model's cadence and sends each unit's output to the client.

## Overview
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant RT as Realtime layer
    participant CO as Coordinator
    participant P as Perception
    participant T as Thinker
    participant C as Codec

    RT->>CO: open(session S)
    Note over CO: select one worker per stage by S
    CO->>P: open
    CO->>T: open
    CO->>C: open

    Note over RT,C: unit N, m

issues.title: [Feature Request] Support release_memory_occupation / resume_memory_occupation for Omni stages
issues.body:
### Summary

It would be very useful if SGLang-Omni could officially support the upstream SGLang memory-saver lifecycle, including functionality equivalent to:

- `release_memory_occupation`
- `resume_memory_occupation`

for GPU-backed Omni stages such as ASR.

My main use case is `OpenMOSS/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize`.

---

### Environment

- SGLang-Omni: `0.1.5`
- SGLang: `0.5.19`
- Model: `OpenMOSS/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize`
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell 72GB
- Single-GPU deployment
- Docker / SGLang-Omni serving

In my current configuration, the MOSS-TD Omni service keeps roughly **21 GB of VRAM allocated while idle**.

Warm inference is very fast, so restarting the entire Omni service between jobs is not ideal.

---

### Use case

My workload is bursty rather than continuous:

```text
resume / wake MOSS-TD
        ↓
transcribe one long video
        ↓
release GPU memory
        ↓
run other GPU workloads
        ↓
resume MOSS-TD for the next job
````

Other workloads on the same GPU include LLM inference, TTS and audio source separation.

The ideal behavior would therefore be:

```text
SGLang-Omni stays alive
        ↓
MOSS stage enters sleep state
        ↓
weights / KV cache VRAM is released
        ↓
another model can use the GPU
        ↓
resume MOSS stage
        ↓
continue inference without a full cold startup
```

---

### Current behavior

The regular SGLang runtime already contains memory-saver related functionality for:

* `weights`
* `kv_cache`
* `cuda_graph`

and includes APIs / internal implementations around:

```text
release_memory_occupation
resume_memory_occupation
```

However, the SGLang-Omni HTTP server does not currently expose equivalent endpoints.

For example, with a healthy Omni service:

```bash
POST /release_memory_occupation
```

returns:

```text
HTTP 404 Not Found
```

and the same is true for:

```bash
POST /resume_memory_occupation
```

---

### Additional integration issue

I also tried enabling the underlying SGLang memory saver through the Omni engine configuration:

```text
--asr.engine.enable_memory_saver true
```

The option reaches the underlying SGLang model runner, but the ASR stage is spawned by SGLang-Omni's own multiprocessing lifecycle.

This caused the ASR worker to fail during model loading with:

```text
AssertionError: TorchMemorySaver observes invalid LD_PRELOAD.

You can use configure_subprocess() utility, or directly specify
LD_PRELOAD=...

(LD_PRELOAD="" ...)
```

This suggests that Omni's stage worker process is not currently launched under the same memory-saver subprocess configuration used by normal SGLang serving.

I experimented with local monkey patches around the Omni stage spawn path, but this is fragile and version-specific, so official support would be much preferable.

---

### Requested behavior

It would be great if SGLang-Omni officially supported putting selected stages into a GPU memory-saving state.

For example:

```http
POST /release_memory_occupation
```

```json
{
  "stages": ["asr"],
  "tags": ["weights", "kv_cache"]
}
```

and:

```http
POST /resume_memory_occupation
```

```json
{
  "stages": ["asr"],
  "tags": ["weights", "kv_cache"]
}
```

The exact API does not need to match upstream SGLang if an Omni-native admin API is more appropriate.

---

### Desired semantics

Ideally the feature would:

1. Only release memory when the selected stage is idle.
2. Keep the Omni HTTP server and control plane alive.
3. Support releasing at least:

   * model weight

issues.title: [Feasibility] Qualify MOSS-TTS-v1.5 8B on 24/32 GB consumer GPUs
issues.body:
## Goal

Qualify `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-TTS-v1.5` (Qwen3-8B delay-pattern model) on a single 24 GB or 32 GB consumer GPU without publishing an unmeasured low-memory profile.

Parent roadmap: #1120.

## Source-backed memory floor

Pinned public revisions used for this assessment:

- MOSS-TTS-v1.5 `cdd3b911b1585e3f2dbc7775ef10f9926f58850a`: 8,489,841,664 BF16 parameters = **15.81 GiB** of parameter bytes
- MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer `3cd226ba2947efa357ef453bcad111b6eafba782`: 1,774,566,400 FP32 parameters = **6.61 GiB** per copy; BF16 = **3.31 GiB**

Current `main` constructs separate audio-tokenizer models in `create_preprocessing_executor()` and `create_vocoder_executor()`, while all three stages are colocated on GPU 0. The parameter-only GPU floor is therefore:

```
15.81 GiB AR + 6.61 GiB reference encoder + 6.61 GiB vocoder = 29.04 GiB
```

This excludes CUDA context, allocator fragmentation, KV cache, CUDA Graph capture, activations, relay buffers, and generated-code tensors. The current layout is therefore not viable on 24 GB and has no credible runtime margin on a 32 GB RTX 5090.

## Candidate layout to validate

A model-specific low-memory layout can move reference preprocessing to CPU and load the vocoder codec in BF16:

```
GPU parameter floor: 15.81 GiB AR + 3.31 GiB vocoder = 19.12 GiB
CPU parameter floor: 6.61 GiB reference encoder
```

Measured card capacities from the consumer-GPU roadmap artifacts leave, before runtime allocations:

- RTX 5090 (32,607 MiB): **12.72 GiB** above the parameter floor
- RTX 4090 (24,564 MiB): **4.87 GiB** above the parameter floor

These are planning bounds, not startup evidence. The 32 GB layout is plausible at bounded concurrency; the 24 GB layout remains too close to claim without direct measurement and may require CPU vocoding, quantized AR weights, or a shared/offloaded codec design.

## Required implementation ownership

- `sglang_omni/models/moss_tts/`: explicit preprocessing device and vocoder dtype policy; no generic Stage/Scheduler branch
- example config: bounded `max_running_requests`, CUDA Graph cap, and `mem_fraction_static` derived from measured startup
- tests: production config loading and resolved factory args, plus explicit override precedence
- docs: publish only measured capacity and quality results

## Exit criteria

- [ ] Startup on one 32 GB consumer GPU with BF16 AR, CPU reference encoder, and BF16 vocoder
- [ ] Record memory after AR weights, KV allocation, CUDA Graph capture, codec loads, first request, and steady state
- [ ] Validate reference-less and reference-audio requests, streaming and non-streaming output, cancellation, and shutdown cleanup
- [ ] Sweep concurrency and graph caps; report TTFA, RTF, throughput, peak VRAM, host RAM, and power
- [ ] Run SeedTTS EN/ZH quality checks against the existing H200 references
- [ ] Run a sustained mixed-request soak including reference and non-reference traffic
- [ ] Test the same layout directly on 24 GB hardware and publish either a working bounded profile or a measured non-feasibility verdict

## Related work

- #1198 mixed several model fallbacks and carried only unit-level behavior evidence; model-specific work should supersede it
- #1287 covers MOSS-TTS Local (a different 1.7B architecture)
- #1288 covers Voxtral TTS

issues.title: [RFC] Core AI POC vs MLX-mini on Apple Silicon
issues.body:
## Motivation

show the **Apple Core AI** poc resutls.

[#1967](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/1967) already tracks first-class Apple Silicon support as **MLX (performance) + Torch/MPS (compatibility)**. Core AI is a third contract: compiled `*.aimodel` bundles, macOS 27+ system runtime, persistent KV inside Core AI, currently batch-one / greedy. It should not be folded into the model-support table in #1967 until we agree on POC scope.

This issue is the place to decide:
1. What a **bounded Core AI POC** looks like (and what it is not).
2. Why the deocode latency can not match our expection

## What we already measured

Public PoC: `adityavaid/sglang` @ `55c8cf4`, model `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`.

**M1 Pro 32 GB, macOS 27.0**, 1024-ctx batch=1 median decode step (warmup, then 128 decode tokens):

| Backend | Median decode | tok/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| MLX `mlx_q4` (group 64) | 6.77 ms | ~148 |
| MLX default BF16/fp | 10.89 ms | ~92 |
| Core AI native INT4 | 23.59 ms | ~42 |
| Core AI native FP16 | 26.18 ms | ~38 |


## Proposed POC (bounded)

Treat Core AI as an **experiment + regression sentinel**, not a production Omni backend.

In scope:

- Qwen3-0.6B only, native forward, FP16 and optional INT4 .
- macOS 27 + Apple Silicon gate (`poc.py probe` / specialization).
- Batch=1 1024-ctx per-step decode vs MLX float and `mlx_q4` on the same host.


## Related
@adityavaid Thank you for this Core AI serving PoC, especially the `coreai-opt` authoring path.

- Apple Silicon roadmap: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/1967
- Hardware reports (optional extra hosts): https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/2158

Please comment with disagreements on scope, especially whether Omni should take a Core AI dependency.

issues.title: [Qwen3-Omni] Audio encoder startup fails after Transformers helper rename
issues.body:
Qwen3-Omni fails during audio-encoder startup on main `33ba0bbf3898026862248478ace54322426b9f74` in the September 20 manual H100 nightly.

### Cause

#2267 (`2d0b48ff`) changed an external Transformers symbol reference:

```diff
- self._downsample_lengths = hf_modeling._get_feat_extract_output_lengths
+ self._downsample_lengths = hf_modeling.get_feat_extract_output_lengths
```

The workflow-pinned environment still exposes `_get_feat_extract_output_lengths`. The new reference raises before the server becomes ready.

[Failing line](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/33ba0bbf3898026862248478ace54322426b9f74/sglang_omni/models/qwen3_omni/components/audio_encoder.py#L178)

### Observed error

```text
RuntimeError: Process audio_encoder died during startup (exit code 1)

stages.py:941, in create_audio_encoder_executor
    model = Qwen3OmniAudioEncoder(...)
audio_encoder.py:178, in __init__
    self._downsample_lengths = hf_modeling.get_feat_extract_output_lengths
AttributeError: module 'transformers.models.qwen3_omni_moe.modeling_qwen3_omni_moe'
has no attribute 'get_feat_extract_output_lengths'.
Did you mean: '_get_feat_extract_output_lengths'?
```

The thinker stage reported **3 fixture errors**. This blocks inference rather than failing a performance threshold.

### Reproduction

With the CI dependencies and model/data caches prepared, at the revision above:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_model/test_qwen3_omni_thinker_length.py -v -s --maxfail=0
```

Environment: H100 80 GB HBM3, two GPUs per suite, Enroot; workflow-pinned image:

```text
hongccc/sglang-omni@sha256:ebe4239e29a764ee3a2806385c061c5fd438a26f01458e503d3822dcba5790df
```

### Suggested fix

Restore the external helper's actual name and add a constructor regression test against the pinned Transformers module. Keep checkpoint loading mocked, but exercise the real helper lookup. A fix has not been validated in this issue's reproduction.

issues.title: [Feature] Bound conversation history growth in `/v1/realtime` sessions
issues.body:
## Motivation `RealtimeSession.conversation` (`sglang_omni/serve/realtime/session.py`) is an in-memory list that grows without bound for the lifetime of the session: ```python self.conversation: list[ConversationItem] = [] ``` Every turn, `build_response_request` replays the full history into the messages array: ```python for item in self.conversation: messages.append(Message(role=item.role, content=item.text)) ``` There is no client event to delete or compact history. The conversation client-event set is limited to `session.update`, `input_audio_buffer.append`, `input_audio_buffer.clear`, `response.cancel`, and `conversation.item.truncate` — and `truncate` only removes interrupted assistant items from playback bookkeeping. The only bound today is the engine's `context_length`, which surfaces as a hard request failure mid-conversation rather than graceful degradation. For long-lived voice sessions — the primary `/v1/realtime` use case — this is a liveness problem: latency creeps up as prefill grows with each turn, and the session eventually dies at the context limit with no recovery path. The Full Duplex RFC (#2052) explicitly defers "context-usage reporting and compaction" to follow-ups. This issue claims the reporting/bounding half of that follow-up for the turn-based path, which is deployable today and independent of the duplex infrastructure work. ## Proposed design Add a `max_history_turns` (or `max_history_items`) field to `SessionConfig`, settable via `session.update`: - `null` (default): current unbounded behavior preserved. - Positive integer: keep the most recent N turns; drop oldest items on append. - The system `instructions` message is never dropped — it is built fresh each turn and does not live in the list, so this is already safe. - Dropping is applied in `run_turn` after appending the completed user/assistant pair, so a turn in progress is never partially evicted. - The effective bound is reflected in `session.created` / `session.updated` so clients can mirror server-side state. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant CL as Client participant SS as RealtimeSession Note over SS: max_history_turns = N (granted at session.update) CL->>SS: input_audio_buffer.append (speech) Note over SS: VAD speech_stopped → auto-commit SS->>SS: run_turn: response + transcription passes SS->>SS: append (user, assistant) pair SS->>SS: while len(conversation) > N: drop oldest SS-->>CL: response.* events (full current-turn reply) Note over SS: next turn's build_response_request replays
at most N turns ``` A token-based bound would be more precise but requires tokenizer access in the session layer. A turn/item-based bound is model-agnostic, trivially testable, and matches the `SessionRuntime` design direction in #2070 (transport-agnostic, typed config). A server-side default cap could follow later as a deployment flag. ## Scope split Two distinct problems share the "history growth" name, and they live on different paths: | Path | Where history lives | Bounding mechanism | Status | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Turn-based sessions (today)** | App-level `conversation` list, replayed into messages each turn | List operation, no engine changes | Deployable now — **this issue** | | **Native duplex sessions (roadmap)** | Retained KV and generated-token history in the core streaming session (#2003 / #2069); the AR bridge appends new input to that history and suppressing output does not remo

issues.title: Checkpoint path resolution is done differently in every model family
issues.body:
Loading the same repo id costs a different amount of startup time depending on which model family you use, because each family resolves the path its own way:

- six families use the shared `resolve_model_path` — llada2_uni, ming_omni, ming_tts, moss_tts, moss_tts_local, qwen3_omni
- three call `snapshot_download` directly — higgs_tts, and ming_omni / moss_tts in some paths
- about six hand the repo id straight to `from_pretrained` — arkasr, fun_asr, moss_transcribe_diarize, minimax_music3, qwen3_tts, and qwen3_asr until #1808 — which makes every such call re-resolve the repo and ask the Hub whether the cached files moved

The cost is real. On qwen3_asr this pattern was 24 Hub round trips and about 5.6 s of a 12.7 s cold start, with `config.json` revalidated five times; #1808 has the numbers.

No rewrite is needed and nothing breaks. The shared helper already exists, and after #1808 it also refuses to serve an incomplete cache, so every migrated call site inherits that check for free. A migration is a few lines per site and preserves behaviour — the helper returns the same directory the direct call resolves to. Two precedents already exist: #1808 for qwen3_asr's engine builder, and the MLX runner alignment in #1730.

Suggested path: one call site per small PR, each with a cold-start measurement, starting with the ASR families since their startup is what a laptop user waits on. I can send the ones I can test on Apple hardware; the CUDA-only families are one-line changes best done by someone who can run them.

Collaborated with Claude Code.

issues.title: [Feature] Enable torch.compile by default with persistent first-start cache
issues.body:
`torch.compile` is a proven serving optimization in SGLang Omni (lower kernel-launch overhead, fused Inductor/Triton kernels), but it is still opt-in for most models. The usual reason is cold-start cost: the first compile can add tens of seconds before the server accepts traffic.

That cost should be paid **once**, not on every process start. PyTorch already persists compiled artifacts under `~/.cache/torch/inductor` (or `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR`). If Omni treats compile + cache as part of the default server lifecycle, later restarts reuse the cache and should not re-pay the compile delay.

Hereby, we wanna to:

1. Turn `torch.compile` on by default for models that already have a supported compile path.
2. On the first `sgl-omni serve` with an empty cache, compile the live graphs and persist the artifacts.
3. Accept a one-time first-start delay of about **60 seconds**.
4. On every later start with a warm cache, skip that delay and serve with compiled kernels immediately.
5. Keep an explicit opt-out (`--enable-torch-compile false` / `engine.enable_torch_compile=false`) for debugging and unsupported backends.

`torch.compile` then becomes a default performance optimization, not a hidden flag that only expert users turn on.

issues.title: [Roadmap] Prefill/Decode Disaggregation
issues.body:
Design and mechanism co-authored by @MelodyyyYin and me; this issue indexes the work and records the change logs of measurements. The design document behind it is on [Lark](https://ylarkus3pw750a4b.usttp.larksuite.com/wiki/IOkgwbtn2iydAMkRZgnuSI28tob).

## Background

An autoregressive stage does two different jobs. Prefill reads a whole prompt in one step; decode emits one token at a time. Run both on one card and one scheduler thread, and every arriving prompt stalls the tokens already in flight. On Qwen3-Omni that cost is large and it is worst on images, because a 6127-token image prompt cannot be chunked: `_needs_full_prefill` forces the whole prompt through one step, and no decode work batches with it. Measured on one H200, the inter-token gap that overlaps a prefill is 2.28x the gap that does not.

Splitting the two jobs into separate processes is not a new idea, and we are not inventing the pieces. [DistServe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09670) made the case that separating them raises goodput per GPU. [Upstream SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) already carries the receiving side: the `PREBUILT` admission path lets a decode engine continue a request whose prompt it never ran, and its [disaggregation code](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation) keeps prefix reuse alive on both halves. This repo already carries the transport: paged KV transfer over CUDA IPC landed in #1315 and #1382 with no production consumer, and PD is its first. Stage placement, per-stage processes, and replica binding already exist too. The #1773 implementation uses explicitly declared Prefill and Decode stages and defines the contract that moves a request across their boundary.

What omni adds to the picture is that **the split ratio is not a constant**. A request's prefill share moves with its input. `docs/cookbook/moss_transcribe_diarize.md` profiles a 60-second clip at concurrency 1 with AR decode at 94.0% of total time, and a 5-second clip at concurrency 16 with the encoder at 38.2% and prefill at 29.7%. One prefill worker paired with one decode worker fits one end of that range and strands a GPU at the other. This is why placement here is a continuous parameter rather than a fixed device separation: which devices each half gets, how much of a card each half gets, and eventually how many of each there are. Compare each placement against colocated serving at equal GPU count, with the same workload and CUDA graph settings. Report throughput alongside first-token latency and token gaps; the best placement depends on the workload and its SLO.

## Design responsibilities

The explicit-stage implementation in #1773 uses the responsibilities below. It is under review and has not merged into main.

| Layer | Owns | Does not own |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Omni pipeline and runtime | Declared stages, process/replica expansion, placement, routing, completion, abort and health | KV copy protocol, sampling, model execution |
| PD handoff | The typed continuation, transfer identity, replica bindings and source lease | KV copy protocol, decode batching policy |
| CommEngine and transport | Prepare/copy/ACK exchange, transfer cancellation and source-lease lifetime | Continuation contents, sampling, scheduler admission |
| PD schedulers and DecodeKVReceiver | Source mapping export, destination reservation/commit/abort, request reconstruction, `PREBUILT` admission and scheduler-owned cleanup | Any new transport, any model-

issues.title: [Bug] Working Apple SHM setup logs errors for unused Relay dependencies
issues.body:
On a supported native Apple Silicon installation, importing the common Relay API emits ERROR messages for absent Mooncake and NIXL libraries, even though the import and SHM setup succeed. The messages make a working configuration look broken and suggest installing transport packages that it does not need.

## Environment

- Revision: `69ddc6baa9bc5430c0db63bb6fa806b778849b83`
- Hardware: Apple M1 Pro, 32 GB
- macOS 26.5.1; Python 3.12.12; Torch 2.13.0

The project's installation dependency markers deliberately omit the Mooncake/NIXL CUDA packages on macOS arm64, so their absence is expected in this supported configuration.

## Minimal reproduction

Run from the unmodified repository root on that installation. No model, inference service or microphone is needed.

```python
import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
from sglang_omni.relay.base import Relay, create_relay

print("base import succeeded")
relay = create_relay("shm", engine_id="probe", device="cpu")
print(type(relay).__name__)
relay.close()
```

Observed output includes:

```text
ERROR:sglang_omni.relay.mooncake:Failed to import mooncake: No module named 'mooncake'. MooncakeRelay will not work. Install with: pip install mooncake-transfer-engine
ERROR:sglang_omni.relay.nixl:Failed to import nixl: No module named 'nixl'. NixlRelay will not work.
base import succeeded
ShmRelay
```

## Actual behavior

The script reaches both print statements and closes the SHM relay normally. The two ERROR messages are emitted during the common import, although the script never selects Mooncake or NIXL. This directs users toward dependencies omitted by the installation configuration and makes genuine configuration failures harder to distinguish.

## Expected behavior

Importing the common Relay API or using SHM in this supported configuration should not emit ERROR solely because unused optional transports are absent. Users should be able to use SHM without installing those CUDA packages.

Explicitly selecting an unavailable backend should still fail clearly and identify the missing dependency.

## Cause

Importing `sglang_omni.relay.base` first executes the Relay package initializer. That initializer eagerly imports the Mooncake and NIXL adapters, whose ImportError handlers log ERROR when their external libraries are absent, before a transport is selected.

issues.title: [Bug from Homebrew] [Apple Silicon]: com.apple.provenance kernel-level content tracking causes portable-ruby 4.0.6 to be SIGKILLed on execution
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On macOS 15 Sequoia, Homebrew's portable-ruby 4.0.6 cannot be installed or executed. After download and extraction, the ruby binary is automatically tagged by the kernel with a new com.apple.provenance extended attribute. When any process attempts to execute this binary, the kernel sends SIGKILL(signal 9) immediately - nodialog, no prompt, no crash log.

This causes install.sh to fail at the verification step(./ruby --version), which rolls back the installation. As a result, every brew command that triggers a portable-ruby upgrade fails, making it impossible to install or upgrade any formula.

Key characteristics of com.apple.provenance:

- **Kernel-protected**: xattr -d, xattr -c, and xattr -w all return Permission denied, even for the file owner. The attribute cannot be modified or removed by user-space tools.

- **Propagates through all file operations**: Copying (cp), redirecting (cat > file), and even base64 round-tripping (base64 | base64 -d) all preserve the provenance attribute on the output file. This indicates kernel-level process/context tracking, not simple filesystem xattr inheritance.

- **Persists across filesystems**: Even when copied to an exFAT volume (which does not support extended attributes natively), the file is still tagged with both com.apple.provenance and com.apple.quarantine, and execution still results in SIGKILL.


### Actual Result
```
==> Downloading https://ghcr.io/v2/homebrew/core/portable-ruby/blobs/sha256:83a3ff85d83acf0e3dd8105de0fdb01da96b7c0eaf2dfaae2ba6500ec2ae4a64
Already downloaded: /Users/<user>/Library/Caches/Homebrew/portable-ruby-4.0.6.arm64_big_sur.bottle.tar.gz

==> Pouring portable-ruby-4.0.6.arm64_big_sur.bottle.tar.gz
/opt/homebrew/Library/Homebrew/cmd/vendor-install.sh: line 251: 95296 Killed: 9               "./${VENDOR_VERSION}/bin/${VENDOR_NAME}" --version > /dev/null

Error: Failed to install ruby 4.0.6!
Error: Failed to upgrade Homebrew Portable Ruby!
```

`sudo spctl --master-disable`

Step2：
`spctl --status`

Step3：
```
rm -rf /opt/homebrew/Library/Homebrew/vendor/portable-ruby/4.0.6
rm -f ~/Library/Caches/Homebrew/portable-ruby-4.0.6.arm64_big_sur.bottle.tar.gz
```

Step4：
`brew config`

Step5：
```
cd ~/sglang-omni
./install.sh
```

Step6：Enable Gatekeeper
`sudo spctl --master-enable`

Prerequisites:

- macOS 15.0 or later (confirmed on 15.3.1)

issues.title: [Tooling] GPU profiling reports name torch internals, not omni python code
issues.body:
## Problem

Profiling an omni stage today produces kernel-level truth and no way to act on it. The report's "Python location" column - the one column that is supposed to answer "which of our code is the bottleneck" - comes back as `torch/nn/modules/linear.py(130): forward`, `torch/nn/functional.py(5735): pad`, `torch/nn/modules/conv.py(366): _conv_forward`. Those frames say which op ran; they never say which line asked for it. The result is a report full of `nvjet_sm90_tst_...`, `elementwise_kernel<128, 4, ...BinaryFunctor<c10::BFloat16...>>` and `CatArrayBatchedCopy` that a reader cannot connect to any file they could edit. Too much low-level detail, no located bottleneck.

There is a second, quieter failure. A CUDA graph replay carries no python stack at all, so the config we actually serve cannot name our code even in principle; and a graph-off run can name it but its timings are not the ones a user pays. Concluding from one trace therefore either loses the location or measures the wrong thing - and the usual outcome is a confident wrong answer, e.g. "this stage is launch-bound, add CUDA graphs" for a stage whose production path has had graphs for months.

## Root cause

The kernel analysis itself is not ours: `/sgl-workspace/sglang/.claude/skills/llm-torch-profiler-analysis` already ranks kernels, finds overlap headroom and matches fuse patterns, and it does that well. What it does not know is that `sglang_omni/` is source code. It ranks every python frame against a fixed allowlist of repo prefixes - `python/sglang/`, `sgl_kernel/`, `vllm/`, `tensorrt_llm/`, `tokenspeed/` - and an omni frame matches none of them, so it scores as a generic `.py` frame and loses to whatever torch frame sits deeper in the stack. Three places encode that allowlist, and the important discovery is that **two of them are independent ladders that disagree**:

| where | what it ranks | omni's score | why the column goes wrong |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `profile_common.normalize_repo_relative_path` | absolute path -> repo-relative | n/a | the bare `sglang/` fallback also matches a *parent* directory called `sglang`, so a checkout at `/sgl-workspace/sglang/test3/sglang-omni` is rewritten to the fabricated path `python/sglang/test3/sglang-omni/...` |
| `triage_kernel_helpers.source_location_priority` / `is_preferred_source_location` / `frame_priority` | the **kernel table**'s location | generic `.py` = 120 | `python/sglang/` is 300 and `torch/` is demoted to 20, so torch already loses here - but omni does not win, it ties with any other `.py` file |
| `triage_overlap_helpers.choose_best_scope` / `source_scope_priority` | the **overlap table**'s "Python scope" | position in the stack + a small prefix bonus | separate code from the kernel ladder, with **no `torch/` rule at all**, so the deepest frame wins outright and the column reads `torch/nn/modules/linear.py` even when the kernel table got it right |

Hard constraint: the parent repo `/sgl-workspace/sglang` must not be modified. Any fix has to be an omni-side shim.

## What the work established

Four things that shaped the design, each of which cost a wrong run to learn:

- **Graph-off + `with_stack` is for source mapping only.** It is not a measurement config. Conclusions have to return to the graph-on serving config for paired validation, which is why the deliverable is a *pair* of traces and not a flag.
- **One-time cost charged to a steady-state kernel is the most common way a profiling run reaches a c

issues.title: [Bug] Qwen3-ASR (Apple/MLX backend): chunked transcription falls into deterministic runaway repetition loops; repetition_penalty silently ignored
issues.body:
> Checklist: searched related issues (closest: #1360, #975); reproduced on current main; environment + minimal reproducer below.

### Describe the bug

Chunked long-form transcription with **Qwen3-ASR on the Apple (MLX) backend** deterministically falls into **runaway repetition loops** inside individual chunks — e.g. a 15 s chunk whose entire output is `哎，可是我像像像像…像` (the character 像 repeated 119 times, burning the whole per-chunk token budget). On a 43 min mixed-language business call we counted 14 such loops; on a 23 min Chinese meeting, 4. The severe ones are sentence-initial filler loops (`可是，但是，但是…`, `But I just, just today, but, but, …`) and cluster in far-field / degraded-acoustics regions.

Two compounding defects make this hard to mitigate from the API:

1. **`repetition_penalty` is silently ignored for Qwen3-ASR.** The field is accepted by `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, threaded through the whole serve layer, and then dropped engine-side: `sglang_omni/models/qwen3_asr/request_builders.py` constructs `SamplingParams(max_new_tokens=…, temperature=…, top_p=1.0, …)` and never reads `repetition_penalty` (zero `repetition` matches anywhere under `models/qwen3_asr/`). Runtime proof: `-F repetition_penalty=1.3` returns **byte-identical (md5) output** to the baseline on a looping chunk.
2. **Greedy is forced, so there is no sampling-based escape hatch either**: any nonzero `temperature` fails the request (`Qwen3-ASR Apple backend currently supports only greedy decoding; set temperature=0`).

### Reproduction

Server:

```bash
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/ffmpeg@7/lib" SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 \
.venv-apple/bin/sgl-omni serve \
  --model-path mlx-community/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-4bit \
  --model-name Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B \
  --asr.engine.max_running_requests 1 \
  --audio_chunking.max_audio_clip_s 15 \
  --port 8000
```

Then:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -F model=Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B \
  -F file=@long_farfield_meeting.wav \
  -F response_format=verbose_json
```

Any long (>30 min) far-field Chinese (or zh/en mixed) meeting recording with degraded segments triggers loops in a handful of chunks. The trigger is **boundary-sensitive**: the same acoustic content, when the RMS splitter's quiet-point search shifts the cut by ~1–2 s, decodes normally (the repeated token is followed by real words), so the precise chunk matters.

**Minimal reproducer we isolated:** the exact 14.05 s chunk the serve layer cut at 1877.1 s of our call. Replayed **standalone (one request, one chunk, nothing else running)** it reproduces the loop **byte-for-byte identical** to its occurrence inside the 43 min run — ruling out scheduling and any cross-request state:

| Experiment (same 15 s chunk) | Result |
|---|---|
| baseline | loop: 像 ×119 (130 chars total) |
| `-F repetition_penalty=1.3` | **md5-identical to baseline** → penalty dropped |
| `-F max_new_tokens=64` | output truncated at 64 tokens → loop is bounded only by the per-chunk token budget |
| `-F temperature=0.5` | HTTP error: greedy-only backend |
| whole-file run, `--audio_chunking.max_concurrent_chunks 1` vs default 8 | **md5-identical, both files** (43 min and 23 min) → intra-request chunk scheduling has zero effect on output |

We can share the exact 15 s trigger WAV privately (it is cut from a confidential business call, so not attaching it here); the standalone replay above is sufficient to reproduce.

### Root-cause pointer & suggested fixes

- Wire `repetition_pen

issues.title: [Runtime Profiling] ARK-ASR
issues.body:
## Goal

Establish a reproducible first-pass runtime profile for `arkasr` (`AutoArk-AI/ARK-ASR-3B`) on current `main`, identify its dominant serving bottleneck, and turn the evidence into a bounded follow-up optimization hypothesis.

Parent tracking issue: #1798  
Runtime Profile Agent roadmap: #1650  
ARK-ASR integration context: #1396 and #1143

## Scope

Use the repository's `model-profiling` skill and the layered methodology tracked in #1798.

Discovery pass only:

- Pin and record the exact SGLang-Omni commit, SGLang/container digest, model checkpoint revision, dataset revision, GPU, driver, CUDA, and CPU affinity.
- Run the short-form SeedTTS benchmark at concurrency `1, 8, 16, 32, 64`.
- Record throughput/QPS, RTFx, p50/p95/p99/max latency, WER, request completeness/failures, realized batch sizes, CPU utilization, GPU utilization, and memory.
- Start with Layer 1 GPU-busy-ratio evidence, then follow the methodology's CPU/orchestration-bound or GPU-bound branch.
- When the CPU/orchestration branch applies, decompose audio preparation, pre-LM encoder, prefill, decode, queue/admission, and streaming-output costs.
- Verify that the intended runtime paths actually execute: pre-LM encoder service, encoder CUDA Graph, breakable prefill CUDA Graph, async decode, and embedding cache.
- Stop after discovery and report candidate Layer 4 hypotheses. Do not select or implement an optimization before the evidence is reviewed.

Long-form profiling is a follow-up unless the short-form discovery shows that input length changes the bottleneck conclusion enough to require a second Layer 1 measurement in this pass.

## Benchmark entrypoint

- `benchmarks/eval/benchmark_asr_seedtts.py`
- Related long-form follow-up: `benchmarks/eval/benchmark_asr_longform.py`

## Done when

- [x] Reproduction commands, exact environment/model/dataset revisions, hardware, GPU cleanliness, and CPU isolation are recorded.
- [x] The concurrency sweep covers `1, 8, 16, 32, 64` with warmup and raw per-request distributions retained.
- [x] Layer 1 and the applicable discovery branch are complete, with evidence strength graded using #1798's rubric.
- [x] The report states whether each intended optimized runtime path actually ran, using counters/logs/traces rather than absence of errors.
- [x] A findings–evidence–recommendation table and candidate next experiment are posted here, with small raw artifacts attached when practical.
- [x] Every process started by the run is cleaned up and GPU cleanup is verified.

## Non-goals

- No model/runtime behavior change in the discovery pass.
- No model-specific kernel work before profiling demonstrates a remaining GPU-kernel bottleneck.
- No default change or Layer 4 A/B without a separately reviewed hypothesis.

issues.title: [Bug][Ming-Omni] Video input preprocessing is incompatible with Transformers 5.x
issues.body:
## Summary

Ming-Omni video inputs fail during preprocessing on current `main`. The repository pins `transformers==5.12.1`, where `Qwen2VLImageProcessor` no longer accepts the legacy `videos=` argument used by Ming.

The failure occurs before the video encoder and Thinker run, so every Ming request containing video is currently blocked.

## Affected code

`sglang_omni/models/ming_omni/components/preprocessor.py` currently calls:

```python
result = processor.preprocess(
    images=None,
    videos=np_videos,
    return_tensors="pt",
)
```

The call was introduced with Ming video support in #471. Transformers 4.57.6 still accepted it with a deprecation warning, but Transformers 5.12.1 rejects it.

The repository directly pins Transformers 5.12.1 in `pyproject.toml` and the CPU, ROCm, NPU, and XPU dependency manifests.

## Reproduction

This reproduces on CPU and does not require the Ming checkpoint or a GPU:

```powershell
@'
import numpy as np
import transformers
from transformers import Qwen2VLImageProcessor

print("transformers:", transformers.__version__)
frames = np.zeros((2, 224, 224, 3), dtype=np.uint8)

Qwen2VLImageProcessor().preprocess(
    images=None,
    videos=[frames],
    return_tensors="pt",
)
'@ | docker run --rm -i --entrypoint python \
  hongccc/sglang-omni@sha256:02a85f00438c901c72a2eb2ef738974a807f63af3d13084445604f3344067b19 -
```

Actual result:

```text
transformers: 5.12.1
TypeError: Qwen2VLImageProcessorKwargs.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'videos'
```

## Expected behavior

Ming video frames should be converted into `pixel_values_videos` and `video_grid_thw`, then continue through the image/video encoder and Thinker.

## Proposed direction

Transformers 5.x provides a separate `Qwen2VLVideoProcessor`. Ming should use it for video while retaining `Qwen2VLImageProcessor` for images.

Because `ensure_video_list_async` already decodes, resizes, and samples frames, the video processor should be invoked with `do_sample_frames=False` to avoid sampling a second time.

A local proof using `tests/data/draw.mp4` produced:

```text
video_grid_thw: [[4, 36, 64]]
pixel_values_videos.shape: (9216, 1536)
video token count: 2304
```

The grid and tensor shape match the former Transformers 4.57.6 video-processing contract. This verifies preprocessing compatibility only; complete real-model video-to-text inference still requires separate GPU validation.

issues.title: [TTS][Qwen3] 1.7B variant: dedicated single-instance serving optimization
issues.body:
## Goal

Community deployments primarily use `Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base`, but the original tuning work focused on 0.6B. On one H100, the 1.7B single instance peaked at 10.26 QPS while same-card DP2+MPS reached 15.26 QPS (+49%), pointing to host-side serving overhead rather than a model-compute limit.

Exit criterion: bring single-instance peak within 95% of same-card DP2+MPS on the same silicon, with C16 EN WER within 0.2 points of baseline and TTFA p95 at c8/c16 degraded by no more than 10%, or document a profile-backed structural reason for the remaining gap.

## Validated outcome

| Silicon | Baseline single instance | Optimized single instance | Same-card DP2+MPS | Optimized gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H200 | 8.74 QPS | 12.40 QPS | 13.76 QPS | **+41.9%** |
| H100 | 10.59 QPS | 14.86 QPS | 15.61 QPS | **+40.3%**; 95.2% of pool peak |

Quality remained within the gate (H100 C16 EN WER: default 1.06%, optimized 1.11%, DP2 1.01%). The admission/queueing TTFA cliff was removed; H100 c64 TTFA p95 improved from 4.76s to 0.54s, and H200 c64 measured 1.08s.

## Completed work

- [x] **Admission, queueing, and host path:** #1413, #1449, #1462, #1649
- [x] **Benchmark and regression coverage:** #1505
- [x] **Streaming and vocoder foundation:** #1286, #1336, #1523, #1675, #1756, #1786
- [x] **Predictor and sampling optimizations:** #1641, #1726
- [x] **Evaluated NO-GO or superseded paths:** #704, #1643, #1722, #1733, #1790, #1847

## Remaining work

- [ ] **P0 — Eliminate the overload device-side assert.** Under load, an invalid codec value can reach the vocoder lookup and abort the pipeline (`vectorized_gather_kernel` index out of bounds; one observed run failed 230 requests). Use the reproducible `feat/qtts17-mask-shaping` fork branch to identify the first producer-side invalid tuple, enforce the producer invariant, and prove the signature is gone on both the accelerated repro and baseline paths.
- [ ] **P1 — Ship the confirmed 1.7B defaults.** After P0, rerun the no-compile H200 grid at c32/c64/c96 with `max_running_requests=64`, `cuda_graph_max_bs=64`, and isolated vocoder. If the throughput, WER, TTFA, VRAM, startup, and stability gates hold, update the 1.7B factory defaults. The previously measured admission-64 plus isolated-vocoder point reached 12.05 QPS versus the 8.73-QPS baseline, but it must be reconfirmed after #1649 removed Talker compile.

## Related active work

- **Awaiting review or merge:** #1554, #1625, #1640, #1642, #1757, #1794, #1848, #1853
- **Still needs benchmark or quality evidence:** #1581, #1698, #1753, #1772, #1846, #1852, #1855

## Optional follow-up

NVIDIA SM-selected attention backend remains an experiment, not a completion blocker. Only pursue it if profiling shows meaningful attention cost on SM100+; any backend change requires a controlled performance A/B and the full quality gate.

General Qwen3-TTS concurrency, DP/MPS deployment, and streaming/stateful work remain tracked in #1399, #1400, #1754, and their individual PRs rather than in this 1.7B single-instance Roadmap.

issues.title: MiniMax-Music3: dit_dav stage fails via device_mixin.set_device NotImplementedError, then "no NVIDIA driver" after workaround
issues.body:
Trying to serve MiniMax-Music3 (`sgl-omni serve --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-Music3 --port 8000`) on a real 2x A100-80GB instance (AWS, via Hugging Face Inference Endpoints, driver 580.159.03 / CUDA 13.0). Base environment: `hongccc/sglang-omni:dev`. Reproduced across multiple commits, including pinning to `05e268a` ("[Model] Support MiniMax Music 3 Model") — the very first commit that added MiniMax-Music3 support — so this isn't a recent regression, it appears to have never worked for this stage.

## Bug 1: `current_platform.set_device()` calls a stub that's documented as not-yet-active

```
File "sglang_omni/pipeline/stage_workers.py", line 581, in _construct_stage
    current_platform.set_device(int(gpu_id))
File ".../sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py", line 180, in set_device
    raise NotImplementedError
NotImplementedError
```

`device_mixin.py`'s own docstring says `set_device` is `[Planned]`: "Reserved interface. SGLang core still uses hardcoded calls (e.g. `torch.cuda.set_device()`). OOT implementations will NOT take effect until the core is migrated in a future PR." So `stage_workers.py`'s `_construct_stage` (specifically for the `minimax_music3_dit_dav` process) is calling an interface that isn't backed yet — this reproduces even at commit `05e268a`, the first commit with MiniMax-Music3 support at all, so it isn't a later regression.

**Workaround applied**: monkey-patched `DeviceMixin.set_device` to call `torch.cuda.set_device()` directly (matching the documented interim behavior). Confirmed via traceback that the patch takes effect.

## Bug 2: after the patch, `torch.cuda.set_device()` reports "no NVIDIA driver" in this subprocess specifically

```
File ".../torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 638, in set_device
    torch._C._cuda_setDevice(device)
File ".../torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 478, in _lazy_init
    torch._C._cuda_init()
RuntimeError: Found no NVIDIA driver on your system. Please check that you have an NVIDIA GPU and installed a driver from http://www.nvidia.com/Download/index.aspx
```

This happens **only in the `minimax_music3_dit_dav` worker subprocess**. The parent process's `nvidia-smi` (run immediately before `sgl-omni serve` starts) correctly shows both A100-80GB GPUs. Tried:
- Explicitly setting `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1` / `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all` before `serve` starts (inherited by the child) — no effect, identical error.
- Checked whether this is a fork-after-CUDA-init issue (`fork()` breaks inherited CUDA contexts) — ruled out, `spawn()` in `stage_workers.py` already uses `multiprocessing.context.SpawnContext` explicitly (`ctx: multiprocessing.context.SpawnContext`, line ~246), so it isn't a classic fork/CUDA problem either.

Haven't been able to dig further — no interactive shell access into the live GPU instance (HF Inference Endpoints only exposes logs, not exec).

## Also worth noting (unrelated but hit along the way)

Earlier attempts (before pinning `sglang-omni` and before this Dockerfile hit the base image's real ENTRYPOINT correctly) also surfaced `undefined symbol: cuFuncSetAttribute` / `undefined symbol: cuModuleGetFunction` from Triton-JIT-compiled kernels (`/root/.triton/cache/.../*.so`). Fixed by clearing `~/.triton/cache` before each run and prepending `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` onto `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (confirmed necessary — removing it reintroduced the bug in a different Triton code path). Flagging in case it's relevant to whatever's causing Bug 2 (possible shared root cause in how

issues.title: [Evaluation] Stage MiniMax Music 3 serving-fidelity and signal-integrity qualification
issues.body:
## Motivation

This is an implementation tracker following the evaluation discussion in #1481. The goal is not to define one universal "music quality" score. It is to add the parts that are actionable for a serving runtime in two reviewable stages, while keeping subjective and heavyweight learned evaluation external.

I ran a preliminary offline signal-integrity pass over the 14 MiniMax Music 3 WAV files attached to #1481. The main observations were:

- 7/14 files reached or exceeded 0 dBTP under a 4x true-peak estimate.
- 27/28 channels carried a small positive DC offset (+0.0005 to +0.0015).
- 7/14 files reached the 750-frame output cap. This is not itself an error, but recording that the cap was reached would distinguish a bounded output from a model-selected ending.
- Click and silence detectors are content-sensitive: vinyl crackle, percussion, and intentional musical breaks can trigger them. These measurements should therefore remain diagnostics unless a model-specific policy is declared.

These findings do not determine whether the generated music is good. They identify measurable serving and signal properties and motivate the staged scope below.

## Stage 1: serving-fidelity qualification

**PR:** #1996

Add an opt-in MiniMax Music 3 GPU test next to `tests/test_model/test_qwen3_tts_batch_invariance.py`.

The test will cover:

1. Same-process repeatability for identical lyrics, caption, seed, and frame cap.
2. Repeatability across a clean server restart.
3. Batch invariance between serial batch-1 requests and concurrent requests under deterministic inference.
4. Positive execution evidence from model information or runtime statistics proving that the AR classifier-free-guidance rows were actually batched.

The hard assertion will be equality of decoded PCM for the controlled deterministic protocol. Attached reference WAV hashes will be report-only because a fixed hash may also pin the hardware, driver, and kernel stack.

This stage will be run on H100 before the PR is marked ready. A failure will be reported as a serving finding rather than hidden by weakening the comparison.

## Stage 2: reusable signal-integrity benchmark

**PR:** TBD

Add a small music evaluation path under `benchmarks/`, following the repository's existing dataset/task/metric organization and existing dependencies.

Proposed report-only measurements:

- decoded format, sample rate, channel count, frame count, and duration;
- whether generation reached the requested frame cap;
- peak and estimated true peak;
- clipped-sample count;
- per-channel DC offset;
- silent-window ratio and contiguous silence regions;
- stereo correlation;
- optional comparison with a matched reference run: exact PCM, aligned correlation, and NRMSE.

Synthetic CPU tests will cover the metric implementation. Model execution and reference comparisons will remain opt-in GPU benchmarks.

## Out of scope

- A universal automated music-quality pass/fail score.
- Genre-specific thresholds without validation data.
- Adding CLAP, MuQ-MuLan, Audiobox Aesthetics, SongEval, or other model weights to SGLang Omni CI.
- Treating FAD or any single learned metric as a merge gate.
- Human-listening infrastructure inside this repository.

Prompt alignment, aesthetics, distribution metrics, and blinded listening remain useful higher-level evaluation, but they answer model-quality questions rather than whether SGLang Omni served the model faithfully.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Stage 1 test is implement
