issues.title: [RFC][Qwen3-Omni] AutoRound MXFP4/8 Scheme Support
issues.body:
### Motivation

PR #722 added Qwen3-Omni AutoRound INT4 thinker support plus an Omni-side quantization compatibility layer. This RFC extends that support to AutoRound MX exports:

- MXFP4: accepted for Thinker MoE experts only
- MXFP8: W8A8 support for validated Blackwell paths
- Talker/code2wav: remain BF16

The main rule is: Omni may translate AutoRound metadata only for combinations that the pinned SGLang runtime can execute correctly on the target hardware. Unsupported combinations of scheme, layer type, and hardware must fail fast at load time.

Note on MXFP8: MXFP8 is a W8A8 scheme by definition — activations are also
microscaled — so it is **not** a pure metadata-translation problem. The
activation path exercises the MoE kernels, the attention backend, and CUDA Graph
capture. The underlying kernels support this path (native on NVIDIA Blackwell and
on future Intel discrete GPUs based on the Xe3p-XPC architecture, code-named Crescent Island; **CRI** for short,
including the activation-quantization path), but we will still
**validate the activation path in E2E tests before claiming MXFP8 support on the
Omni side.**

### Expected Scope & Support Matrix

MX execution is hardware- and layer-type dependent, so v1 is deliberately narrow
and enforced by the loader.

#### MXFP4 Scope

| Hardware | Thinker MoE experts | Thinker dense/attention | Talker/code2wav | Execution contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hopper SM90, H100/H200 | ✅ pending E2E gate | ❌ rejected | ❌ rejected | SGLang supports MXFP4 MoE through the FlashInfer Cutlass mixed-input path. The AutoRound export is W4A4, but CUDA execution normalizes it to MXFP4 expert weights with BF16 activations (`W4A16`-style execution). The loader must record/log that A4 activations are not preserved. |
| Blackwell SM100, B200/GB200 | ✅ pending E2E gate | ❌ rejected | ❌ rejected | SGLang `flashinfer_mxfp4_moe_precision=default` quantizes activations with `mxfp8_quantize` (`W4A8`-style execution), while `flashinfer_mxfp4_moe_precision=bf16` keeps BF16 activations (`W4A16`-style execution). There is no A4 activation-preserving CUDA path. The loader must record/log that A4 activations are not preserved. |
| Blackwell SM120 | 🟡 pending validation | ❌ rejected | ❌ rejected | This path should be treated as `W4A8`-style execution, not `W4A16`, and not as preserved AutoRound W4A4. It requires separate SM120 E2E validation. |
| Intel XPU CRI | 🟡 future work | ❌ rejected | ❌ rejected | No SGLang main-source or merged-PR evidence exists for an Intel XPU W4A4 MXFP4 backend yet. The [Intel XPU roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24922) lists MXFP as future functional support. |
| Other NVIDIA | ❌ rejected | ❌ rejected | ❌ rejected | No plan. |

#### MXFP8 Scope

MXFP8 is W8A8: weights and activations are microscaled. It is not only metadata translation. It touches dense kernels, MoE kernels, activation quantization, and CUDA Graph capture.

There is no Hopper dequant-to-BF16 MXFP8 fallback in the current/pinned SGLang path. Hopper MXFP8 must be rejected unless new SGLang-side fallback work is added explicitly.

| Hardware | Thinker MoE experts | Thinker dense/attention | Talker/code2wav | Execution contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hopper SM90, H100/H200 | ❌ rejected | ❌ rejected | ❌ rejected | Current SGLang MXFP8 MoE requires SM100 on CUDA, and dense MXFP8 requires Blackwell-class CUDA paths. |
| Blackwell SM100, B200/GB200 | ✅ pending E2E gate | ✅ pending E2E gate

positioning.overview: vLLM 是目前最活跃的开源 LLM 推理与服务引擎之一，起源于 UC Berkeley Sky Computing Lab，由 2000+ 贡献者维护。它围绕 PagedAttention 这一核心内存管理技术构建，解决大语言模型推理中 KV cache 内存浪费与吞吐瓶颈问题，同时提供 continuous batching、chunked prefill、prefix caching、CUDA/HIP graph、speculative decoding、disaggregated prefill/decode 等全套高性能 serving 能力。项目处于成熟且快速演进阶段：最近三个 Release（v0.29.0 2026-09-09、v0.30.0 2026-09-22、v0.31.0 2026-10-05）显示约每两周一个版本；提交热点集中在 vllm/models、tests/v1、tests/kernels、vllm/v1、vllm/entrypoints、vllm/lora，说明 v1 架构重构、新模型接入、kernel 回归测试是当前主线。仓库规模可观：csrc/ 322 个文件（CUDA/HIP/C++ 内核）、rust/ 509 个文件（Rust 前端与 runtime）、tests/ 2341 个文件、vllm/ 872 个文件、docs/ 356 个文件、benchmarks/ 138 个文件、examples/ 267 个文件。README 明确列出支持的硬件包括 NVIDIA GPU、AMD GPU、Intel GPU、x86/ARM/PowerPC CPU，以及 TPU、Gaudi、Ascend、Apple Silicon 等插件化后端。对 GPU kernel 工程师而言，这是切入 LLM serving 内核优化的主流入口。
positioning.problem: 解决 LLM 推理 serving 中的三个核心问题：(1) KV cache 内存效率——通过 PagedAttention 将 KV 内存按需分页分配，避免预留最大长度导致的浪费；(2) 吞吐与延迟——通过 continuous batching、chunked prefill、prefix caching、piecewise/full CUDA graphs、disaggregated prefill/decode 最大化 GPU 利用率；(3) 多硬件与多模型覆盖——统一支持 200+ Hugging Face 架构、多种量化格式（FP8/MXFP8/MXFP4/NVFP4/INT8/INT4/GPTQ/AWQ/GGUF/TorchAO 等）和多种分布式并行策略（TP/PP/DP/EP/CP）。典型场景：部署开源 LLM 做在线推理服务、构建 OpenAI 兼容 API 服务器、多 LoRA 动态切换、MoE 模型分布式推理、多模态模型 serving。
positioning.users: 目标用户包括：(1) ML 工程师 / MLE 在云上或本地部署开源 LLM 做在线服务，使用 vLLM 的 OpenAI 兼容 API server；(2) 推理性能工程师优化特定模型或硬件上的吞吐、延迟、内存占用，会深入 vllm/v1/、csrc/、vllm/kernels/ 做 kernel 级调优；(3) 硬件厂商或后端插件开发者，通过 hardware plugin 接口接入新加速器；(4) 学术研究者复现或扩展 PagedAttention、speculative decoding、disaggregated serving 等方向。典型使用场景：单卡/多卡推理、disaggregated prefill-decode 分离部署、MoE expert parallelism、多 LoRA serving、量化模型推理、多模态模型推理。

landscape.difference: NVIDIA 官方推理引擎，深度绑定 TensorRT 与硬件，kernel 优化更底层但生态封闭、模型覆盖较窄、社区贡献受限；vLLM 更开放、模型覆盖广、社区驱动，但部分极致 kernel 仍需追赶。
同属开源 LLM serving，SGLang 在 RadixAttention 与结构化输出上更突出，前端更偏向编程式 API；vLLM 在硬件覆盖广度、disaggregated serving、v1 架构重构上更激进，生态与模型支持更成熟。
Rust + Python 的 HF 官方推理服务器，集成 HF 生态更紧密，但内核层面更依赖现有库；vLLM 在 PagedAttention、CUDA graph、speculative decoding、多硬件插件上更深入，kernel 自研比例更高。
端侧/CPU 优先、量化推理、轻量部署；vLLM 面向数据中心 GPU 集群，强调高吞吐 serving 与分布式推理，两者场景互补。
国内活跃的 LLM 推理引擎，TurboMind 引擎在国产硬件与部分模型上优化深入；vLLM 国际社区更大、硬件插件体系更通用，但 LMDeploy 在特定国产芯片与模型上可能更成熟。

positioning.stage: 成熟且快速演进。v0.29–v0.31 三周三个版本，v1 架构重构主线清晰，2000+ 贡献者，200+ 模型支持，生产级部署广泛使用。

codemap.layers:
vLLM 的代码组织可以清晰地划分为五层，从上到下依次为：接入层（Entrypoints & Frontend）、调度层（Engine & Scheduler）、执行层（Model Executor & Worker）、Kernel 层（csrc/ + vllm/kernels）、硬件抽象层（Platform/Device Backend）。

1) 接入层：`vllm/entrypoints/` 提供 OpenAI 兼容 API server（`api_server.py`）、CLI（`cli/main.py`）、gRPC 等入口；`rust/` 是 Rust 前端，承担高性能 HTTP 路由与请求解析，通过 PyO3 暴露给 Python。

2) 调度层：`vllm/engine/`（`llm_engine.py`、`core.py`）负责 continuous batching、chunked prefill、prefix caching 调度；`vllm/v1/` 是正在重构的 v1 架构（提交热点），将调度逻辑收敛到更清晰的 v1 Engine 中。

3) 执行层：`vllm/model_executor/` 定义模型前向逻辑；`vllm/worker/`（需验证具体路径）管理 GPU worker 与 KV cache 分配；`vllm/distributed/` 封装 TP/PP/DP/EP/CP 并行。

4) Kernel 层：`csrc/`（322 文件）包含 CUDA/HIP/C++ 内核——attention、MoE、quantization、cache 操作、collective 通信；`vllm/kernels/` 是 Python 侧 Triton/CuTeDSL 内核封装；`csrc/libtorch_stable/` 是基于 `torch::stable` API 的新一代内核（DeepSeek-V4 MLA 融合 kernel、NVFP4 quant、W8A8 CUTLASS GEMM 等）。

5) 硬件抽象层：`vllm/platforms/`（需验证）提供多后端抽象；`csrc/cpu/` 覆盖 x86/ARM/RISC-V/PowerPC/Apple Silicon；`csrc/rocm/` 为 AMD GPU；`csrc/attention/` 通过 `attention_dtypes.h` 做 dtype 分发。

这种分层让同一份调度逻辑可以跑在 NVIDIA、AMD、Intel GPU 以及 Apple Silicon CPU 上，而 kernel 优化只需在对应后端目录下修改。

codemap.data_flow:
一次典型推理请求的数据流如下：

1) 请求进入：HTTP/gRPC 请求到达 `rust/` 前端（PyO3 绑定）或 `vllm/entrypoints/api_server.py`，被封装为 `SamplingParams` + token ids，送入 `LLMEngine.add_request()`。

2) 调度：`vllm/engine/llm_engine.py` 的 `EngineCore` 运行 scheduler（`scheduler.py`），根据 PagedAttention 的 block table 状态决定本轮调度哪些 request 的 prefill/decode。调度器输出 `SchedulerOutputs`，包含选中的 request 列表、它们的 block allocation、是否为 chunked prefill。

3) 模型前向准备：`vllm/model_executor/` 的 model runner 将调度结果组装为 `ModelInput`（包含 input_ids、positions、block_tables、slot_mapping 等 IR），通过 `vllm/ir/`（Intermediate Representation）做图捕获。

4) Worker 执行：`vllm/worker/`（需验证路径）的 `Worker` 在对应 device 上调用 `model_executor.execute_model()`，触发模型 forward。

5) Kernel 层计算：forward 过程中调用各 kernel——
   - `csrc/attention/` 或 `csrc/libtorch_stable/attention/` 做 paged attention / FlashMLA / TRTLLM-GEN attention
   - `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/` 做 FP8/NVFP4/MXFP4 量化 GEMM（CUTLASS、CuTeDSL、Marlin、Machete）
   - `csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/` 做 MoE routing + grouped GEMM
   - `csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu` 做 `reshape_and_cache`（将新 KV 写入 paged cache）
   - `csrc/libtorch_stable/activation_kernels.cu` 做 SwiGLU/GeGLU 等激活
   - `csrc/libtorch_stable/pos_encoding_kernels.cu` 做 RoPE

6) 采样：logits 回到 `vllm/model_executor/layers/sampler.py`（需验证），调用 `csrc/cpu/sampling_kernels.cpp` 或 GPU sampling kernel 做 top-k/top-p/greedy/Gumbel-max 采样。

7) 输出处理：采样结果经 `engine/output_processor.py`（需验证）做 detokenize、stop string 检查、streaming 输出，最终通过 entrypoints 返回给客户端。

关键数据结构：`SequenceGroup`（请求组）、`Sequence`（单个序列）、`BlockTable`（PagedAttention 块表）、`ModelInput`（IR）、`SchedulerOutputs`（调度结果）、`SamplerOutput`（采样输出）。调度点：`EngineCore.step()` → `scheduler.schedule()` → `worker.execute_model()` → `model_executor.execute_model()`。

install: # 1. 安装 uv（macOS 推荐用 Homebrew 或官方脚本）
brew install uv  # 或 curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
# 2. 创建 Python 3.12 虚拟环境（Apple Silicon 上 3.12 最稳）
uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate
# 3. 安装 CPU 专用依赖（跳过 CUDA/ROCm）
uv pip install -r requirements/common.txt
uv pip install -r requirements/cpu.txt
# 4. 关键：强制 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu，避免 setup.py 尝试编译 CUDA 扩展
# setup.py 中明确有逻辑：macOS 上若 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE != 'cpu' 会自动降级为 cpu
# 但显式设置可避免触发 torch.cuda 相关检查
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu
# 5. 使用预编译扩展editable安装（跳过本地编译 csrc/ 中的 CUDA 内核）
# 这是 AGENTS.md 推荐的方式，Apple Silicon 上无法编译 .cu/.cuh 文件
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto
# 6. 若上一步失败（无预编译 wheel 匹配当前 torch 版本），尝试纯 Python 安装
# 这会跳过 C++/Rust 扩展编译，仅安装 Python 包
# uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation
# 7. 安装测试依赖（CPU 子集）
uv pip install -r requirements/test/cuda.in  # 或 requirements/dev.txt
no_gpu_paths: 可执行路径（CPU/MPS）：
- csrc/cpu/ 下所有 .cpp/.hpp：cpu_attn.cpp、cpu_fused_moe.cpp、layernorm.cpp、sampling_kernels.cpp、mamba_cpu.cpp、dnnl_kernels.cpp 等，这些是纯 C++ 实现，Apple Silicon 上通过 -mcpu=apple-m1 或 NEON 指令编译
- vllm/kernels/ 中部分 Triton/CuTeDSL 内核：若 torch 支持 MPS backend，部分 kernel 可回退到 MPS；但多数 CUDA-specific kernel（如 paged_attention、flash_attn）无法执行
- vllm/engine/、vllm/v1/、vllm/entrypoints/：调度逻辑纯 Python，可在 CPU 上跑通流程（但推理极慢）
- tests/platforms/、tests/cpu/（若存在）：平台抽象层测试
只能读代码或需 Colab T4 验证：
- csrc/libtorch_stable/ 下所有 .cu 文件：activation_kernels.cu、cache_kernels.cu、fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu 等，全部依赖 CUDA API
- csrc/attention/ 下 .cuh 文件：attention_generic.cuh、dtype_fp8.cuh 等
- csrc/cutlass_extensions/、csrc/moe/、csrc/quantization/：CUTLASS/CuTe 内核
- tests/kernels/、tests/cuda/、tests/rocm/：GPU 专用测试
- rust/ 目录：Rust 前端需要 cargo 编译，且部分模块依赖 CUDA 特性

- 完整 tests/ 套件：数小时，且多数需 GPU
debug_tips: 断点：
- 在 vllm/engine/core.py 的 schedule() 函数设断点，观察 continuous batching 调度逻辑
- 在 vllm/worker/cpu_model_runner.py（若存在）的 execute_model() 设断点，跟踪 CPU 推理流程

日志开关：
- VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG：开启详细日志
- VLLM_TRACE_ENGINE=1：追踪引擎内部状态变化
- VLLM_KV_CACHE_MONITOR=1：监控 KV cache 分配
环境变量：
- VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu：强制 CPU 模式
- VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1：使用预编译扩展
- VLLM_SKIP_RUNTIME_ENV_CHECK=1：跳过运行时环境检查（加速启动）

Profiling 入口：

runbook.ci:
CI 系统：Buildkite（.buildkite/ 目录，225 个文件）

主要流水线：
- test-pipeline.yaml：主测试流水线
- test-amd.yaml：AMD GPU 测试
- ci_config.yaml、ci_config_rocm.yaml、ci_config_intel.yaml：多硬件配置
- performance-benchmarks/：性能基准测试
- lm-eval-harness/：模型评估测试

PR 会被卡住的条件：
1. pre-commit 失败（.clang-format、.ruff、setup.py 检查）
2. 代码覆盖率下降（codecov.yml）
3. 测试失败：tests/v1/、tests/kernels/、tests/models/ 是热点区域
4. 文档构建失败（docs/ 目录）
5. Rust 编译失败（rust/ 目录）
6. 多硬件测试不通过（NVIDIA/AMD/Intel GPU）

注意：Apple Silicon 上无法运行 CI 中的 GPU 测试，需在 Colab T4 上验证
pitfalls: 1. 编译陷阱：Apple Silicon 上无法编译 CUDA 扩展（.cu/.cuh 文件），必须使用 VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 跳过编译，否则 setup.py 会报错或尝试 hipify 失败
2. PyTorch 版本锁定：pyproject.toml 要求 torch==2.13.0，但 Apple Silicon 上 PyTorch 的 MPS 版本可能有差异，需确认 torch 版本兼容性
3. Rust 前端编译：rust/ 目录需要 cargo 和 Rust 工具链（rust-toolchain.toml），且部分模块依赖 CUDA 特性，Apple Silicon 上可能编译失败
4. 内存限制：16GB 统一内存极小，跑稍大的模型（如 7B）会 OOM，建议用 opt-125m 或 gpt2 测试
5. 性能误导：CPU 推理速度极慢（比 GPU 慢 100x+），不要以 CPU 性能评估优化效果
6. 测试过滤：tests/ 中多数测试标记了 @pytest.mark.cuda 或需要 GPU，直接跑全量测试会大量跳过或失败，必须用 -k 'cpu' 或 -m 'not cuda' 过滤
7. 预编译 wheel 不可用：vLLM 官方 wheel 通常只含 CUDA 扩展，Apple Silicon 上可能找不到匹配的预编译版本，需做好纯 Python 安装的准备
8. dnnl 依赖：csrc/cpu/dnnl_kernels.cpp 需要 oneDNN 库，requirements/cpu.txt 可能未正确拉取，需手动 brew install onednn
9. NEON/AMX 指令：csrc/cpu/cpu_attn_neon.hpp 等依赖 ARM NEON 指令，Apple Silicon 支持但需确认编译器标志（-mcpu=apple-m1）
10. 调度逻辑误解：vllm/v1/ 是重构中的新架构，部分 API 与 v0 不同，阅读代码时注意区分 EngineCore 的 v0/v1 实现

community.process: 1. 先 Issue / RFC：AGENTS.md 明确要求『Before proposing a PR, run these checks』，用 gh issue view / gh pr list 检查重复工作；若已有 open PR 处理同一修复则不得重复提交。2. DCO：仓库根目录有 DCO 文件，提交需带 Signed-off-by。3. pre-commit：.pre-commit-config.yaml 存在，AGENTS.md 要求『Always make sure pre-commit and its hooks are installed』并运行 pre-commit install。4. AI 辅助贡献：AGENTS.md 有完整规定——纯 code-agent PR 不被允许，必须有人类提交者理解并逐行 review；PR description 必须说明为何不重复已有 PR、跑了哪些测试、模型评估结果、并明确声明使用了 AI 辅助。5. 测试：AGENTS.md 要求用 uv 管理环境，跑 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/path/to/test_file.py -v。6. 不得提交低价值 busywork PR（单 typo、孤立 style 改动等）。
community.review_style: 从 Issue 与 PR 评论推断：(1) 性能相关 Issue（如 #60008、#59534、#25094）要求给出具体数字（µs、% throughput），不接受模糊描述；(2) Bug 报告（如 #60007、#59086）需要最小复现命令与硬件/模型/dtype 信息；(3) RFC 类 Issue（如 #59055、#59382、#38175）讨论较充分，维护者会引导方向；(4) 响应速度：活跃 Issue 多在 1-2 天内有回复，但 stale 标签的 Issue（如 #28467、#28498）长期无人处理；(5) 对 kernel 优化 PR 审查严格，需附带 benchmark 数据。
etiquette: 得体：(1) 提 PR 前用 gh issue view / gh pr list 检查重复工作，在 PR description 中明确说明为何不重复已有 PR；(2) 性能相关改动附带 benchmark 数据（µs、% throughput、硬件型号）；(3) Bug 报告给出最小复现命令、模型、dtype、硬件；(4) 使用 AI 辅助时在 PR description 中明确声明；(5) 通过 uv 管理环境，不用系统 python3 或裸 pip；(6) 提交前跑 pre-commit 与相关测试。

不得体：(1) 提交低价值 busywork PR（单 typo、孤立 style 改动、one mutable default），AGENTS.md 明确禁止；(2) 纯 code-agent PR 无人类 review，会被自动封禁；(3) 重复已有 open PR 的工作而不解释差异；(4) 性能 Issue 无具体数字、Bug 报告无复现步骤；(5) 用系统 python3 或裸 pip install 而非 uv。
what_they_want: (1) Batch Invariant 性能优化：Issue #27433（99 条评论，4 位 assignee）是当前重点，涉及 kernel 层面的确定性输出与性能权衡。
(2) ROCm / AMD GPU 性能：Issue #57149、#59575、#56021 显示 gfx950/MI355X 与 RDNA 后端急需优化，vllmellm 是主要对接人。
(3) torch.compile 量化性能：Issue #25094（QuantFP8 group quantization 慢于 CUDA）与 #39479（config hashing refactor）需要跟进。
(4) Mamba / Hybrid 模型 prefix caching：Issue #60008 显示 mamba_cache_mode="align" 有 11-16% 吞吐损失，需 kernel 层面优化。
(5) 新模型接入与性能优化：Issue #57406（GLM 5.3）、#52613（MiniMax-M3 MXFP8）、#59784（Qwen3-VL-Reranker）等显示 200+ 模型覆盖带来持续维护压力。
(6) 测试覆盖：tests/v1、tests/kernels 是提交热点，显示 v1 架构重构与 kernel 回归测试需要更多贡献。
(7) 文档：Issue #41230（NIXL KV connector metrics 文档）等显示部分功能文档缺失。
(8) Transformers v5 升级：Issue #38379 是长期任务，需要熟悉依赖迁移的开发者。

issues.title: [Performance]: Hybrid Mamba prefix caching (`mamba_cache_mode="align"`) costs 11-16% throughput on Nemotron-3.5-Lightning with no cache hits: per-group eager block-table ops, per-step align kernels outside CUDA graphs, and block-boundary prefill splits
issues.body:
## Summary

Turning on prefix caching for a hybrid Mamba2 model forces `mamba_cache_mode="align"`
(`vllm/model_executor/models/config.py:640-656`; since
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58997 the only modes are `none` and `align`).
On NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (4x GB200, DP4/EP4, Model Runner V2),
with a random 8K-in / 1K-out workload where nothing ever hits the cache, align mode
costs:

- **Output throughput: -13.4% to -16.2%** (median of 6 paired rounds, c=1/8/32/64).
- **TPOT: +14% to +20%** from align mode itself, independent of block size and of
  prefill splitting. The decode step has **28 extra eager launches**: 4 Mamba
  KV-cache groups x 7 torch ops in `mamba_get_block_table_tensor`. The V2 align
  pre-process / pre-copy / post-process kernels also run every step outside the
  CUDA graph. GPU compute per step is unchanged; **GPU idle time per step grows by
  0.55-0.75 ms**.
- **TTFT at c=1: x1.8** (125 -> 229 ms). The scheduler splits an 8192-token prompt at
  the block boundary (4176 + 4016), and each prefill step carries 70-90 ms of fixed
  non-GPU cost, which is now paid twice.
- Block size and KV capacity are **not** the cause. With prefix caching off, changing
  the block size to 6768 or 8192 stays within run-to-run noise. All configurations
  have >= 576x max concurrency and zero preemptions.

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, prefix caching for Mamba2 is currently rejected at
startup. A two-line fix (copy all 5 exact-replay states in align mode) makes hits and
misses bitwise equal to prefix caching off. The extra copy costs about 9.4 us per step.
That fix is not a PR yet; see the batch-invariance section below.

This issue collects the measurements, the root cause and what the open PRs cover, so
that someone can pick up the remaining work.

## Environment

- Hardware: 1 node, 4x NVIDIA GB200 (NVLink).
- Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4` (ModelOpt mixed
  precision: W4A16 NVFP4 routed and shared experts and lm_head, FP8 Mamba
  in_proj/out_proj). 23 Mamba2 layers, `chunk_size=128`.
- vLLM: upstream `main` at `6e517b15c1` (2026-10-02, already contains #58997) plus
  12 out-of-tree commits (build `a92e2ac3c4`). The out-of-tree commits add a
  FlashInfer CuTe-DSL W4A16 MoE expert backend (selected by
  `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutedsl`), the batch-invariant Mamba2 exact-replay stack
  from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55905, and two DP sampler-seed
  fixes. None of them touches the align-mode path: `vllm/v1/core/`,
  `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py` and
  `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py` are identical to `6e517b15c1`,
  and the `mamba_utils.py` changes only take effect under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`.
  All file:line references below are against `6e517b15c1`.
- Runtime: Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`), `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`
  unless stated, async scheduling default, CUDA graph mode `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`
  (default for this model).
- Parallelism: TP1, DP4, expert parallel (EP4), all2all
  `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`.
- MoE: `flashinfer_cutedsl` (CuTe-DSL W4A16 experts). Attention: FlashInfer, FP8 KV
  cache (`fp8_e4m3`).
- Client: `vllm-rs bench serve` (in-tree Rust benchmark, `rust/src/bench`), random
  dataset with token-id prompts, 8192 in / 1024 out, `--ignore-eos`, temperature 0,
  `--request-rate inf`, `--max-concurrency` 1/8/32/64,
  `--num-prompts max(4c, 8)` after a warmup point of `max(c, 4)` requests.

## Measure

issues.title: [RFC]: Release all releasable GPU memory in sleep mode (tracking)
issues.body:
> **Update (tracking).** This issue started as a report about WorkspaceManager memory (original report below, by @penguin-wwy). Investigation showed that the workspace is one of several allocations that sleep mode leaves on the GPU. This issue now tracks all of them.

### Summary

Colocated RL setups call `/sleep` to hand GPU memory back to the trainer. With only `weights` and `kv_cache` under sleep-mode management, a sleeping DeepSeek-V4 engine still holds **14–21 GiB per GPU**. We attributed that memory to its owners on 4× GB300. The PRs below make the releasable parts releasable. With all of them applied, what remains is 5.6–6.2 GiB per GPU on DeepSeek-V4 (3.9–4.7 GiB with the existing `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend` plus #59360). Most of it is driver-side state: CUDA graph executables and the CUDA context.

### Current main (2026-10-04, `bdd31c31d`, with #59156/#59158/#59160 merged)

Memory per GPU while asleep (level 1), MiB, saving vs the first column in parentheses. Every run is bit-exact against the awake run (28 greedy + 28 seeded top-k/top-p probes, 3 cycles). "Open PRs" = #59228 + #59909 + #59360 + #59939 + #59625 + #59934 applied together.

| Model / setup | Main, sleep mode | Main + `--sleep-mode-offload-cudagraph` | Open PRs + `--sleep-mode-offload-cudagraph --enable-nccl-comm-suspend` | ... + #59537 + #59540 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 + EP4, MTP | 10869 | 8633 (−2236) | **6451 (−4418, 41%)** | **6097 (−4772, 44%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DP4 + EP4, DeepGEMM MoE, fp8 KV, mbt 8192 | 9953 | 8507 (−1446) | **7355 (−2598, 26%)** | **7323 (−2630, 26%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DP8 + EP8 over 2 nodes (this issue's setup) | 9941 | 8495 (−1446) | **7343 (−2598, 26%)** | **7327 (−2614, 26%)** |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 over 2 nodes, MTP off | 13653 | 6123 (−7530) | **4481 (−9172, 67%)** | **4247 (−9406, 69%)** |
| GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8 over 2 nodes, MTP | 20945 | 11655 (−9290) | **9991 (−10954, 52%)** | **9787 (−11158, 53%)** |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8, TP4 + EP4 | 7617 | 7341 (−276) | **5051 (−2566, 34%)** | **4961 (−2656, 35%)** |

- #59909 frees the same graph memory as the merged backup mode, without the CPU copy (7.4 GiB/GPU less pinned host memory on V4.1).
- #59537 moves graph-capture memory to the KV cache (+0.62 GiB/GPU on V4-Flash TP4, +4.57 GiB/GPU on GLM-5.2).
- Qwen3-235B level 2 + `reload_weights`: bit-exact, same asleep memory as level 1.
- Wake takes 0.2-1.4 s longer with `--enable-nccl-comm-suspend`.
- These numbers are higher than the 09-30 tables below. On V4-Flash TP4 the 2.3 GiB gap breaks down as: +1.3 GiB of CUDA graph executable memory from this cluster's driver (the 09-30 code measures the same on this node; the 09-30 tables are from a different GB300 cluster), +0.5 GiB of MTP runner buffers that the merged #59158 no longer tags (a follow-up puts the model runner back in the `runtime` pool), and +0.5 GiB of FlashInfer TRT-LLM allreduce workspace since #56891, which #59360 releases. Host RSS stays at the asleep level after wake because PyTorch caches the pinned backup buffers.

### What stays on the GPU, and which PR releases it

| Resident while asleep | PR | How | Contents after wake |
|---|---|---|---|
| WorkspaceManager scratch (MoE / attention workspaces, scales with DP × `max_num_batched_tokens`) | #59156 | allocated in a `workspace` cuMem pool | discarded (scratch) |
| State built with the KV cache (block tables, sparse-MLA and indexer metadata) and buffers owned by the m

issues.title: [Bug]: TRITON_MLA is not batch invariant under chunked prefill with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (DeepSeek-V2-Lite, DeepSeek-V3.1)
issues.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM `main` at `f590eb2448a51028f6044c6f60104ce0ef3189e9`, torch 2.13.0+cu130
- NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3), driver 580.167.08, CUDA toolkit 13.1
- Models: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` (TP=1) and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` (TP=4)
- Attention backend: `TRITON_MLA`, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`

### 🐛 Describe the bug


With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the output of an MLA model changes when its prefill is split into chunks. Both DeepSeek models above fail the chunked-prefill test of the batch-invariance suite, while their needle tests and `bs1_vs_bsN` bitwise tests pass. Both are on the tested-models list in `docs/features/batch_invariance.md`.

**Repro**

```bash
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat \
  pytest -v -s "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_logprobs_bitwise_batch_invariance_ragged_chunked_prefill[TRITON_MLA]"
```

```text
AssertionError: Batch invariance violated under chunked prefill (max_num_batched_tokens=131):
prompt 1 (263 tokens): logprobs differ, max|delta|=8.945e-02; prompt 8 (248 tokens): tokens differ;
prompt 10 (97 tokens): tokens differ; ...
```

Three runs in fresh processes give the same failure and the same delta. `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` fails the same test the same way.

**Isolation**

The difference does not need other requests in the batch. One prompt run alone, with only the token budget changed:

| `max_num_batched_tokens` | Prefill | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 | one chunk | reference |
| 131 | several chunks | selected-token logprobs differ from the first step (about 1e-3), sampled tokens differ from decode step 9 |

Other observations:

- With `max_num_batched_tokens=4096` the batched test input shows no mismatch. With 512 one prompt still mismatches.
- `enforce_eager=True` still fails, so CUDA graphs and `torch.compile` are not needed to trigger it.
- Prefix caching is off (the test disables it, and it is disabled for `TRITON_MLA` in batch-invariant mode).

Since chunk boundaries depend on the scheduler's token budget, and so on the other requests in the step, this makes the output depend on batch composition.

**Suspected area (not proven)**

The MLA prefill path for a chunk that has cached context (`_compute_prefill_context` in `mla_attention.py`): cached context is gathered and up-projected per context chunk, attended separately, and combined with `merge_attn_states`. A single-chunk prefill does not go through that merge, and merging LSE-rescaled partial results is not bitwise associative. I have not instrumented it at layer level. #46592 discusses canonical chunk boundaries for a related reason (prefix caching).

**CI coverage**

The Batch Invariance jobs run the full `test_batch_invariance.py` only with the default model. For `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` they run only the needle test with `-k TRITON_MLA`, so the chunked-prefill test (added in #55612) is not exercised for `TRITON_MLA`.

I only ran this on GB300, but nothing in this path looks Blackwell-specific. Happy to run more experiments on this hardware.



### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issues.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 (MXFP8) streaming: generation stops (empty delta, finish_reason=stop) right after reasoning closes, whenever a tool call should follow — non-streaming with identical payload succeeds
issues.body:
### Your current environment

`collect_env.py` could not be run on this host — no outbound internet access (air-gapped deployment). Manually collected equivalent below.

**Versions**
- vLLM: `0.27.0` (build `vllm-0.27.0-tp4-41db7380`)
- PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu129`
- Transformers: `5.15.0`
- GPU: 4x NVIDIA H200 (143771 MiB), driver `595.58.03`

**Model**
- `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3`
- Quantization: `mxfp8` (NVIDIA ModelOpt MXFP8 checkpoint, `weight_block_size=[1,32]`, MoE via `MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel`/`MARLIN` backend) — vLLM's own startup log flags this format as *"experimental and could change in future"*

**Launch command**
```bash
vllm serve /model --served-model-name MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --block-size 128 --max-model-len 65536 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```



### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `stream: true` and `tools` provided, for requests where the model's reasoning is longer / more hedging before deciding to call a tool, the SSE stream **stops immediately after the reasoning block closes**: the next chunk has an empty `delta` and `finish_reason: "stop"`. Nothing is generated after that — no content, no `tool_calls`. This is not a parsing failure; generation itself halts.

The byte-identical payload sent with `"stream": false` succeeds reliably (tested 6/6).

> **Note:** only reproduced so far on an MXFP8-quantized checkpoint (NVIDIA ModelOpt format). Untested whether an unquantized bf16 checkpoint is also affected.

**Minimal repro**

Flat 2-field tool schema — confirmed tool schema complexity/count is not the trigger (fails the same way with 1 tool or 5 tools):

```python
import requests

payload = {
    "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3",
    "stream": True,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "сделай docx с названием test и текстом привет"}],
    "tools": [{
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "generate_docx_report",
            "description": "Generate a Word document from content.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "filename": {"type": "string"},
                    "content": {"type": "string"},
                },
                "required": ["filename", "content"],
            },
        },
    }],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
}

r = requests.post("http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions", json=payload, stream=True)
for line in r.iter_lines():
    if line:
        print(line.decode())
```

**Expected**

Reasoning closes, then either visible content or a populated `tool_calls` delta follows — same as the non-streaming response to the identical payload (`"stream": False` above).

**Observed**

After the last reasoning chunk, the stream emits one more chunk with an empty delta and `finish_reason: "stop"`, then ends. Nothing else is generated.

**Ruled out**
- Tool schema size — reproduces with both a minimal flat 2-field schema and a real ~2KB docstring-heavy schema
- Tool count — 1 tool vs 5 tools, same result
- Payload size in general — byte-identical payloads, only `stream` differs

**Correlation observed (not confirmed causal)**

Requests where the model's own reasoning is short/decisive stream through fine. Requests where reasoning is longer with self-correction (*"But I should check... Actually... Let me reconsider..."*) reliably hit the halt.

**Current work

issues.title: [Feature]: Integrate Cake kernels via FlashInfer: model-by-model tracker
issues.body:
**End-to-end validation and issue reporting:** Our shape coverage and correctness have not yet been validated end to end in model serving. If you encounter (1) end-to-end accuracy degradation, (2) unsuitable API requirements, such as unnecessarily requiring contiguous inputs, or (3) faster kernel benchmarks but worse end-to-end performance because the shapes optimized by the kernel do not cover the actual model-serving workload, please open an issue and tag @yyihuang with the affected kernel, the missing or problematic shape(s), and relevant model/serving details or a reproducer. We will resolve reported issues within **6 hours**.

## Motivation

Track integration of Cake kernels already delivered through FlashInfer into vLLM, grouped by the models that requested them. The upstream inventory is [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254); model requirements below come from its subissues and the linked implementation PRs.

The proposed integration is through FlashInfer's public/prepared APIs. Each task should connect the relevant model operator, weight/cache layout, and execution mode to an eligible kernel, then measure the complete serving path. Upstream kernel benchmarks are useful starting points, not claims of vLLM end-to-end speedup.

**Snapshot: 2026-10-03 (UTC; October 2 in US Pacific); FlashInfer main [46340689a5ab](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/46340689a5ab5665ab39f6281dac4d021d7ae94b).** “Merged” below means available in upstream FlashInfer, not necessarily in a released wheel or integrated here. Open follow-ups are explicitly marked and are not included in the merged coverage. Most listed kernels target SM100/SM103; exact architecture, SM-count, dtype, layout, and shape admission remain API-specific. Let the serving adapter retain its existing backend for configurations outside those contracts.

Notation: `T/M` = token rows, `B` = requests, `Q` = query tokens per request, `S` = KV length. MoE tuples are **(hidden size, expert intermediate size, number of experts, top-k)**; an intermediate size marked “local” is after TP sharding. Enumerated benchmark shapes are evidence points, not an assertion that every combination is supported.

## Integration and acceptance

- [ ] Pin a FlashInfer revision/release containing the required merged APIs and register backend selection at the existing operator boundary.
- [ ] Check the selected release branch separately: [#5978](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5978) is merged into `release-v0.7.1` only and reverts the BF16 head-dim-256 small-M speculative-decode route because of an intermittent B200 hang. This is a separate route from the E4M3/page-64 DCP entries below; a merge on the release branch does not establish a fix on main.
- [ ] Prepare weights, plans, output buffers, and workspaces before graph capture; account for changing request lengths, routing, state indices, and graph buckets.
- [ ] Validate each listed model/checkpoint, quantization recipe, TP/EP/CP configuration, and state/cache layout. Cover prefill, decode, speculative verification, ragged batches, and prefix-cache reuse where relevant.
- [ ] Compare against the current engine backend on model quality, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, and memory. Record the actual selected route and unsupported configurations before changing defaults.

vLLM already has FlashInfer hooks for several of these models. This tracker proposes selecting and qualifying the Cake

issues.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (hybrid GDN + MoE): a prompt's logprobs move by up to 0.2 when another sequence shares its engine step (v0.30.0, sm_120)
issues.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM 0.30.0 (pip wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12
- 1x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (sm_120), driver 580.178.04
- `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`
- `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` @ `95a723d`, default engine arguments; also `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` (bf16) @ `995ad96`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

A lone prompt is bit-reproducible, but **the same batch of two identical prompts, submitted twice, gives different logprobs** (up to 0.168), and a prompt's logprobs move by up to 0.2 when another sequence shares its engine step.

**Reproduction** (the script is below; it uses nothing beyond vLLM). The same 1,400-token prompt (random token ids) is scored for one output token, with logprobs over 20 allowed ids, four ways:
1. alone;
2. alone again;
3. as both rows of a batch of two;
4. the same batch of two again.

Over 20 prompts:

| Comparison | max \|Δ logprob\| |
| --- | ---: |
| alone, repeated | 0.0 |
| alone against a batch of two | 0.198 |
| batch of two, repeated | 0.168 |

**The part we think is a defect** is the last row: something in the multi-sequence path is non-deterministic from run to run, not only batch-variant.

**Why the size matters.** We understand vLLM is not batch-invariant outside `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, and that batch-invariant GDN support is in progress (#48613, #49827, #55868). Today that mode refuses this model at start ("not supported for GDN_ATTN").
In a decision-style use that reads one token's distribution over a few options, the chosen option changed on 10 to 17% of 272 real prompts when the same prompt was scored in a batch.
This model amplifies small rounding differences strongly: with our serving code, the same lone prompt prefilled in one step (prefix caching off) and split at a block boundary (prefix caching on, align mode) differs by up to 0.44 in a probability (median 0.068).

**What we measured on top, with our serving code** (272 prompts of about 1,425 tokens, 100 for most factors; one factor changed per engine start).
- The batch effect stays with each of:
  - prefix caching off;
  - `max_num_batched_tokens=32768` (no prompt split);
  - `--gdn-prefill-backend triton`;
  - `enforce_eager=True`;
  - `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype` float32 or bfloat16;
  - `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:16:8 CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_SIZE=1`;
  - the bf16 checkpoint (max |Δp| 0.19 to 0.42 over 100 prompts), so the FP8 kernels are not required.
- It vanishes with `max_num_seqs=1`: exactly 0.0 in every condition.
- A row read from the prefix cache and the same row recomputed are bit-identical when each is alone.

**Also observed:** with `enable_return_routed_experts=True`, a lone request's routed experts are reproducible.
For two identical requests in one batch, about 40% of (token, layer) entries differ from the lone request's from token 0 onwards, while the two copies agree with each other.
Token 0 attends only to itself, so we read this as the per-request capture being misaligned when several requests share a step; possibly a separate issue.

**Question:** which kernel in this model's multi-sequence path is non-deterministic between identical runs? Candidates we could not separate: the Triton fused MoE (it runs with the default config on sm_120, "Using default MoE config"), the GDN chunked prefill over varlen batches, and FA2 varlen. #54945 reports identical-request non-determinism in a different MoE path (FlashInfer CUTLASS NVFP4, fused finalize); it may be related.

issues.title: [Performance]: spec-decode boot-to-boot throughput dispersion on L4 (CV up to 13.92%), resolved in 0.30.0
issues.body:
### Proposal to improve performance

Not a proposal so much as a measurement suggestion. Speculative-decoding throughput on this stack is boot-dependent to a degree a single-boot benchmark cannot see: on 0.29.0 / L4, twelve boots of a byte-identical configuration gave CV 13.92% in one container and 3.73% in another. Anything comparing speculative configurations from one boot each is partly measuring which boot it got.

0.30.0 looks much better on this axis (0.99% and 1.61% across two containers on different physical cards), so this may already be resolved. I am reporting it mainly because the mechanism is not what I assumed, and the protocol seems worth having on record either way.

### Report of performance regression

Reporting this because 0.30.0 appears to resolve it, and the obvious explanation turns out to be wrong, so something else changed and I would like to know what.

**Setup.** Qwen3-4B target, `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` drafter, 5 speculative tokens, bf16 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, FlashInfer pinned. GSM8K, concurrency 1, one fixed prompt set replayed on every boot. 12 boots per arm inside a single container, one physical GPU per session (UUID recorded). The harness speaks HTTP only and never imports vLLM.

Throughput at concurrency 1, output tokens/s:

| card | engine | session | default | --enforce-eager | ratio | default CV |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L4 (SM89) | 0.29.0 | A | 39.2 | 80.5 | **0.487** | **13.92%** |
| L4 (SM89) | 0.29.0 | B | 61.2 | 79.7 | **0.768** | **3.73%** |
| L4 (SM89) | 0.30.0 | C | 82.8 | 81.6 | **1.014** | 0.99% |
| L4 (SM89) | 0.30.0 | D | 78.2 | 77.0 | **1.017** | 1.61% |
| A10 (SM86) | 0.29.0 | E | 132.6 | 138.3 | 0.959 | 2.08% |

Each ratio is the default arm divided by the eager arm measured in the same container, so session and card effects cancel. On 0.29.0/L4 the CUDA-graph path runs at 49% and 77% of the eager path; on 0.30.0 it reaches parity. Acceptance length is flat throughout (tau 4.11-4.15), so this is throughput rather than a change in what the drafter gets accepted.

### Misc discussion on performance

Two observations, one related issue, and a question.

**1. The CUDA-graph fallback still fires on 0.30.0.** I had assumed the improvement was the speculative path gaining full graphs. It is not. The warning is byte-identical on both versions and capture proceeds under PIECEWISE in each:

> CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE is not supported with spec-decode for attention backend FlashInferBackend (support: AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE); setting cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE

Backend selection is unchanged too: both versions log FLASHINFER for the target and FLASH_ATTN for the second selection. So neither graph mode nor backend choice explains the difference.

**2. On 0.29.0 the dispersion magnitude is itself not reproducible.** Two twelve-boot measurements of the identical configuration gave CV 13.92% and 3.73%, with means 39.2 and 61.2 tok/s. The effect is present in both; its size is not a property of the configuration. The eager arm is stable across every session measured (80.5, 79.7, 81.6, 77.0 on L4; 138.3 on A10), which is what makes it usable as a control.

**Related, but I do not think it is the same thing: #58677.** That reports the draft model's torch.compile cache identity flipping between exactly two values across restarts with byte-identical argv, attributed to the shared VllmConfig being mutated in-place during the main model's warmup and CUDA-

issues.title: [Bug]: --disable-custom-all-reduce says it falls back to NCCL, but FlashInfer and symm-mem all-reduce stay enabled
issues.body:
### Your current environment

```text
vLLM 0.30.0 (official vllm/vllm-openai image), torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer-python 0.6.18.post1, NCCL 2.30.7
2x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (SXM, NV18), driver 580.126.09, CUDA 13.0, Ubuntu 24.04
collect_env.py was not captured on that run. The code references are unchanged on main 138810056 (2026-10-04).
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`--disable-custom-all-reduce` is documented as "Disable the custom all-reduce kernel and fall back to NCCL." ([`ParallelConfig.disable_custom_all_reduce`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0cbac6cd1305f710e12193596b27488397bcb205/vllm/config/parallel.py#L221-L222); the same text is the `--help` entry). On H100 it doesn't fall back to NCCL: the flag turns off only the `CUSTOM` backend, and the TP group keeps using FlashInfer and torch symmetric-memory all-reduce.

In [`CudaCommunicator.__init__`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0cbac6cd1305f710e12193596b27488397bcb205/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/cuda_communicator.py#L61-L66) the flag only reaches `use_custom_allreduce` (through `_ENABLE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE`). `use_flashinfer_allreduce` and `use_torch_symm_mem` are gated by `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER` and `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM` alone, and both default to 1 (FlashInfer since #52998).

Startup line `Using [...] all-reduce backends (in dispatch order) for group 'tp:0'` on 2x H100 SXM, TP=2, vLLM 0.30.0:

| Settings | Backends |
|---|---|
| default | `['FLASHINFER', 'CUSTOM', 'SYMM_MEM', 'PYNCCL']` |
| `--disable-custom-all-reduce` | `['FLASHINFER', 'SYMM_MEM', 'PYNCCL']` |
| `--disable-custom-all-reduce` + `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0` + `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0` | `['PYNCCL']` |

So getting NCCL only takes the flag plus two env vars. This applies where FlashInfer all-reduce and symm-mem are supported (SM 9.0 / 10.x). On other GPUs, e.g. SM120, the flag does end up NCCL-only.

This matters because the flag is the usual "rule out vLLM's own collectives" switch when debugging hangs and crashes (e.g. #53894, #56180). Someone who sets it on Hopper or Blackwell to rule out a FlashInfer all-reduce problem still has FlashInfer all-reduce running.

Is this intended? Two ways to make it consistent, and I'm happy to send a PR for whichever you prefer:

1. Keep the behavior and fix the docstring: the flag disables only vLLM's custom all-reduce kernel, and NCCL-only additionally needs `VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=0 VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0`.
2. Make the flag do what it says: when it is set, also skip FlashInfer and symm-mem all-reduce for the TP group.

I searched existing issues and PRs and found nothing about this.

I traced the code with help from Claude Code, which also ran the checks on my machines. The logs and numbers above come from those runs.

issues.title: [RFC] Weight Reload Correctness for RL
issues.body:
**Related RFCs:** [#54477](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54477) (reload refactor), [#45585](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45585) (RL CI roadmap), [#48310](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48310) (sleep/wake correctness), [#48305](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48305) (training-inference consistency), and [#48478](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48478) (production fail-closed storage contract for category 1).

## Problem

Weight reload must produce correct inference output for all model architectures and parallelism configurations. The cases below span vLLM and downstream RL integrations.

This RFC classifies failures by root cause rather than symptom. A single bug may violate more than one invariant, but each item is tracked under its primary category. Repeated layerwise copy-back, post-load, and completion failures motivate the direct-mode refactor in [#54477](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54477); that refactor must satisfy the invariants here rather than replace their acceptance tests.

## Scope

In scope: model/adapter weight load and reload, post-load transformations, reload state restoration, parameter routing, weight-name resolution, and cache invalidation caused by a model or adapter update.

This tracker owns the update half of the complete RL transition:

```text
pause/drain -> sleep -> wake(weights) -> reload/update -> post-load/finalize
            -> wake(kv_cache) -> invalidate versioned caches -> resume
```

The sleep/wake half is tracked in #48310. A successful RL update must satisfy both RFCs; HTTP success alone is not a correctness oracle.

## Failure taxonomy

| # | Category | Required invariant | Minimum regression check |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Storage identity | A tensor address captured by CUDA/HIP Graph or retained by a backend must not change across reload | capture → reload → pointer check → allocation pressure → replay |
| 2 | Runtime value refresh | Every runtime-derived tensor must be recomputed from the new source weight and refreshed in place | load A → post-load → load B → post-load → check derived values/output |
| 3 | Loader lifecycle | A weight loader must remain valid for the parameter's current layout and lifecycle phase; accounting must finalize each layer exactly once and only after every required tensor arrives | load A → layout/kernel setup → load B; vary transfer order/chunking and check exact completion accounting |
| 4 | Reload state preservation | Parameters, buffers, configuration, and backend state required by forward must survive or be rebuilt correctly | compare cold load with warm reload across all runtime state |

issues.title: [Bug]: OffloadingConnector with LHBNC returns wrong output on CPU hits
issues.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.30.0 (ced6857), torch 2.13.0+cu129, NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe, driver 575.51.03. The code below is unchanged on main (0c16eee).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC` and the native CPU offload, a request whose prefix is loaded back from the CPU tier produces wrong output. There is no error or warning, and the blocks are counted as stored and as hits.

`register_kv_caches` builds a `(num_blocks, page)` view per layer with the layer's block stride, and treats any layer whose block stride differs from its page size as a packed layout:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0c16eee3f1ff777298cc894c3eeb85f3880c6d6a/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/worker.py#L104-L111

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0c16eee3f1ff777298cc894c3eeb85f3880c6d6a/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/worker.py#L133-L163

The comments assume a packed layout (DSv4) has block stride > page. LHBNC is the opposite case: the heads of one block sit a whole layer of blocks apart, so the block stride is `N*C` while the page is `H*N*C`. The packed branch then offloads `block_stride` bytes per block, which is head 0 of layer 0. (Before #51718 the packed case came from `is_kv_cache_tensor_packed`, not from this stride comparison.)

Repro (A100, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B: 48 layers, 8 KV heads, block 16):

```bash
VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B \
  --kv-offloading-size 30 --kv-offloading-backend native \
  --num-gpu-blocks-override 4500 --max-model-len 71936 --enforce-eager
```

1. Send a 7,060-token prompt at temperature 0. The prompt repeats a sentence about Gutenberg and ends with "Who combined movable metal type with a screw press, and around which year?".
2. Send a 71,900-token prompt so the first prompt is evicted from the GPU cache.
3. Send the first prompt again; its prefix is loaded from the CPU tier.

| | LBNHC | LHBNC |
|---|---|---|
| step 1 output | ` Johannes Gutenberg combined movable metal type with a screw press around 1440.` | same |
| step 3 output | same as step 1 | ` _140140101010101010101010101401` |
| GPU→CPU bytes for a 64K-token prompt (`vllm:kv_offload_total_bytes_total`) | 12.9 GB | 33.5 MB (1/384 = 1/(48 layers × 8 heads)) |

Expected: offload the whole page, or reject the layout at startup. `OffloadingConnector` prefers LBHNC, so only an explicit `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC` reaches this path.

Supporting LHBNC here is possible by offloading each (block, layer, head) slice separately, the way the offload handler used to split K/V-first caches (`kv_dim_before_num_blocks`), or more generally by letting connectors tell layout resolution which layouts they can handle. For now I propose failing at startup with a clear error, and I will open a PR for that. If the design discussion picks this up later, I am happy to help; feel free to ping me.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issues.title: [Performance]: FlashAttention backend rebuilds KV-cache views on every call (+~21 µs CPU/layer since #44455)
issues.body:
### Proposal to improve performance

Cache the (canonicalized) views on the impl and reuse them while the same `kv_cache` tensor is passed in. On v0.30, a local patch doing this cuts TTFT p50 by 12–16%, and the outputs match an fp32 reference with no numerical change:


```python
# FlashAttentionImpl
def _get_kv_views(self, kv_cache, canonicalize: bool):
    c = self._kv_view_cache
    if c is None or c[0] is not kv_cache:
        k, v = kv_cache.transpose(1, 2).split(self.head_size, dim=-1)
        ck, cv = canonicalize_singleton_dim_strides(k), canonicalize_singleton_dim_strides(v)
        c = self._kv_view_cache = (kv_cache, k, v, ck, cv)
    return (c[3], c[4]) if canonicalize else (c[1], c[2])
```

Notes:
- The identity check matters. `profile_cudagraph_memory` first binds a minimal KV cache (`_init_minimal_kv_cache_for_profiling`), runs attention on it, frees it, and then allocates the real one. A cache keyed only on the first call would keep pointing at freed memory.
- There is precedent for this: `TritonAttentionImpl` already caches KV-scale views in `_k_scale_cache` / `_v_scale_cache` ([triton_attn.py#L383-L440](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py#L383-L440)), and `_cleanup_profiling_kv_cache` clears them. The FA view cache could be cleared in the same place. It should also be kept per impl, not in a module-level dict, so that the replaced tensor is not kept alive.
- Hybrid models (e.g. Qwen3.5) only get this cost on their `full_attention` layers.

I'm happy to open a PR.


### Report of performance regression

Since #44455 (KV-cache layout refactor, v0.26), `FlashAttentionImpl` derives the K/V cache views on every call:

- `forward`: `kv_cache.transpose(1, 2).split(self.head_size, dim=-1)`, then `canonicalize_singleton_dim_strides` on both views ([flash_attn.py#L1232-L1250 @ v0.30.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py#L1232-L1250))
- `do_kv_cache_update`: the same `transpose(1, 2).split(...)` ([flash_attn.py#L1454 @ v0.30.0](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py#L1454))

Before #44455 this was a single `kv_cache.unbind(1)` ([v0.25.0#L816](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.25.0/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py#L816)). The code is unchanged on current `main`.

These views depend only on the per-layer `kv_cache` tensor's storage, shape and strides. That tensor is fixed once the KV cache is allocated. The views are recomputed per layer per step anyway, and the slots each step touches come in separately via `slot_mapping` / `block_table`.

Under the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, attention for prefill / mixed batches runs eagerly, so this is host time on the critical path for short prefills.

| per attention call (profiler, H100) | v0.25 | v0.26 |
|---|---|---|
| K/V view ops | `unbind` + 2× `select`: 11.6 µs | `transpose` + `split` + 2× `narrow`: 17.0 µs |
| `unified_attention_with_output` total | 134.1 µs | 155.2 µs (+21) |

For a 64-layer model that is about +1.35 ms per prefill step. On 8×H100 (TP=8), with short prompts and `max_tokens=1`, TTFT p50 went up 1–3.5 ms from 0.25 to 0.26. Only the FA backend is affected; FlashInfer is not.


### Misc discussion on performance

_No response_

### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary)

```text
vLLM 0.30.0 (vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0), torch 2.13.0+cu130
8x H100 80GB (TP=8), attention backe

issues.title: [Bug]: With --api-server-count > 1, gauges such as vllm:num_requests_running have no samples until the first request
issues.body:
### Your current environment

```text
vLLM 0.30.1rc1.dev641+g7867d6c52 (nightly wheel of main), torch 2.13.0+cu132, prometheus_client 0.26.0
1x NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada, driver 580.178.04, Ubuntu 24.04
Also seen on vLLM 0.30.0 (official image) with 2x H100 SXM, TP=2 and DP=2.
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With one API server, `/metrics` reports `vllm:num_requests_running`, `vllm:num_requests_waiting` and `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc` as 0 right after startup. With `--api-server-count 2`, the same scrape on an idle server has the `# TYPE ... gauge` lines but no samples. The samples only appear after the first request.

`vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enforce-eager`, scraped once while idle and once after one greedy request (vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev641+g7867d6c52`, RTX 6000 Ada, prometheus_client 0.26.0). Number of samples for `num_requests_running` / `num_requests_waiting` / `kv_cache_usage_perc`:

| `--api-server-count` | idle: samples | after one request: samples |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 / 1 / 1 (all 0.0) | 1 / 1 / 1 |
| 2 | **0 / 0 / 0** | 1 / 1 / 1 (all 0.0) |

To reproduce:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enforce-eager --api-server-count 2 --port 8100
# idle: the TYPE line is there, but there is no sample
curl -s localhost:8100/metrics | grep -A1 '^# TYPE vllm:num_requests_running'
curl -s localhost:8100/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "prompt": "Hello", "max_tokens": 8, "temperature": 0}'
# after one request: the sample appears
curl -s localhost:8100/metrics | grep '^vllm:num_requests_running'
```

I first hit this on 0.30.0 with TP=2 and with DP=2 on 2x H100. A poller that required `vllm:num_requests_running` failed on its first scrape because the series did not exist yet.

Cause: these gauges use `multiprocess_mode="mostrecent"` (`kv_cache_usage_perc` since #28792). In multiprocess mode, prometheus_client keeps the sample with the newest timestamp for each series. A child that was created but never set has timestamp 0 and is dropped, while `all` and `livesum` export it as 0. vLLM only sets these gauges when scheduler stats arrive, so an idle multi-API-server deployment exports nothing for them.

Impact: dashboards, alerts and autoscalers (for example, scaling on `vllm:num_requests_waiting`) see "no data" instead of 0 on an idle deployment, and anything that requires the series fails until traffic arrives.

Possible fix: set these gauges to 0 when `PrometheusStatLogger` creates them. That writes a timestamp, so idle multi-API-server deployments report 0 like single-server ones; single-process mode doesn't change. I can send a PR if that sounds right.

I searched existing issues and PRs and found nothing about this. Related: #28792 (added `mostrecent` to `kv_cache_usage_perc`).

I traced the code with help from Claude Code, which also ran the checks on my machines. The logs and numbers above come from those runs.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

When serving QWEN2-2B with vLLM on AWS SageMaker (g6e.xlarge, 32GB RAM), we see persistent CPU RAM growth leading to container restarts during normal inference workloads. This occurs regardless of cache configuration (--mm-processor-cache-type SHM/LRU, with default or custom --mm-processor-cache-gb, and with cache entirely disabled).

* RAM Usage: Memory usage increases steadily with requests (seen with both 4GB and 8GB cache values) and RAM is not freed post-inference.
* Container Restarts: Endpoint server restarts around 60–65% total RAM consumed.
* Model Choice: Reproduced with QWEN2-2B (multimodal enabled) and text-only pipelines.
* vLLM Version: We are using the latest stable release.

Expected:
RAM usage should remain stable or return to baseline when requests complete and cache limits are not reached.


Prior Investigation:

Searched and reviewed existing issues ([example issues #12973, #15085, #8629](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues?q=memory+leak)).

The problem appears to affect small models and different cache modes (SHM, LRU, etc.).

Occurs even with mm_processor_cache_gb set to minimal values.

issues.title: [Bug]: FlashInfer with LHBNC on A100 asserts at startup
issues.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.30.0 (ced6857), torch 2.13.0+cu129, flashinfer-python 0.6.18.post1, NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe, driver 575.51.03. The code below is unchanged on main (1388100).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On GPUs other than SM100, `FlashInferBackend.supported_kv_cache_layouts()` returns `None` ("any layout"), so layout resolution accepts LHBNC:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/138810056093301f4881050fcf2b1786939da387/vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py#L547-L553

FlashInfer only addresses NHD/HND pages, and `get_flashinfer_layout_string` has no LHBNC entry. Its assert message assumes the backend already rejected LHBNC:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/138810056093301f4881050fcf2b1786939da387/vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py#L175-L190

Repro on A100:

```bash
VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=LHBNC vllm serve meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER --enforce-eager
```

```text
INFO [utils.py:320] Using LHBNC KV cache layout.
ERROR [core.py:1366] AssertionError: KV cache layout LHBNC has no FlashInfer equivalent; FlashInfer rejects it in supported_kv_cache_layouts
```

Expected: resolution rejects LHBNC up front with the list of valid layouts, as it does for backends that declare their set. The other five layouts run fine with FlashInfer on A100. I have a small fix (declare those five on non-SM100) and will open a PR.

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issues.title: [RFC]: MoRIIO WRITE failure handling and safe KV block reclamation
issues.body:
### Motivation.

MoRIIO WRITE can leave decode requests waiting with KV blocks allocated when the producer disappears (#59114). A receive timeout should fail the request, but should not by itself authorize block reuse. This RFC proposes using the scheduler's existing delayed-free path to separate request failure from eventual block release, and asks what event can safely authorize that release when no completion arrives.

In #59114, I reproduced the failure three times with four requests per run. After killing the prefill instance, clients timed out after approximately 400 seconds. Decode KV usage remained at 11.0998%, above its idle baseline, for another 295–388 seconds.

This shows failure to recover during the observation window. Block ownership was not traced, so it does not establish a permanent leak, a specific leaked block count, whether writes remained in flight, or whether late writes corrupted reused blocks.

The correctness concern is separate from that observation: a timeout tells D to stop waiting, but does not establish that the old transfer can no longer write its destination.

The initial scope is MoRIIO WRITE. Transparent retry, broader P/D failover, READ-mode changes, and connector-wide redesign are out of scope.

### Proposed Change.

Keep request failure and authorization to reuse blocks separate.

#### Receive lifetime

Pending receive tracking should remain independent of the client request. Client abort or disconnect should not discard the mapping or disable tracking for an unfinished receive.

The receive-wait watchdog should be disarmed when the receive completes, not when the request finishes. A request that has received its KV and is still decoding should no longer be subject to it.

A timeout should be reported once for a live request. If the client has already cancelled, cleanup should continue without producing another terminal outcome. Internal receive/block tracking should remain until safe termination or verified recovery.

Timeout detection and cleanup should continue after client disconnect and without new traffic.

#### Lifecycle and ownership

In `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, `finish_requests()` can already make a `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` request terminal while `delay_free_blocks` keeps its blocks allocated. I propose using that path as the starting point rather than introducing connector-owned block allocation.

On timeout, the request should reach an error/terminal path while block release remains delayed. Receive/block tracking should remain available for later completion or recovery. Reporting request failure must not itself authorize block reuse.

There are three separate questions:

- **Request fate:** whether the request is still waiting or has failed/cancelled. Later transfer events must not revive a terminal request.
- **Transfer safety:** whether the old transfer can still write the affected blocks. Timeout, cancellation, and request failure do not establish safe termination.
- **KV validity and allocation:** whether the received KV is usable for decode and when its blocks may be reused. Safe termination does not make partial or failed KV valid.

The connector interface allows a failed receive to report load errors together with `finished_recving`, so `finished_recving` does not necessarily mean that KV transfer succeeded. However, processing it may allow the scheduler to release blocks.

For retained blocks, `finished_recving` or another release-authorizing scheduler input should not

issues.title: [Bug]: On RDNA (gfx12), VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 force-selects ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN at priority 0, ignoring VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTENTION (kernel exceeds RDNA's LDS limit)
issues.body:
### Summary

On RDNA (gfx12 / RDNA4), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` unconditionally forces `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` to the **front** of the attention backend priority list. The environment variable documented to control that backend, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTENTION` (default `False`), is never consulted on this path, so there is no supported way to use aiter's linear/GEMM kernels on RDNA while avoiding its unified-attention kernel.

That matters because on RDNA that kernel does not fit in LDS: it requests **65792 bytes against a 65536 byte limit**, which takes the engine down (ROCm/aiter#5229).

### Where

`vllm/platforms/rocm.py` (current `main`, lines 489-491):

```python
    if is_aiter_found_and_supported():
        backends.append(AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN)
    elif rocm_aiter_ops.is_rdna_aiter_enabled():
        backends.insert(0, AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN)   # <-- priority 0, unconditional
```

`vllm/_aiter_ops.py` (current `main`, line 1877):

```python
    def is_rdna_aiter_enabled(cls) -> bool:
        ...
        return on_rdna4() and cls._AITER_ENABLED      # <-- never checks _TRITON_UNIFIED_ATTN_ENABLED
```

`_TRITON_UNIFIED_ATTN_ENABLED = envs.VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTENTION` **is** defined and defaults to `False`; it is simply not used to gate this backend on the RDNA branch. Note the gfx9 branch `append`s while the RDNA branch `insert(0, ...)`s, so on RDNA the backend is not merely available, it outranks `ROCM_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN`.

`VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN` does **not** work around this — the selector still picks the aiter backend. The only escape is disabling aiter entirely.

### Reproduction

2x AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), ROCm 7.14 wheel stack, torch 2.12.0+rocm7.14.0, `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` (hybrid GDN + MoE), TP=2, `--enforce-eager`.

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTENTION=0    # ignored on RDNA
export VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN         # also ignored
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --model Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 16384 --enforce-eager
```

Log shows the backend selected anyway:

```
Overriding with ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN out of potential backends:
  ['ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN', 'ROCM_ATTN', 'TRITON_ATTN']
Using aiter unified attention for RocmAiterUnifiedAttentionImpl
```

A single short request succeeds. Any request that needs the split-KV 3d path (concurrency, or a long prompt) then kills the engine:

```
triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: shared memory,
Required: 65792, Hardware limit: 65536.
  File "aiter/ops/triton/attention/unified_attention.py", line 603, in unified_attention
    kernel_unified_attention_3d[...]
vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
```

The "one short request works" behaviour is why this is easy to miss in smoke tests.

### Proposed fix

Honour the documented flag on the RDNA path. Two small changes:

```python

    def is_rdna_unified_attn_enabled(cls) -> bool:
        """RDNA4 (gfx12): aiter Triton unified attention. Unlike the other rdna

        kernel can be avoided without giving up aiter's linear GEMM."""
        return cls.is_rdna_aiter_enabled() and cls._TRITON_UNIFIED_ATTN_ENABLED

issues.title: [Question][ROCm] GLM-5.3-Flash kpool indexer: does the 640-token block table reach 32-pool pages on gfx942/gfx950 too?
issues.body:
We found this on hardware vLLM doesn't support (gfx1030, Radeon Pro V620), running GLM-5.3-Flash without aiter. The code path involved is shared with gfx942/gfx950, and we have no MI300/MI355 to check it on. Could someone with one confirm or rule it out?

**What we see.** `Glm5NextIndexerCache` stores pooled keys in pages of 32 pools (storage block 128 tokens at `index_kpool=4`). The hybrid KDA page rule makes the attention block 640. On ROCm the sparse-MLA and indexer backends accept `MultipleOf(16)` (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`), so `select_common_block_size` keeps kernel block 640. The indexer metadata builder only converts the table when the storage block is a multiple of the kernel block (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`, prefill and decode branches; unchanged on main):

```python
if (
    kernel_block_size is not None
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size != kernel_block_size
    and self.kv_cache_spec.block_size % kernel_block_size == 0
):
    factor = self.kv_cache_spec.block_size // kernel_block_size
    indexer_block_table = (block_table[:, ::factor] // factor).contiguous()
```

128 % 640 ≠ 0, so the 640-token table goes to `get_compressed_slot_mapping` (the kpool writer) and to `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache_triton` as if each entry named one 32-pool page. With per-chunk block allocation:
- pools written before their block exists land in padding;
- positions past the allocated blocks alias block 0;
- positions past the 52-column table (at `max_model_len` 32768) are masked by the gather.

On NVIDIA the kernel block is 64, so the `// factor` branch applies. As far as we can tell nothing here is aiter-specific: the kpool path uses `forward_cuda` on ROCm whether aiter is on or off.

**Reproducer.** One GPU, stock vLLM only, no model: [`repro_rocm_kpool_table.py`](https://github.com/Omnicef/vllm/blob/glm53-v030/tests/local/repro_rocm_kpool_table.py). It writes a 9,432-token prompt in the served prefill chunks with the real ROCm kpool writer and slot mapping, gathers it back with the real gather, and compares against the writer's own output. The two arms are the table as the builder produces it and a page-granular table (block `b` → pages `5b … 5b+4`). On gfx1030, identical over two runs:

```
table as the builder produces it  : ooo000000000000xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm  (3/74 pages correct)
page-granular table               : oooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo  (74/74 pages correct)
```

(`o` correct, `0` all-zero, `x` wrong keys, `m` masked.) Above `index_topk`, where the indexer actually selects, this breaks long-context retrieval: a two-fact needle at ~9k tokens failed for us until the table was expanded. If it reproduces on MI300, the fix we use expands each kernel-block id into its storage pages when the kernel block is a multiple of the storage block (about 20 lines in the builder, happy to send).

**Secondary note (tile order).** With aiter off (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset), the decode logits fall back to `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch`. It reads each page token-major, while two ROCm writers store values in 16×16 tiles when `block_size > 1`: `indexer_k_quant_and_cache_triton` and the GLM-5.3 kpool writer. DeepSeek-V4's C4A compressor (`compress_norm_rope_store_triton`) writes token-major, so its pages are unaffected. See the correction on #51555 for numbers. aiter's reader passes `Preshuffle=block_size > 1` and isn't affected.

issues.title: [Docs] Document NIXL KV connector metrics aggregation semantics
issues.body:
## Summary

The NIXL KV connector logs transfer metrics periodically:

```
KV Transfer metrics: Num successful transfers=4, Avg xfer time (ms)=1.381, P90 xfer time (ms)=2.601, Avg post time (ms)=0.672, P90 post time (ms)=0.801, Avg MB per transfer=2.25, Throughput (MB/s)=1629.549, Avg number of descriptors=72.0
```

Currently there is no documentation explaining what these metrics represent, especially in the context of **multi-rank (TP > 1) deployments**. This has already caused confusion among users.

## Current behavior

All metrics are **aggregated across all TP ranks** before summary stats are computed:

1. Each TP rank independently records per-transfer telemetry (`transfer_duration`, `post_duration`, `bytes_transferred`, `num_descriptors`) via `NixlKVConnectorStats.record_transfer()` in [`stats.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/stats.py).
2. Stats from all ranks are concatenated via `aggregate()` (`list.extend()`).
3. `reduce()` computes averages, percentiles, and throughput over the **combined** pool of observations from all ranks.

This means:
- **"Num successful transfers"** is the total count across all ranks, not per-rank.
- **"Avg MB per transfer"** is the average over all individual rank-level transfers, not the total bytes moved for a single KV cache transfer operation.
- **"Throughput (MB/s)"** is `total_MB_all_ranks / total_time_all_ranks` — effectively an average per-rank throughput, not the aggregate system throughput.
- **Percentiles (P90)** are computed over the combined distribution of all ranks' transfer times.

This is unintuitive because users may expect metrics to reflect per-engine totals or aggregate system throughput.

## What needs to be documented

1. **Docstrings in `stats.py`**: Add clear documentation to `NixlKVConnectorStats` explaining that stats are aggregated across all TP ranks and what each metric represents in that context.
2. **Inline comments in `reduce()`**: Clarify the semantics of throughput and averages — that they are per-rank averages over the combined observation pool.
3. **Docstrings in `metrics.py`**: Document the `observe()` → `aggregate()` → `reduce()` → `log()` pipeline and the fact that stats arrive pre-aggregated across workers.
4. **(Optional) Docs page**: Add a section to the disaggregated serving documentation explaining how to interpret the KV Transfer metrics log line.

## Relevant files

- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/stats.py` — `NixlKVConnectorStats` (recording, aggregation, reduction)
- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/metrics.py` — `KVConnectorLogging` (observe/log pipeline), `KVConnectorStats` (base class)

## Context

See related discussion: metrics are aggregated across ranks rather than reported per-rank or per-engine. This is a deliberate design choice (fire-and-forget from workers), but it needs to be clearly documented so users can correctly interpret the numbers.

issues.title: Upgrade to Transformers v5
issues.body:
## What is this issue?

This issue serves as a living tracker for the current issues preventing us from upgrading vLLM to Transformers v5.

We will use sub-issues to track individual failures and PRs should be made against these sub-issues.

The solutions to these issues may need to be applied to either:

- Transformers in the form of:
  - Adding missing backward compatibility (usually for custom code models)
  - General bug fixes/improvements to new features of v5
- vLLM in the form of:
  - Forward compatibility with how something is now done in v5
  - Edge case handling for issues that v4 ignored (such as config validation)

Sometimes, the issue is simply with the model checkpoint itself, for example if it:

- Contains a malformed `config.json` that cannot be used to instantiate the newly input validated `PreTrainedConfig` class
- Custom code* uses deprecated/removed APIs

In these situations, the best solution will likely be to skip these tests in vLLM and open a PR to Transformers to contribute this model. This will be faster and more sustainable than waiting for the model vendor to fix their custom model code, sometimes they nevert do.

Contributing the new model should be done using the new [Modular Transformers](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/modular_transformers) so that the implementation is easy to maintain and will remain maintained by the Transformers team.

_*particularly in the parts of the model implementation that vLLM tries to directly reuse, such as config/tokenizer/multimodal processor_

issues.title: [Bug]: Wrong timestamps if audio > 30s
issues.body:
### Your current environment


NA

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Segment level timestamps are incrementally offset by ~0.5s per segment.**

When transcribing long audio with vLLM Whisper, segment-level timestamps are increasingly inaccurate. Chunking uses by default a 1s window to find low-energy (quiet) regions for splitting, so the next chunk may start up to 1s earlier than the nominal chunk length. This offset is not compensated for when generating segment timestamps, resulting in an average delay of ~0.5s per segment, which accumulates (e.g., 5s after 10 segments).

Clients can workaround by subtracting 0.5s per segment, but that's obviously not accurate.

Also, the [related documentation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e83b7e379c11bf136c1b96bc6a67b6d2207cfde4/docs/contributing/model/transcription.md#audio-preprocessing-and-chunking) is not correct: there are no overlapping chunks, but just a window for searching the best split point. Maybe this confusion is the cause of the issue.

issues.title: [RFC]: Support ViT Full CUDA Graph (Tracker)
issues.body:
### Motivation.

Multimodal large language models (e.g., Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5, GLM-V, Kimi K2.5) rely on a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder to process visual inputs before feeding them into the language model backbone. In production serving scenarios, the ViT forward pass involves launching a large number of small CUDA kernels — including patch embedding, layer normalization, multi-head self-attention, and MLP projections — each of which incurs non-trivial kernel launch overhead on the host side.

Currently, vLLM supports CUDA graph capture for the decoder (LLM) portion of the model, which has proven effective at reducing kernel launch costs and improving throughput. However, the ViT encoder is still executed eagerly, meaning every forward pass re-launches all kernels from scratch. Extending full CUDA graph support to the ViT encoder would allow the entire encoder forward pass to be captured and replayed as a single graph, eliminating per-kernel launch overhead and enabling more consistent, low-latency inference for multimodal models.

issues.title: [Performance] Measure Transformers backend startup time vs native
issues.body:
This comes from an old comment and was never backed by measurements, so the first
task is to establish whether the effect is real at all. It may not be.

Runtime throughput was brought in line with native implementations in #47187, but
nobody has measured startup time either before or since.

### Step 1: is there a difference?

Time engine init for a model that has both implementations, e.g.:

    vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --model-impl transformers
    vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --model-impl vllm

Compare time-to-ready across a few runs and a couple of model sizes. Warm vs cold
HF cache matters, so control for it.

If there is no meaningful difference, say so and close this issue. That is a
perfectly good outcome and still worth having measured.

### Step 2: only if a delta shows up

The backend does some work at load time that native implementations do not, so
these are plausible starting points rather than known causes:

- `fuser.py` — `get_fuser` traces each module class with `fx` to match it against
  the available fusers. Cached per class, but tracing is not free.
- `base.py` — `recursive_replace` walks the module tree applying fusers per instance.
- Config resolution and `auto_map` handling for remote-code models.

A profile of init (py-spy or cProfile) will be more informative than guessing from
this list.

### Done when

Either the startup delta is quantified and explained, or it is shown that there
isn't a meaningful one and this is closed.

issues.title: [RFC]: Limit the use of envvars in vLLM
issues.body:
### Motivation.

vLLM's envvars are on the edge of getting out of control. There are many envvars should instead be configs. Like the attention backend, all2all kernel backend, and even there is a flag to control KV cache layout. envvars are evil because:

1. It is equivalent of using global variables everywhere in the code, which is a bad programming practice.
2. envvars have no advanced structure like, hierarchy, typechecks, etc. 

In summary, I think envvars are the kind of thing that is very easy to add so people tend to add envvars as the shortest path to implement their feature, but this can quickly becomes unmanageable and makes the project very hard to use. 

### Proposed Change.

I think we should:

1. Spend some effort on reviewing the current envvars and move many of them to configs.
2. Have very strict bar on what can be an envvar and question every new envvars in vllm.
