issues.title: v0.7.1 release highlights draft
issues.body:
### v0.7.1 Highlights

FlashInfer v0.7.1 expands Kimi K3 inference support, expert-parallel MoE execution, and linear-attention backends. It also adds reusable MLA execution plans and explicit NVFP4 quantization recipes for serving integrations.

**Kimi K3 adds packed speculative decoding and NVFP4 SiTU experts**

Kimi K3 integrations can use `packed_fused_kda_decode` on Blackwell SM10x to fuse short convolution, Kimi Delta Attention, and gated RMS normalization during speculative verification. The API supports ragged batches, accepted-token cache updates, CUDA Graph capture, and FP32 or BF16 recurrent state. NVFP4 MegaMoE also supports Kimi K3's SiTU activation on Blackwell.

- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4809
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5503
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5455

**Expert-parallel MoE expands to more quantized configurations**

Rubin SM107 supports NVFP4 and MXFP8 MegaMoE through `MoEEpLayer`, with BF16 combine and output. Blackwell SM120/SM121 W4A16 fused MoE supports expert sharding through `expert_map`, with the caller distributing the full batch and summing per-rank outputs. The split MoE layer supports CUDA Graph capture with both NCCL-EP and NIXL-EP through persistent graph state.

- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5384
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4302
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5287

**Linear-attention prefill gains a cuDNN backend**

Gated DeltaNet and Kimi Delta Attention prefill can explicitly select `backend="cudnn"`, using cuDNN's fused linear-attention engines on supported configurations. New entry points also expose Gated Delta Product and Gated Delta Rule 2. The Kimi Delta Attention backend supports ordinary multi-token prefill; speculative verification uses the packed decode API described above.

- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4968

**MLA integrations can reuse plans across more backends**

`BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper` supports planned execution with TRTLLM-GEN, XQA, and monolithic or modular CuTe DSL backends. Backend executables and persistent state are prepared in `plan()` and reused in `run()`, giving integrations a shared lifecycle for repeated execution and CUDA Graph capture.

- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5070

**NVFP4 recipes can be configured per model**

NVFP4 quantization APIs accept an explicit `NVFP44Over6Config`, allowing models in one process to use different 4over6 recipes. The unified MoE `QuantConfig` carries the same setting for supporting runners, including the CuTe DSL per-token path. Backend support is checked when an explicit recipe is requested.

- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5152

issues.title: DGX Spark (SM121) Current Support Audit
issues.body:
# FlashInfer — DGX Spark (SM121) Current Support Audit

**Date:** 2026-04-24
**Scope:** Audit of SM121 (compute capability 12.1, DGX Spark) support across FlashInfer ops, APIs, backends, and testing.
**Goal:** Improve Spark usability on FlashInfer by identifying existing gaps.

**Note: skip to "15. Consolidated Action Items" for TLDR.**

---

## Architecture Context

| Gencode | Target | CUDA Requirement |
|---------|--------|------------------|
| `compute_120a` / `sm_120a` | RTX 5090 (SM120) | CUDA 12.8 |
| `compute_120f` / `sm_120f` | SM12x family (120 + 121) | CUDA 12.9 |
| `compute_121a` / `sm_121a` | DGX Spark (SM121) | CUDA 12.9 |

### SM120 vs SM121: Implications for FlashInfer

Per the [CUDA 13.2 Programming Guide — Compute Capabilities](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html) (Tables 29–33), SM120 and SM121 share a single "12.x" spec column: identical shared memory (99 KB/block, 100 KB/SM), warps (48/SM), registers (64K/SM), tensor core data types (TF32, BF16, FP16, FP8, FP6, FP4, INT8), TMA, and cluster support. [Table 28](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html#compute-capabilities-family-specific-compatibility) confirms `compute_120f` is compatible with **both** CC 12.0 and 12.1. The chip-level differences (SM121 = aarch64 host, unified LPDDR5x, 84 SMs vs SM120's x86_64, discrete GDDR7, up to 170 SMs) do not affect kernel correctness — only SM-count-based heuristics and host toolchain.

### `f` vs `a` compilation targets: performance implications

Per the [PTX ISA 9.3](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html) (§9.7.15.5.14 for dense `mma`, §9.7.15.6.3 for sparse `mma.sp`), `120f` (family) is a subset of `120a`/`121a` (arch-specific). Most SM12x features — including **dense** NVFP4/MXFP4 block-scaled MMA — are family-specific and available via `120f` from PTX ISA 8.8. The arch-specific restriction (requiring `sm_120a`/`sm_121a`) applies **only to sparse MMA** (`mma.sp`) with `.kind::mxf4nvf4`/`.kind::mxf4`:

| PTX Feature | `compute_120` (baseline) | `compute_120f` (family) | `compute_120a` / `compute_121a` (arch) |
|-------------|--------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| FP4/FP6/FP8 conversions (`cvt`) | No | Yes | Yes |
| FP4/FP6 MMA, block-scaled MMA (`.kind::mxf8f6f4`) | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Dense** NVFP4 MMA (`.kind::mxf4nvf4`) | No | **Yes** (PTX ISA ≥ 8.8) | **Yes** |
| **Dense** MXFP4 MMA (`.kind::mxf4`) | No | **Yes** (PTX ISA ≥ 8.8) | **Yes** |
| **Sparse** NVFP4 MMA (`mma.sp` `.kind::mxf4nvf4`) | No | **No** | **Yes** |
| **Sparse** MXFP4 MMA (`mma.sp` `.kind::mxf4`) | No | **No** | **Yes** |

FlashInfer's b12x GEMM kernel (`dense_blockscaled_gemm_sm120_b12x.py`) uses `cute.nvgpu.warp.MmaMXF4NVF4Op` — a **dense** block-scaled MMA atom. This means `sm_120f` wheels already emit native NVFP4/MXFP4 dense MMA instructions. Only **sparse** NVFP4/MXFP4 MMA (not currently used in FlashInfer) requires `sm_120a`/`sm_121a`.

> **Correction (2026-06-12):** An earlier version of this table stated that ALL `.kind::mxf4nvf4`/`.kind::mxf4` MMA was arch-specific-only. Per [Harry-Chen's feedback](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3170#issuecomment-4677810517) and PTX ISA §9.7.15.5.14 vs §9.7.15.6.3, the restriction is limited to the sparse (`mma.sp`) variant.

### Wheel build arch targets

issues.title: [Bug] sm12x MoE CuTe-DSL kernels are never disk-cached — cute.compile hardcodes no_cache=True, so every fresh engine re-pays 15–40 s MLIR compiles per kernel shape
issues.body:
## Summary

The Blackwell sm12x fused-MoE path compiles all of its CuTe-DSL kernels through explicit
`cute.compile(...)`, which unconditionally disables the DSL's file cache. The only caching
layer is three in-process Python dicts, so **every engine start re-pays the full MLIR JIT
cost for every kernel specialization it touches** — measured at **~40 s** for the dynamic
kernel's first hit and **~15–18 s per small-`m` micro-kernel specialization**. In a serving
context (vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`) these compiles land mid-request and freeze
the whole engine (vllm#47458: ~17.5 s stop-the-world stalls, all in-flight requests frozen
including mid-decode).

`CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` / `CUTE_DSL_DISABLE_FILE_CACHING` have no effect on this path — the
gate that would consult them is short-circuited before they are read.

## Environment

- flashinfer 0.6.12, 0.6.13, and **0.6.15.post1** (all verified; `moe_dispatch.py` cache
  structure unchanged across them)
- nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0 and **4.6.0** (both verified)
- SM120: RTX 5070 Ti (×2, TP/PP), RTX 5090 (unsharded), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell — reproduced
  on all three in the vllm#47458 thread
- Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` via vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`

## Mechanism (exact code paths)

1. **The DSL hardcodes `no_cache=True` for explicit compiles.**
   `CompileCallable._compile` sets `kwargs["no_cache"] = True` unconditionally:
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:604-605`
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:1319`

2. **The file cache is gated behind `if not no_cache`** — both the load and the dump —
   so the env vars are never even consulted for explicit compiles:
   - 4.5.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:1645` (load), `:1736` (dump)
   - 4.6.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:2004` (load), `:2105` (dump); in-memory `jit_cache` lookups
     likewise skipped under `no_cache` at `:2012`, `:2293`

3. **The sm12x MoE dispatch only ever compiles through `cute.compile`,** with plain
   in-process dicts on top — nothing reaches disk:
   - 0.6.12/0.6.13: `blackwell_sm12x/moe_dispatch.py:676/912/1675` (compile sites);
     `_STATIC/_MICRO/_DYNAMIC_KERNEL_CACHE`
   - 0.6.15.post1: compile sites at `:697/:942/:1723`; caches at `:486/:733/:1524`

4. Compounding factor (tracked separately as #3836): the micro-kernel `cache_key`
   includes both `m` and `workspace.max_rows` (0.6.15.post1 `moe_dispatch.py:770-791`,
   fields at `:774`/`:778`), so workspace growth invalidates already-compiled small-batch
   entries even *within* a process lifetime. With no disk layer underneath, each
   invalidation is a full 15 s+ recompile, not a reload.

## Verification

Behavioral check from the vllm#47458 thread (credit @waynehacking8, on 0.6.12 / DSL 4.5.0):

- `cute.compile` of a trivial `@cute.jit` function leaves `CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` **empty**.
- Calling the same jit function **directly** (implicit compile path) writes
  `cute_dsl_<hash>.mlir`, and a fresh process then logs `JIT cache hit IN-FILE`.
- Only the implicit direct-call path caches; flashinfer's MoE dispatch never uses it.

Source-level re-verification on 0.6.15.post1 / DSL 4.6.0 (2026-08-02, inside the
`vllm/vllm-openai` nightly image): every line cite in the Mechanism section above was
confirmed against the installed packages — the hardcoded `no_cache=True`, the
`if not no_cache` gates around both file-cache load and dump, the three `cute.compile`
sites, the three in-process dicts, and `m`/`max_rows` still present in the micr

open_prs.title: [CuTe, SM80] Skip KV blocks left of the local window in forward

positioning.overview: FlashAttention 是 Dao-AILab 维护的精确注意力（exact attention）加速库，核心卖点是 IO-aware 的 tiling 实现：在 HBM 与 SRAM 之间按 tile 搬运与计算，把标准 Attention 的 HBM 读写压到理论下界，从而在不牺牲数值精度的前提下显著提速并省显存。仓库目前同时承载多代产品：FA2 在顶层 `csrc/flash_attn`（CUDA，Ampere/Ada/Hopper），FA3 在 `hopper/`（Hopper-only，FP16/BF16/FP8），而活跃开发已切到 FA4——用 CuTeDSL（NVIDIA CUTLASS DSL）写成、在运行时编译为 PTX/CUBIN，面向 Hopper (SM90) 与 Blackwell (SM100/SM110)。AGENTS.md 与 CLAUDE.md 明确写明「active development is on FA4 in `flash_attn/cute/`」，commit 热点也集中在 `flash_attn/cute`（近 43 次提交）、`tests/cute`（15 次）与 `hopper/`。FA4 以 `flash-attn-4` 包发布，最新 release 为 `fa4-v4.0.0.beta33`（2026-09-30），仍处于 beta 阶段。README 对 FA3 标注为「beta release for testing / benchmarking」，FA4 则仍在快速迭代（SM100 支持、MLA、FP8、varlen 等特性在最近提交中频繁出现）。整体定位：面向大模型训练/推理的底层 attention 原语层，被 PyTorch生态（HuggingFace、xFormers、SDXL/DiT 训练等）广泛依赖。
positioning.problem: 标准 scaled dot-product attention 在长序列下的瓶颈是 QK^T 与 softmax 中间矩阵必须完整写入 HBM，导致 (seq_len² · d) 的显存占用与带宽受限的读写。FlashAttention 通过 tiling + 在线 softmax（recompute P 而非保存完整注意力矩阵）把显存降到 O(N·d) 并减少 HBM 访问。FA4 进一步把实现迁移到 CuTeDSL，以便直接利用 Hopper 的 TMA、WGMMA、named barrier 等硬件原语，并在同一套 Python DSL 上同时覆盖 SM90 与 SM100/SM110。目标用户：(1) 大模型训练框架开发者（需要更快、更省显存的 attention 后端，例如 GPT、LLaMA、DiT 训练）；(2) 推理/服务侧工程师（decode、varlen、paged-KV、MLA 等场景）；(3) 硬件/编译器方向的研究者（CuTeDSL 内核模板、kernel 生成、性能调优）。典型场景：替换 `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention` 后端；为扩散模型视频生成提供长上下文注意力；在 H100/B200 上做 FP8/MLA decode；在 AMD MI300 上通过 CK 或 Triton 后端跑 FA2。
positioning.users: 1) 大模型训练框架与研究人员——用 `flash_attn_func` / `flash_attn_qkvpacked_func` 替换原生 attention，降低显存、缩短 step time；2) 推理/服务工程师——使用 FA3/FA4 的 varlen、paged-KV、MLA、FP8 接口做低延迟 decode；3) 硬件性能工程师——在 `flash_attn/cute/` 与 `hopper/` 中研究 CuTeDSL 内核、TMA/WGMMA 利用、SM90/SM100 性能调优；4) AMD ROCm 用户——通过 `csrc/flash_attn_ck` 或 `third_party/aiter` Triton 后端在 MI200/MI300/RDNA 上获得 FA2 等价实现。

landscape.difference: 提供 memory-efficient attention 与可组合算子块，含 CUTLASS / Triton 实现，偏上层算子库与 Torch 集成；FlashAttention 更聚焦于单一 attention 原语的极致性能与多代硬件覆盖，FA4 直接下沉到 CuTeDSL 生成 PTX/CUBIN。
PyTorch 原生后端，调用 FlashAttention / Memory-Efficient Attention / Math 实现；FlashAttention 是 SDPA 所调用的底层后端之一，本仓库提供 SDPA 尚未原生覆盖的 FP8、MLA、paged-KV、varlen 等特性。
是 FA4 的底层 DSL 与模板库；本仓库在其之上构建 attention 专用内核，并暴露 Python 接口 `flash_attn.cute.flash_attn_func`。
为 AMD GPU 提供 Triton 版 FlashAttention 后端，已作为 `third_party/aiter` 子模块被本仓库集成进 ROCm Triton 路径。
同样聚焦 decode / ragged / paged-KV / MLA，但更偏推理运行时与 kernel 库；FlashAttention 覆盖更广的训练+推理场景，且是 FA4 在 CuTeDSL 上同时服务 SM90/SM100。

positioning.stage: 成熟（FA2）+ beta（FA3）+ 快速迭代 beta（FA4）。FA2 是业界事实标准；FA3 README 自标 beta；FA4 以 `flash-attn-4` 包发布，最新 tag 为 `fa4-v4.0.0.beta33`，commit 集中在 SM100/MLA/varlen 特性，仍属 beta。

codemap.layers:
仓库按「代际 × 硬件目标」自然分成五层。

1) 接入层（Python API）：`flash_attn/__init__.py`、`flash_attn/cute/__init__.py`、`flash_attn/cute/interface.py`、`hopper/flash_attn_interface.py`、`hopper/flash_attn_3/`。职责是把 `flash_attn_func` / `flash_attn_varlen_func` 这些用户可见 API 翻译成内部 kernel 调用，处理 dtype、causal、softcap、varlen、paged KV、MLA 等开关。

2) 调度层（tile / split / batch 调度）：`flash_attn/cute/prepare_scheduler.py`、`flash_attn/cute/tile_scheduler.py`、`flash_attn/cute/seqlen_info.py`、`flash_attn/cute/block_info.py`、`flash_attn/cute/cu_blocks_kernel.py`，以及 `hopper/flash_prepare_scheduler.cu`、`hopper/heuristics.h`。职责是把 (batch, heads, seqlen) 切成 CTA tile、决定 split-KV 数、生成 `cu_seqlens` / `cu_blocks` / `SchedulerMetadataTensorsTorch`，并为 SM100 的 CLC / dynamic-persistent 调度器喂状态。

3) 执行层（CuTeDSL kernel 主体）：`flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd*.py`、`flash_attn/cute/flash_bwd*.py`、`flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_mla*.py`、`flash_attn/cute/flash_bwd_mla*.py`、`flash_attn/cute/sm100_hd256_2cta_fmha_backward_*.py`。这是 FA4 的核心——用 CuTeDSL 在 Python 里写 TMA + WGMMA + named-barrier 的 forward/backward/MLA kernel。

4) 硬件抽象层（pipeline / barrier / copy / mma 描述）：`flash_attn/cute/pipeline.py`、`flash_attn/cute/named_barrier.py`、`flash_attn/cute/copy_utils.py`、`flash_attn/cute/mma_sm100_desc.py`、`flash_attn/cute/barrier.py`、`flash_attn/cute/ampere_helpers.py`、`flash_attn/cute/blackwell_helpers.py`。封装 Hopper/Blackwell 的 async pipeline、TMA、bulk-copy、UMMA/TMEM 描述符，让 kernel 层只描述「怎么算」。

5) 工具层（build / test / bench / debug）：`setup.py`、`flash_attn/cute/cute_dsl_ptxas.py`、`flash_attn/cute/cute_dsl_utils.py`、`tests/cute/`、`benchmarks/`、`AI/*.md`、`tools/`。负责编译到 PTX/CUBIN、持久化 kernel cache、two-pass 测试、SASS 级调试。

codemap.data_flow:
一次典型的 FA4 推理/训练前向调用链如下：

1) 用户调用 `flash_attn.cute.interface.flash_attn_func(q, k, v, causal=..., softmax_scale=...)`。interface 先做 dtype/shape 对齐（BF16/FP16，headdim 对齐到 8），判断走 standard、varlen、paged 还是 MLA 路径，并读取 env（`FLASH_ATTENTION_MLA_1CTA`、`FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED` 等）。

2) interface 调用 `flash_attn.cute.prepare_scheduler.FlashPrepareScheduler`，在 host 侧把 (batch, seqlen_q, seqlen_k, nheads, nheads_kv, headdim) 切成 M/N tile，计算 `num_m_blocks`、`num_n_blocks`、split-KV 数（`num_splits_dynamic`），产出 `SchedulerMetadataTensorsTorch`（含 `cu_total_m_blocks`、`cu_total_splits_m_blocks`、`blocks_to_batch_idx`、`tile_count_semaphore`）。对 varlen 还会先启动 `CuSeqlensToBlocksKernel`（`cu_blocks_kernel.py`）把 `cu_seqlens` 转成 block 偏移。

3) 根据目标架构（SM90/SM100/SM120）与 headdim、causal、MLA 标志，interface 选择具体 kernel：standard 走 `flash_fwd.py` 的 `flash_fwd_sm{90,100,120}`；MLA 走 `flash_fwd_mla_sm100.py`；block-sparse 走 `block_sparsity.py` + `topk_gather_kv.py`。

4) kernel 启动前先由 `flash_attn.cute.cute_dsl_ptxas` 把 `@cute.jit` 函数编译成 PTX/CUBIN（若命中磁盘缓存 `/tmp/${USER}/flash_attention_cute_dsl_cache/` 则跳过编译）。编译使用 `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` + `apache-tvm-ffi`，支持 FakeTensor 模式（不分配 GPU 显存）。

5) kernel 执行时，`tile_scheduler.py` 构造 `SchedulerState`（`create_clc` 或 `create_dynamic_persistent`），把硬件 CLC 或软件 dynamic-persistent 调度器初始化；`pipeline.py` 的 `PipelineStateSimple` / `PipelineTmaAsync` / `PipelineUmmaAsync` 管理 producer-consumer 环形缓冲。kernel 主体用 `copy_utils.py` 的 TMA bulk-copy 把 Q/K/V tile 从 HBM 搬到 SMEM，用 `mma_sm100_desc.py` 构造 WGMMA/UMMA 描述符做 QK^T 与 PV 矩阵乘，`softmax.py` 做在线 softmax（recompute P，不保存完整注意力矩阵），`mask.py` 注入 causal/local/ALiBi mask，`named_barrier.py` 做 warp-group 同步。

6) 输出 `out`（与 Q 同形状）与 `softmax_lse`（log-sum-exp，形状 b×h×seqlen_q，给 backward 用）被写回 HBM。

7) backward 时，`flash_bwd.py` / `flash_bwd_mla_sm100.py` 复用 forward 的 scheduler 元数据，用 `flash_bwd_preprocess` 把 dout 与 out 结合，再启动 dK/dV kernel（`BlackwellFusedMultiHeadAttentionBackwardDKDVKernel`）与 dQ kernel（`BlackwellFusedMultiHeadAttentionBackwardDQKernel`），最后 `flash_bwd_postprocess` 把部分和归约成最终梯度。

关键调度点：interface 的路径选择、prepare_scheduler 的 tile/split 决策、tile_scheduler 的 CLC vs dynamic-persistent 选择、pipeline 的 producer-consumer 同步。关键数据结构：`SchedulerMetadataTensorsTorch`、`SchedulerState` / `ClcSchedulerState`、`PipelineStateSimple`、`cute.Tensor`（Q/K/V/out/lse）。

install: # 1. 创建独立 Python 环境（推荐 Python 3.10–3.12，与 PyTorch 2.2+ 兼容）
conda create -n fa4 python=3.11 -y && conda activate fa4
# 2. 安装 PyTorch（Apple Silicon 用 MPS 后端，CPU 用默认）
pip install torch torchvision torchaudio
# 3. 克隆仓库（含子模块 third_party/aiter）
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention.git
cd flash-attention
# 4. 安装 FA4 的 Python 依赖（仅 CPU/MPS，不编译 CUDA kernel）
# 注意：nvidia-cutlass-dsl 依赖 CUDA 运行时，在 Mac 上无法真正编译 kernel，
# 但可以安装包以导入 Python 模块、阅读 CuTeDSL 代码。
pip install -e "flash_attn/cute[dev]" 2>&1 | tee install.log
# 5. 若上一步因 CUDA 依赖失败，则仅安装可运行部分：
pip install einops apache-tvm-ffi quack-kernels  # 跳过 nvidia-cutlass-dsl
pip install -e flash_attn/cute  # 无 extras，可能仍会尝试编译，需验证
# 6. 验证 Python 导入（不触发 kernel 编译）
python -c "from flash_attn.cute import flash_attn_func; print('import ok')"
# 7. 安装测试/开发工具
pip install pytest pytest-xdist pre-commit ruff
# 关键环境变量（Mac 上无 GPU 时设置）
export FLASH_ATTENTION_SKIP_CUDA_BUILD=TRUE   # 跳过 CUDA 编译，仅保留 Python 层
export FLASH_ATTENTION_FORCE_BUILD=FALSE       # 不强制本地编译
no_gpu_paths: 【可在 CPU/MPS 上执行的代码路径】
- `flash_attn/cute/__init__.py`、`flash_attn/cute/interface.py`：Python 调度层，可 import 并调用高层 API（但底层 kernel 会失败）。
- `flash_attn/cute/prepare_scheduler.py`、`flash_attn/cute/tile_scheduler.py`、`flash_attn/cute/seqlen_info.py`、`flash_attn/cute/block_info.py`：调度逻辑，可在 CPU 上跑单元测试（部分测试用 FakeTensorMode）。
- `flash_attn/cute/pipeline.py`、`flash_attn/cute/named_barrier.py`、`flash_attn/cute/mask.py`、`flash_attn/cute/softmax.py`：抽象描述，可在无 GPU 环境下 import 和调试。
- `flash_attn/flash_attn_triton.py`、`flash_attn/flash_attn_triton_og.py`：Triton 实现，理论上可在 AMD GPU 或 CPU 上跑，但 Mac 上无 Triton 后端支持，仅能读代码。
- `tests/cute/test_*.py` 中标记 `@maybe_fake_tensor_mode(USE_FAKE_TENSOR)` 的测试：用 FakeTensorMode 编译 kernel，不分配 GPU 内存（见 AGENTS.md 两阶段测试说明）。
- `tests/test_util.py`、`tests/test_rotary.py`：纯 CPU 测试，无 GPU 依赖。
【只能在 GPU 上执行的代码路径】
- `flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd*.py`、`flash_attn/cute/flash_bwd*.py`、`flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_mla*.py`、`flash_attn/cute/flash_bwd_mla*.py`：CuTeDSL kernel 主体，编译到 PTX/CUBIN，必须 NVIDIA GPU。
- `flash_attn/cute/sm100_hd256_2cta_fmha_backward_*.py`、`flash_attn/cute/sm100_*`、`flash_attn/cute/sm120_*`：SM100/SM120 专用 kernel，需 Blackwell GPU。
- `csrc/flash_attn/src/*.cu`：FA2 CUDA kernel，需 Ampere/Ada/Hopper GPU。
- `csrc/flash_attn_ck/*.cpp`：ROCm Composable Kernel 实现，需 AMD GPU。
- `hopper/` 下所有 `.cu`、`.hpp`、`.h`：FA3 Hopper-only 实现，需 H100/H800。
- `benchmarks/*.py`、`hopper/benchmark_*.py`：基准测试，需真实 GPU。
【Mac 上的实际策略】
- 本地用 FakeTensorMode 跑编译阶段测试（验证 kernel 能否编译通过），用 Colab 免费 T4 做最终执行验证。
- 阅读代码时重点关注 `flash_attn/cute/` 下的调度与 kernel 逻辑，用 `print` 或 `logging` 调试 Python 层。

test_suite: 测试框架：pytest + pytest-xdist（并行执行），部分测试用 `@maybe_fake_tensor_mode` 装饰器支持 FakeTensorMode。
测试目录：
- `tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py`：FA4 forward/backward 主测试（smoke_test 2/5）。
- `tests/cute/test_flash_attn_mla.py`：MLA（Multi-head Latent Attention）测试，覆盖 dense/sparse/paged KV。
- `tests/cute/test_flash_attn_varlen.py`：变长序列（varlen）测试。
- `tests/cute/test_mask_mod.py`、`tests/cute/test_score_mod.py`：mask 与 score 修饰符测试。
- `tests/cute/test_block_sparsity.py`：块稀疏注意力测试。
- `tests/test_flash_attn.py`：FA2 测试（需 GPU）。
- `tests/test_flash_attn_ck.py`：ROCm CK 后端测试（需 AMD GPU）。
- `tests/test_flash_attn_triton_amd.py`：Triton AMD 后端测试（需 AMD GPU）。
- `tests/test_util.py`、`tests/test_rotary.py`：纯 CPU 工具测试。
只跑 CPU 子集（Mac 无 GPU）：
pytest tests/test_util.py tests/test_rotary.py -x -q  # 纯 CPU，秒级完成
pytest tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -k "test_block_info or test_seqlen_info or test_scheduler" -x -q  # 调度逻辑测试
FakeTensorMode 编译阶段测试（无 GPU 内存分配，但会打开 CUDA 上下文）：
FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1 FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1 pytest -n 4 tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -x  # 编译所有 kernel，约 5–15 分钟
完整测试套件（需 GPU，Colab T4）：
FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=0 FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1 pytest tests/cute/ -x -q  # 30–60 分钟
耗时估算：
- CPU 子集（test_util + test_rotary）：< 10 秒。
- FakeTensorMode 编译 pass（test_flash_attn.py）：5–15 分钟（取决于 CPU 核心数）。
- GPU 执行 pass（test_flash_attn.py）：20–40 分钟（T4）。
- 完整 `tests/cute/` 套件：30–60 分钟（T4）。
debug_tips: 【断点与日志】
- Python 层断点：在 `flash_attn/cute/interface.py`、`flash_attn/cute/prepare_scheduler.py`、`flash_attn/cute/tile_scheduler.py` 中用 `import pdb; pdb.set_trace()` 或 IDE 调试。
- CuTeDSL kernel 内调试：用 `cute.printf` 或 `print` 在 kernel 内输出（需 GPU 执行）。
- 日志开关：`flash_attn/cute/fa_logging.py` 提供日志工具，设置 `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)` 查看调度信息。
【环境变量】
- `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1`：启用 FakeTensorMode，编译 kernel 但不执行（AGENTS.md 明确说明）。
- `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1`：启用持久化磁盘缓存，路径 `/tmp/${USER}/flash_attention_cute_dsl_cache/`。
- `FLASH_ATTENTION_TEST_EXPECT_CACHED=1`：执行阶段测试时，若 kernel 未命中缓存则失败（用于 CI 验证缓存完整性）。
- `FLASH_ATTENTION_TEST_COUNT_COMPILES=1`：仅统计编译次数，不执行测试。
- `FLASH_ATTENTION_SKIP_CUDA_BUILD=TRUE`：跳过 CUDA 编译，仅保留 Python 层（setup.py 中定义）。
- `FLASH_ATTENTION_FORCE_BUILD=TRUE`：强制本地编译，忽略预编译 wheel。
- `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<gpu_id>`：限制可见 GPU，用于多 GPU 环境隔离。
【Profiling 入口】
- `flash_attn/cute/benchmark.py`、`flash_attn/cute/benchmark_flash_attention_fp8.py`：FA4 基准测试脚本。
- `benchmarks/bench_sm90.py`、`benchmarks/benchmark_flash_attention.py`：FA2/FA3 基准测试。
- `hopper/benchmark_attn.py`、`hopper/benchmark_flash_attention_fp8.py`：FA3 基准测试。
- 用 `nsys profile` 或 `nvprof` 对 Python 脚本做 GPU profiling（需 NVIDIA GPU）。
【常见调试场景】
- 若 `import flash_attn.cute` 失败，检查 `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 是否安装，或降级到仅 Python 层。
- 若 FakeTensorMode 编译失败，检查 `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED` 是否启用，或删除缓存目录重试。
- 若 kernel 执行结果不对，用 `FLASH_ATTENTION_TEST_EXPECT_CACHED=1` 确认是否使用了过期缓存。
ci: CI 框架：GitHub Actions（`.github/workflows/`），含 bump beta tag 脚本（`.github/scripts/bump_beta_tag.py`）。
CI 主要跑：
- 代码格式检查：`ruff format`（最近 commit `fb97d25` 为 ruff format 提交）。
- 静态检查：`pre-commit`（`.pre-commit-config.yaml` 配置）。
- 编译测试：`FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1` 编译 pass + `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=0` 执行 pass（见 `tools/two_pass_tests.sh`）。
- 完整测试套件：`pytest tests/cute/` 在多个 GPU 上并行（`-n 256` workers）。
PR 会被以下检查卡住：
- `ruff format` 格式不符（最近 commit `fb97d25` 显示仓库已强制 ruff 格式化）。
- `pre-commit` 钩子失败（isort、ruff、mypy 等）。
- FakeTensorMode 编译失败（kernel 无法编译）。
- GPU 执行阶段测试失败（数值精度、shape 不匹配等）。
- `FLASH_ATTENTION_TEST_EXPECT_CACHED=1` 时 kernel 未命中缓存（CI 要求所有 kernel 在编译 pass 中已缓存）。
pitfalls: 【坑 1：Mac 上无法真正编译或执行 CUDA kernel】
Apple Silicon 无 NVIDIA GPU，`nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 依赖 CUDA 运行时，只能安装 Python 包但无法编译 PTX/CUBIN。本地开发只能读代码、跑 FakeTensorMode 编译验证，最终执行必须用 Colab T4 或远程 GPU。
【坑 2：setup.py 默认尝试 CUDA 编译
直接 `pip install -e .` 会触发 CUDA 编译，在 Mac 上会失败。必须设置 `FLASH_ATTENTION_SKIP_CUDA_BUILD=TRUE` 或仅安装 `flash_attn/cute` 子包。
【坑 3：CuTeDSL 缓存导致过期 binary
`FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1` 启用磁盘缓存后，修改 kernel 代码可能仍命中旧缓存。调试时删除 `/tmp/${USER}/flash_attention_cute_dsl_cache/` 或禁用缓存。
【坑 4：FakeTensorMode 与真实执行的差异
FakeTensorMode 只验证编译，不验证数值精度。编译通过的 kernel 在 GPU 上仍可能数值错误（见 AI/ 目录下的 DEBUG_*.md 文档）。
【坑 5：环境变量拼写与大小写
`FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR`、`FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED` 等变量名拼写错误会静默失效，导致测试行为不符合预期。
【坑 6：子模块 third_party/aiter 未初始化
ROCm Triton 后端依赖 `third_party/aiter`，`git clone` 时需 `--recurse-submodules`，否则 `FLASH_ATTENTION_TRITON_AMD_ENABLE=TRUE` 安装会失败。
【坑 7：测试装饰器 `@maybe_fake_tensor_mode` 缺失
新增测试函数必须加 `@maybe_fake_tensor_mode(USE_FAKE_TENSOR)` 装饰器，并在数据依赖检查前用 `if is_fake_mode(): return` 退出，否则 CI 两阶段测试会失败（AGENTS.md 明确说明）。
【坑 8：FA2/FA3/FA4 三代代码共存，易混淆
仓库同时包含 FA2（`csrc/flash_attn/`）、FA3（`hopper/`）、FA4（`flash_attn/cute/`），活跃开发在 FA4。修改代码前确认目标代际，避免在 FA2 上修复 FA4 的 bug。
【坑 9：Windows 支持仍 experimental
README 提到 Windows 编译从 v2.3.2 开始可能工作，但需更多测试。Mac 上无官方 Windows 支持，但 Linux 容器或远程开发是可行替代。
【坑 10：ninja 编译 RAM 不足
README 明确警告：若机器 RAM < 96GB 且 CPU 核心多，`ninja` 可能耗尽内存。Mac 16GB 应设置 `MAX_JOBS=2` 或 `MAX_JOBS=4` 限制并行编译任务。

community.process: 仓库根目录没有独立的 CONTRIBUTING.md，贡献流程主要靠 AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md 与 setup.py 环境变量驱动。CLAUDE.md 明确：活跃开发在 `flash_attn/cute/`，安装用 `pip install -e "flash_attn/cute[dev]"`，测试用 `pytest tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py` 等；并给出「two-pass testing」流程（先用 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1` 并行编译，再用缓存执行）。pre-commit 配置存在（`.pre-commit-config.yaml`），且 PR #2940 专门做 `ruff format`，表明代码风格用 ruff 强制格式化。没有看到 CLA/DCO 文件。Issue 模板与 PR 模板未在根目录显式出现，但 `.github/workflows` 与 `.github/actions` 存在，CI 会跑构建与测试。贡献者应先在 GitHub Issue 复现/讨论（如 #2957、#2969 带具体 GPU 与 head_dim 条件），再提 PR。
community.review_style: Review 风格偏「硬核内核工程师」：紧贴具体 GPU 架构、head_dim、varlen、GQA、deterministic 等细节。Issue 标题高度具体（如「[CuTe, SM100] dsink loses precision: dpsum uses the bf16-rounded O」「[CuTe, SM90] Paged KV with page_size != tile_n: wrong output at head_dim 80/96 (non-causal), illegal memory access at 160/224」），要求复现条件精确到 dtype、head_dim、page_size、causal 开关。PR 拆分细致（如 #2964–#2968 把「Unify hd256 backward」拆成 5 个子 PR：tests first → 2CTA schedules → opt-in → GQA/varlen → delete dedicated kernels），说明维护者偏好小步、可审查的增量提交。响应速度：高频提交与 weekly beta release 表明核心维护者几乎每日在线；Issue 指派（Johnsonms、tzadouri、micmelesse）显示会按模块分派。对数值精度、illegal memory access、deterministic 类 Issue 反应最快。

etiquette: 得体：提 Issue 时明确标注 GPU 型号（SM90/SM100/SM120/ROCm）、head_dim、dtype、causal/varlen/paged_kv 开关、是否 deterministic；复现脚本最小化。
得体：提 PR 时遵循现有拆分习惯（tests first → 小步增量 → 最终 delete dedicated kernels），并在 PR 标题标注代际与硬件前缀，如 [CuTe, SM100]、[FA2]、[ROCm/CK]。
得体：本地用 two-pass testing（`FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1` 编译 + 缓存执行）验证，确保 kernel 编译通过且测试命中缓存（`FLASH_ATTENTION_TEST_EXPECT_CACHED=1`）。
得体：代码风格遵循 ruff（PR #2940 已强制），提交前跑 pre-commit。
得体：在 RFC 类 Issue（如 #2456 head_dim=256/512、#2915 sparse MLA 64-head）先讨论方案再动笔。
不得体：在 Mac 上无 GPU 时直接跑 `pytest tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py` 期望全部通过——必须用 FakeTensorMode 或 two-pass 流程。
不得体：跨代际大改（如同时动 FA2/FA3/FA4）而不拆 PR；维护者明显偏好按代际与硬件分界线独立提交。
不得体：在 Issue 里只写「性能慢/报错」却不给 GPU 架构、head_dtype、seqlen、batch 等关键信息——这类 Issue 会被要求补充复现条件。
不得体：未经讨论直接提「重构整个 scheduler」类 PR；调度器（prepare_scheduler / tile_scheduler / seqlen_info）是核心路径，改动需先 RFC。
what_they_want: SM100/SM120 (Blackwell) 支持完善：近期提交与 Issue 密集指向 SM100（B200/SM103）的 hd256 backward、varlen Q、decode、sink 精度、illegal memory access 等问题（#2950、#2951、#2952、#2969、#2860、#2852），是当前最活跃的开发线。
MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention) 扩展：#2938 刚合入 1CTA MLA forward (dense + sparse top-k) 与 dispatch heuristic；#2915 提出 native 64-head sparse MLA 设计；MLA backward 与 paged KV 仍在推进。
head_dim=256/512 统一：#2456 RFC 与 #2964–#2968 系列 PR 正在把 hd256 backward 统一为默认并删除专用 kernel；hd512 仍在讨论。
数值精度与 deterministic：#2969 dsink precision、#2946 learnable-sink logits overflow、#2244 FA3 deterministic backward 非确定性、#2957 Paged KV 数值错误——精度类 bug 优先级高。
ROCm / CK / aiter 后端：#2933 gfx905 asm backward、#2963 gfx12 BF16 D256 split-head backward、#2901 num_splits heuristic 修复——micmelesse 在推动，欢迎 ROCm 后端贡献。
Python dispatch 开销优化：#2426 记录 FA4 ~20–25us Python dispatch overhead，需要熟悉 `flash_attn/cute/interface.py` 与 `torch.library` 的人做 dispatch 层瘦身。
跨平台构建（Windows / CUDA 13 / PyTorch 2.15）：#2872、#2799、#2861 显示 Windows 与最新 PyTorch/CUDA 适配仍在打磨。
FA2 维护与 split-KV：#2961「Normalize split-KV combine scales」等表明 FA2 仍在被训练框架依赖，需要人维护 split-KV combine 的正确性。
测试基础设施：two-pass testing 工具（`tools/two_pass_tests.sh`）、CI matrix（#2976 publish.yml tag filter）需要人维护与扩展。

gaps.gap: FA4 的 Python 层测试覆盖在 SM100/SM110 新特性上仍然稀疏，尤其缺少 head_dim=256 backward、varlen decode、MLA sparse top-k 等组合场景的细粒度单测
gaps.evidence: commit 热点集中在 `flash_attn/cute`（43 次）与 `tests/cute`（15 次），但最近提交如 #2938「1CTA MLA forward (dense + sparse top-k), sparse MLA backward at any head count」、#2952「Allow deterministic=True in the hd256 backward」、#2951「hd256: S ping-pong on SM103, 2CTA for varlen Q and decode」都引入了新 kernel 变体；`tests/cute/` 目录仅 15 次提交热点，且 AGENTS.md 列出的测试文件只有 `test_flash_attn.py`、`test_flash_attn_mla.py`、`test_flash_attn_varlen.py` 等少数几个，未见针对 hd256 backward / varlen decode / MLA sparse 的独立测试文件。
gaps.why_you: 写测试只需要在 CPU 上构造小张量、用 FakeTensorMode 触发 kernel 编译路径（AGENTS.md 已明确支持 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1`），无需真实 GPU 即可验证接口正确性与形状/类型分发逻辑。这是无 GPU 条件下最高杠杆的贡献。

gaps.gap: FA4 文档与 README 对 SM100/SM110 支持矩阵、已支持特性（MLA、FP8、varlen、head_dim=256）的描述严重滞后于代码实际能力
gaps.evidence: README 仍把 FA3 标为「beta release for testing / benchmarking」，FA4 章节仅给出最小安装示例；最新 release `fa4-v4.0.0.beta33`（2026-09-30）已支持 SM100/SM110、MLA、FP8、varlen decode、hd256 backward（见 #2952、#2938、#2951），但 README 与 `usage.md` 未同步更新支持矩阵表格。
gaps.why_you: 文档工作完全在 CPU 上完成，只需读源码（`flash_attn/cute/interface.py`、`flash_attn/cute/__init__.py`、`tests/cute/` 中的测试参数）即可整理出真实支持矩阵。这是建立社区信任与降低贡献者门槛的关键一步。

gaps.gap: FA4 缺少独立的、可离线运行的 benchmark 脚本与回归基准，尤其缺少 SM100/SM110 上 hd256、MLA、varlen decode 的性能基线
gaps.evidence: `benchmarks/` 目录有 `bench_sm90.py`、`benchmark_mla_paged_kv.py`、`benchmark_sparse_mla_fwd.py`、`benchmark_varlen_sched.py` 等，但无 `bench_sm100.py` 或 `bench_hd256.py`；最近提交 #2951、#2952 引入 hd256 新 kernel 却未伴随可复现的 benchmark 脚本。
gaps.why_you: benchmark 脚本本身可在 CPU 上编写与 dry-run 验证（用 FakeTensorMode 或仅需验证脚本逻辑），最终数值确认才需 Colab T4 几十分钟。这是把「能跑」变成「可衡量」的桥梁。

gaps.gap: FA4 的 error message 与输入校验在 Python 接口层（`interface.py`、`flash_fwd*.py` 入口）仍然粗糙，用户遇到不支持的 dtype/head_dim/varlen 组合时难以定位
gaps.evidence: Issue #2456 RFC「FA4 — head_dim=256 & head_dim=512」与 #2969「dsink loses precision」表明边界条件处理仍是活跃议题；`flash_attn/cute/interface.py` 作为用户入口，其参数校验与错误提示在快速迭代中未同步完善。
gaps.why_you: 改善错误提示只需读 Python 层代码，无需 GPU。这是高 ROI 的「让库对新人友好」贡献，也让你自己快速熟悉所有代码路径。

gaps.gap: FA4 的 CI / 测试基础设施文档缺失，尤其缺少「如何在无 GPU 环境下跑测试」的明确指引
gaps.evidence: AGENTS.md 与 CLAUDE.md 详细描述了两阶段测试（FakeTensorMode 编译 + 真实执行），但 README 与 `CONTRIBUTING`（为空）均未提及；`tools/two_pass_tests.sh` 存在但无顶层文档链接。
gaps.why_you: 你自己在 MacBook Air 上就会遇到这个问题，解决它同时产出文档，直接降低后续所有贡献者的门槛。

gaps.gap: FA4 的调度器（`prepare_scheduler.py`、`tile_scheduler.py`、`cu_blocks_kernel.py`）缺少独立的单元测试与注释，CLC/dynamic-persistent 调度逻辑的正确性仅靠端到端测试覆盖
gaps.evidence: `flash_attn/cute/prepare_scheduler.py` 是 `hopper/flash_prepare_scheduler.cu` 的 CuTeDSL 重实现（文件头注释明确说明），`tile_scheduler.py` 含 `ClcDynamicPersistentTileScheduler` 封装；`tests/cute/` 中无对应独立测试文件。
gaps.why_you: 调度器逻辑可在 CPU 上用 FakeTensorMode 或纯 Python 单元测试验证（`SchedulerMetadataTensorsTorch` 是纯 Python NamedTuple），无需 GPU。这是理解 FA4 核心并切入深层贡献的捷径。

gaps.gap: FA4 与 FA2/FA3 的 API 兼容性对照文档缺失，用户从旧版本迁移时缺乏明确指引
gaps.evidence: `flash_attn/__init__.py`（FA2）、`flash_attn/cute/__init__.py`（FA4）、`hopper/flash_attn_interface.py`（FA3）三套接口并存；`usage.md` 仅覆盖旧版用法，未给出迁移对照表。
gaps.why_you: 整理对照表只需读三个 `__init__.py` 与 `interface.py`，纯文档工作，无 GPU 依赖。这是社区高需求、低门槛的贡献。

gaps.gap: FA4 的 ROCm/CK 后端（`csrc/flash_attn_ck/`）与 CUDA 后端在 varlen、split-K 等特性上的行为差异缺少文档与回归测试
gaps.evidence: commit #2901「Fix num_splits heuristic, which could never return more than 1」暴露 CK 后端 split-K 逻辑与 CUDA 侧不一致；`tests/test_flash_attn_ck.py` 存在但覆盖范围未知，README 中 ROCm 章节未提及与 CUDA 的行为差异。
gaps.why_you: 整理差异与补充测试可在 CPU 上读代码完成，最终验证才需 ROCm GPU（可暂缓）。这是跨后端一致性这一长期议题的切入点。

entry.ownership_target: FA4 Python 层（`flash_attn/cute/`）的测试基础设施、调度器单元测试、以及 SM100/SM110 新特性的文档与 benchmark 基线
entry.why_this_target: AGENTS.md 与 CLAUDE.md 明确写明「active development is on FA4 in `flash_attn/cute/`」，commit 热点（`flash_attn/cute` 43 次、`tests/cute` 15 次）证实这是当前开发中心。该层的工作（测试、文档、benchmark 脚本、错误提示、调度器单测）大量可在 CPU/FakeTensorMode 下完成，仅最终数值确认需 Colab T4。这条路径从「补测试/文档」起步，逐步深入到「调度器逻辑 → kernel 调试 → 新特性实现」，是通向维护者身份的最稳妥路线——既避开无 GPU 的硬约束，又直接服务于核心维护者（Johnsonms、tzadouri）当前最活跃的模块。
phase_30: 【读代码】通读 `flash_attn/cute/__init__.py`、`flash_attn/cute/interface.py`，用 Python 画出 FA4 的 API 调用链与参数分发逻辑（dtype/causal/softcap/varlen/paged KV/MLA 开关如何路由到具体 kernel）。
【读代码】通读 `flash_attn/cute/prepare_scheduler.py` 与 `flash_attn/cute/tile_scheduler.py`，理解 `FlashPrepareScheduler`、`SchedulerState`、`ClcDynamicPersistentTileScheduler` 的职责与状态机。
【读代码】通读 `flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm90.py`、`flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_sm100.py`、`flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd_mla_sm100.py`，理解 forward kernel 的 tile 策略与 TMA/WGMMA 使用模式。
【搭环境】在 MacBook Air 上按 runbook 完成 `pip install -e "flash_attn/cute[dev]"`（或降级安装），验证 `python -c "from flash_attn.cute import flash_attn_func"` 通过；设置 `FLASH_ATTENTION_SKIP_CUDA_BUILD=TRUE`。
【跑测试】在 CPU 上运行 `FLASH_ATTENTION_FAKE_TENSOR=1 FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1 pytest -n 4 tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -x`，确认 FakeTensorMode 编译通过，建立本地开发基线。
【扫 Issue】浏览 Issue 标签 `good first issue`、`documentation`、`tests`、`SM100`、`MLA`，记录 5–10 个与测试/文档/支持矩阵相关的开放 Issue，标注哪些可在无 GPU 下完成。
【社区露面】在 1–2 个「文档滞后」或「测试缺失」的 Issue 下留言确认意图（如「我打算整理 SM100 支持矩阵文档」），观察维护者反应，建立存在感。
phase_60: 【补测试】为 `flash_attn/cute/prepare_scheduler.py` 与 `flash_attn/cute/tile_scheduler.py` 写独立单元测试（用 FakeTensorMode 或纯 Python），覆盖 `SchedulerMetadataTensorsTorch`、`FlashPrepareScheduler.get_grid_shape`、`SchedulerState.create_clc/create_dynamic_persistent` 等。
【补测试】为 `flash_attn/cute/interface.py` 的参数校验与错误路径写测试，覆盖不支持的 dtype/head_dim/varlen 组合，验证错误信息清晰可读。
【写 benchmark】编写 `benchmarks/bench_sm100.py` 与 `benchmarks/bench_hd256.py`，覆盖 hd128/hd256 forward/backward、varlen、MLA 等组合；先在 CPU 上 dry-run 验证脚本逻辑，再用 Colab T4 跑一次收集基线数值。
【更新文档】更新 README 的 FA4 章节，添加 SM100/SM110 支持矩阵表格（dtype × head_dim × causal × varlen × MLA × FP8），引用 `tests/cute/` 中的测试参数作为证据。
【更新文档】在 `usage.md` 或新文件 `migration.md` 中整理 FA2 → FA3 → FA4 API 对照表，列出 `flash_attn.flash_attn_func` vs `flash_attn.cute.flash_attn_func` vs `flash_attn_3.flash_attn_interface.flash_attn_func` 的参数差异。
【提 PR】提交 2–3 个「测试 + 文档」PR，每个 PR 范围明确（如「Add unit tests for FlashPrepareScheduler」或「Document SM100 support matrix」），控制在 200 行以内，便于 review。
【申请权限】在首次 PR 被合并后，在 Discord/Issue 中申请 triage 权限或 reviewer 提名，表达长期维护 `flash_attn/cute/tests` 与文档的意愿。
phase_90: 【深入调度器】基于对 `prepare_scheduler.py` 与 `tile_scheduler.py` 的理解，认领一个调度器相关的 Issue（如 CLC dynamic-persistent 在 varlen decode 下的 tile 分配优化），在 Colab T4 上验证性能。
【深入 kernel 调试】认领一个 kernel 精度或性能 Issue（如 #2969「dsink loses精度」或 hd256 backward 的数值问题），用 Colab T4 复现并提交修复。
【补 MLA 测试】为 `flash_fwd_mla_1cta_sm100.py` 与 sparse MLA（#2938 引入）写独立测试，覆盖 dense/sparse top-k/paged KV 组合。
【跨后端一致性】整理 `csrc/flash_attn_ck/` 与 `flash_attn/cute/` 在 split-K、varlen 行为上的差异文档，补充 `tests/test_flash_attn_ck.py` 中缺失的回归用例。
【CI 改善】基于 `tools/two_pass_tests.sh` 与 AGENTS.md 的两阶段测试流程，写一份 `CONTRIBUTING.md` 或 `docs/testing.md`，明确「无 GPU 时如何跑测试」。
【成为 reviewer】在 `flash_attn/cute/tests`、`flash_attn/cute/*.py` 的 PR 上持续 review，争取被维护者（Johnsonms、tzadouri）认可为 `flash_attn/cute` 方向的 reviewer。
【发布基线】将 benchmark 脚本与 Colab T4 基线结果整理为 `benchmarks/RESULTS_SM100.md`，为后续性能回归提供参照。

first_prs.title: Add unit tests for FlashPrepareScheduler and SchedulerState
first_prs.scope: 在 `tests/cute/test_prepare_scheduler.py`（新建）中覆盖 `FlashPrepareScheduler` 的 `__init__`、`get_grid_shape`、`__call__` 的 FakeTensorMode 编译路径，以及 `SchedulerMetadataTensorsTorch` 的字段访问；在 `tests/cute/test_tile_scheduler.py`（新建）中覆盖 `SchedulerState.create_clc`、`create_dynamic_persistent`、`consumer_wait/release` 状态机。
first_prs.why_safe: 纯 Python + FakeTensorMode，不触发真实 GPU 执行；测试对象是调度器状态机，不涉及数值精度；失败时不会影响现有端到端测试。

first_prs.title: Document SM100/SM110 support matrix in README
first_prs.scope: 更新 README 的「FlashAttention-4」章节，新增支持矩阵表格（dtype × head_dim × causal × varlen × MLA × FP8 × sliding window），每个单元格标注「✅/❌/部分」并引用对应测试文件或 Issue 编号作为证据；同步更新 `usage.md` 中的安装示例。

first_prs.title: Add input validation tests for flash_attn.cute.interface
first_prs.scope: 在 `tests/cute/test_interface.py`（新建）中测试 `flash_attn_func` 与 `flash_attn_varlen_func` 对非法参数（如不支持的 dtype、head_dim=300、varlen 但无 cu_seqlens）的错误抛出行为，验证 `ValueError` 消息包含可操作的提示。

Colab T4 上的 benchmark 基线被社区引用（如在 Issue 讨论或 PR 中作为性能参照）。
被维护者提名为 `flash_attn/cute/tests` 或 `flash_attn/cute/docs` 方向的 reviewer。
连续 3 个月每月至少 1 个 PR 被合并，且范围从文档/测试逐步扩展到调度器逻辑或 kernel 修复。

risks.risk: 无 GPU 导致无法验证 kernel 实际性能与数值精度，贡献长期停留在「文档/测试」层，难以切入核心 kernel 开发
risks.mitigation: 用 FakeTensorMode 覆盖编译路径与接口逻辑；与有 GPU 的社区成员结对（在 Issue 中明确「需要 Colab T4 验证」）；申请 Lambda Labs / Colab Pro 等免费/低成本 GPU 资源；优先选择「调度器逻辑」「tile 策略」这类可在 CPU 上验证正确性的方向。

risks.risk: FA4 处于 beta 阶段（最新 `fa4-v4.0.0.beta33`），API 与 kernel 接口快速变化，文档与测试很快过时
risks.mitigation: 文档中明确标注「as of fa4-v4.0.0.beta33」版本号；测试用参数化覆盖而非硬编码；订阅 release notification，在每个新 beta 发布后跑一次测试套件；优先写「支持矩阵」类文档而非「具体用法」类文档，前者变化频率更低。

risks.risk: 核心维护者（Tri Dao、Johnsonms）响应慢或对新贡献者冷漠，导致 PR 长期挂起
risks.mitigation: 先从小范围、高确定性的 PR（文档、拼写修复、单测）入手建立信任；在 Issue 中充分引用代码证据（文件路径 + 行号）证明自己做过功课；同时在 PyTorch/HuggingFace 相关 repo 建立并行贡献记录，降低对单一社区的依赖。

issues.title: [CuTe, SM100] dsink loses precision: dpsum uses the bf16-rounded O
issues.body:
On SM100 (B200, main `037e808b`), 16 `test_flash_attn_output` cases with `has_learnable_sink=True` fail `check_dsink_vs_ref` by up to 7 bf16 ulp. Example (`128-128-128-True-0-0.0-False-False-True-gqa-dtype0`):
```
dSink: diff=tensor([0.0000, 0.0547, 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000]) exceeds tolerance=tensor([0.0469, 0.0469, 0.0938, 0.1562, 0.0938, 0.0469])
```

**Cause**: `dsink = -Σ_rows exp(sink - lse) · dpsum` cancels heavily (Σ|terms| = 131 vs |dsink| = 1.9 on head 1 above), and the preprocess forms `dpsum = rowsum(dO · out)` from the **bf16-rounded** `out`. Recomputing in fp64 with the kernel's own bf16 `out` reproduces the kernel's value; with the exact O the error disappears:

| head 1 | dsink |
|---|---|
| kernel | −1.8594 |
| fp64, dpsum from the kernel's bf16 `out` | −1.8605 |
| fp64, exact O | −1.9118 |
| test reference | −1.9141 |

`dq` carries the same error but it stays within its own tolerance. Not related to #2946 (SM90 finalizer overflow).

**Fix** (#2971): the dense SM100 forward writes `o_lo = fp32(O) − bf16(O)` when `learnable_sink` requires grad, as the sparse-MLA forward already does; `_bwd_preprocess` forms dpsum from `out + o_lo`.

issues.title: [CuTe, SM90] Paged KV with page_size != tile_n: wrong output at head_dim 80/96 (non-causal), illegal memory access at 160/224
issues.body:
On SM90, a forward call with a page table returns wrong output at head_dim 80 and 96 without causal masking, and hits an illegal memory access at head_dim 160 and 224. This happens when the page size is not the kernel's tile_n, so K/V load through the cp.async `PagedKVManager` loader. The same K/V give the right result without a page table, or with `page_size == tile_n` (paged TMA). At head_dim 80 and 96 nothing raises and the output is finite.

Repro on `main` (843bf0b86b), GH200, torch 2.13.0+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, quack-kernels 0.6.5:

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from flash_attn.cute import flash_attn_varlen_func

torch.manual_seed(0)
seqlen_k, nheads, page_size = 300, 4, 16
num_pages = (seqlen_k + page_size - 1) // page_size
page_table = torch.arange(num_pages, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)[None]
seqused_k = torch.tensor([seqlen_k], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
for d in (96, 160):
    q = torch.randn(1, 16, nheads, d, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    k = torch.randn(1, seqlen_k, nheads, d, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    v = torch.randn_like(k)
    ref = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(*(x.transpose(1, 2).float() for x in (q, k, v)))
    ref = ref.transpose(1, 2)
    out = flash_attn_varlen_func(q, k, v)[0]
    print(f"d={d} contiguous: max abs err {(out.float() - ref).abs().max().item():.4f}")
    # The same keys in pages of 16 (page_size != tile_n, so the cp.async loader runs)
    pad = (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, num_pages * page_size - seqlen_k)
    k_paged = F.pad(k, pad).view(num_pages, page_size, nheads, d)
    v_paged = F.pad(v, pad).view(num_pages, page_size, nheads, d)
    out = flash_attn_varlen_func(q, k_paged, v_paged, page_table=page_table, seqused_k=seqused_k)[0]
    print(f"d={d} paged:      max abs err {(out.float() - ref).abs().max().item():.4f}")
```

```
d=96 contiguous: max abs err 0.0012
d=96 paged:      max abs err 0.3638
d=160 contiguous: max abs err 0.0012
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

The head_dim 96 paged error changes from run to run. Expected: the paged errors match the contiguous ones. With the fix in #2958 they do, and all four lines print 0.0012.

### Cause

`load_KV` copies a tile of tile_n rows in passes of `num_threads // gmem_threads_per_row` rows ([paged_kv.py#L233-L248](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/843bf0b86bda1c92edc440ec58f9b5194609abac/flash_attn/cute/paged_kv.py#L233-L248)). A pass is 32 rows at head_dim 96, 160 and 224, and 64 rows at head_dim 80. The SM90 tiles for these head dims have tile_n 144, 112 and 80 ([interface.py#L164-L181](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/843bf0b86bda1c92edc440ec58f9b5194609abac/flash_attn/cute/interface.py#L164-L181)). These are not multiples of the pass height, so the last pass also covers rows tile_n and up.

The SM90 shared-memory layout is `((8, tile_n/8), (w, d/w), stage)`, with w the swizzle-atom width. In it, row tile_n + i of one head-dim block is row i of the next block. For the last block, the overflow is the first rows of the next stage, or lies past the K/V buffer. The seqlen predicate does not stop these writes, because a predicated-off cp.async zero-fills its destination instead of skipping it.

So each K/V load writes zeros, or a row of page 0, over the first rows of the tile's other head-dim blocks, racing with their real data. It also writes over the first rows of the other stage, which can hold the next bl

issues.title: [CuTe, SM90] Finite learnable-sink logits overflow final normalization
issues.body:
On the native SM90 FA4 path, a finite positive learnable-sink logit can overflow final normalization and produce an infinite LSE. This reproduces with zero ordinary attention logits and sink=100; every input is finite.

Baseline: `616b0e8abab13b87b01525b3916d5a863ab02ae0`. Hardware: NVIDIA H20 (SM90), reproduced on both GPUs. Runtime: Torch 2.7.0+cu128, CUDA 12.8, CuTe DSL 4.8.0, Quack 0.5.3 and TVM-FFI 0.1.12. The linked validation report records the installed runtime and its dependency-metadata conflict.

Minimal reproduction, matching the non-causal BF16/PackGQA-disabled analytical regression:

```python
import math
import torch
from flash_attn.cute import flash_attn_func

q = torch.zeros(1, 4, 4, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
k = torch.zeros(1, 64, 2, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
v = torch.ones_like(k)
sink = torch.tensor([-100.0, 0.0, 8.0, 100.0], device="cuda")
out, lse = flash_attn_func(
    q, k, v, learnable_sink=sink,
    pack_gqa=False, num_splits=1, return_lse=True,
)
assert torch.isfinite(lse).all(), lse
expected = torch.logaddexp(torch.full_like(sink, math.log(64)), sink)
expected = expected[None, :, None].expand_as(lse)
torch.testing.assert_close(lse, expected, rtol=0, atol=1e-4)
```

For each head, expected LSE is `log(64 + exp(sink))`, evaluated stably with `logaddexp`. The sink=100 head should return finite LSE approximately100; the baseline returns infinity.

The SM90 finalizer adds the sink exponential relative to the previous QK maximum, without first incorporating the sink into that maximum. Draft fix #2944 rebases the denominator **and the output multiplier** against `max(attention_max, sink_logit)`, preserving the no-sink specialization and the online KV loop.

| Validation | Baseline | Draft patch |
|---|---|---|
| Analytical sink=100 | Infinite LSE | Finite LSE=100 |
| New analytical/mask/GQA/forward-backward cases | Reproducer fails | 76 pass, no skips/xfails |
| Existing sink dtype and varlen/LSE-gradient regressions | Existing criteria | 6 pass with unchanged criteria |
| Complete original Qwen3-0.6B inference on both H20s | Native FA4 reference | Exact logits and all32 generated tokens |

The Qwen3 model has no learnable sink and therefore validates the no-sink regression path; sink semantics and gradients are checked independently. This is a correctness report, with no speedup claim. Native validation here covers SM90; other architectures require separate evidence.

Draft PR: https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2944

[Committed report, frozen harnesses and raw results](https://github.com/0z5a/flash-attention/blob/4a86547f7e7f51e6c4c35734142a8bfe3e28b2dd/tests/cute/TEST_RESULT_SM90_SINK.md).

issues.title: FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1 causes cudaErrorInvalidDeviceFunction on cross-process load
issues.body:
**Title:** `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1` causes `cudaErrorInvalidDeviceFunction` on cross-process load

## Summary

Enabling the cute DSL persistent JIT cache (`FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1` + `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR=<path>`) causes the next process to crash on its first attention call with:

```
RuntimeError: CUDA Error: cudaErrorInvalidDeviceFunction
  in _flash_attn_fwd.compile_cache[compile_key](...)
```

The cache key in `flash_attn/cute/cache_utils.py` doesn't fully disambiguate compiled artifacts. A `.cubin` cached by one process is loaded into a different process's `compile_cache` dict for a slightly different call site, then handed to CUDA's launch, which rejects it.

Within a single process the in-memory cache works correctly — same process's compiled kernels match their use sites. The bug is specifically in cross-process reuse of the disk-cached artifacts.

## Environment

- flash-attention: `Dao-AILab/flash-attention@<recent HEAD>` (also reproducible with `RandNMR73/flash-attention@fa4-compile`, fork SHA `71677f5f`)
- torch: 2.11.0+cu128
- CUDA: 12.9.1
- Python: 3.12.13
- GPU: NVIDIA GB200 (sm_100)
- nvidia-cutlass-dsl: bundled with torch wheel
- Workload: LTX-2 video diffusion (FastVideo), bidirectional self-attention via `flash_attn.cute`

## Reproduce

1. Set `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED=1` and `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR=/persistent/path` in the container env.
2. Start a Python process that exercises `flash_attn.cute` over multiple attention shapes (we hit it on first call after a warmup pass with stage-1 + stage-2 latent shapes).
3. Let the process terminate gracefully so the cache flushes to disk (`/persistent/path` populated with cubin files).
4. Start a fresh process with the same env vars.
5. On the first `flash_attn.cute` call after `compile_cache` has loaded from disk, observe `cudaErrorInvalidDeviceFunction`.

## Logs

```
[1;36m(Worker pid=319)[0;0m ERROR 05-14 13:37:55.812 [multiproc_executor.py:537]     out, lse = _flash_attn_fwd(
[1;36m(Worker pid=319)[0;0m ERROR 05-14 13:37:55.812 [multiproc_executor.py:537]                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
[1;36m(Worker pid=319)[0;0m ERROR 05-14 13:37:55.812 [multiproc_executor.py:537]     _flash_attn_fwd.compile_cache[compile_key](
[1;36m(Worker pid=319)[0;0m ERROR 05-14 13:37:55.812 [multiproc_executor.py:537] RuntimeError: CUDA Error: cudaErrorInvalidDeviceFunction
```

## Suspected cause

The cache key in `flash_attn/cute/cache_utils.py:_compute_source_fingerprint` hashes Python source content + cutlass/tvm_ffi versions, but the actual compiled kernel binary depends on additional runtime context that isn't captured in the key:
- The exact call-site argument shapes (the JIT specializes per shape).
- Possibly device-specific JIT artifacts that are bound to driver instance / module state.

When process B loads process A's cached cubin under a key collision and hands it to CUDA, the kernel's expected device function signature doesn't match the launch site, and the driver returns `cudaErrorInvalidDeviceFunction`.

## Workaround

Leave `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_ENABLED` unset (default off). The in-process JIT cache still works fine; only the cross-process persistence path is affected.

## Expected fix

Either:
- Tighten the cache key to include per-call-site signature (input shape tuple, dtype, head_dim, etc.) so cross-process loads never resolve to a wrong cubin.
- Validate the loaded artifact against the call site

issues.title: [CuTe, SM80/SM120] Forward walks every KV block for local (sliding-window) attention
issues.body:
### Problem

With a local window, `FlashAttentionForwardSm80` computes all KV blocks from the diagonal down to block 0, then masks the ones outside the window. The output is correct, but the cost grows with the full `seqlen_k` instead of the window. SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, RTX 50xx) runs this kernel through `FlashAttentionForwardSm120(FlashAttentionForwardSm80)`, so sliding-window attention on those cards costs about 0.6× dense at long sequence lengths.

### Cause

The final mainloop in `flash_fwd.py` ("The remaining iterations have no masking", followed by `# TODO: local`) runs `cutlass.range(n_block)`. It ignores the `n_block_min` that `BlockInfo.get_n_block_min_max` already computes from `window_size_left`:

https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/d15f1531a460ba456f41b01a774f33ab2db8febf/flash_attn/cute/flash_fwd.py#L1061-L1070

The bug is present on `main` and in 4.0.0b33.

### Repro numbers

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), flash-attn-4 4.0.0b32, bf16, 56 heads, hdim 64, `window_size=(4096, 4096)`, varlen, batch 1:

| seqlen | time (ms) | TFLOP/s |
|---|---|---|
| 32,768 | 28.2 | 137 |
| 65,536 | 104.5 | 74 |
| 131,072 | 392.2 | 39 |
| 262,144 | 1524.5 | 20 |

Time grows about 4× per 2× seqlen (quadratic), where a fixed window should be linear.

### Proposed fix

Stop the loop at `n_block_min` (`cutlass.range(n_block - n_block_min)`). On the same setup, this brings 262k to 95.6 ms (16×). Outputs are identical to the unpatched kernel and match a band-masked SDPA reference per sequence. I'll open a PR.

issues.title: FA4: ~20-25us Python dispatch overhead per call — optimization targets
issues.body:
## Summary

CONSORT profiling of FA4's Python-level overhead reveals a constant ~20-25 us dispatch overhead per `flash_attn_func` call (both forward and backward). This is significant for small/medium problem sizes:

- **24% overhead** at batch=1, seqlen=128, heads=4, hdim=64
- **17% overhead** at batch=1, seqlen=2048, heads=16, hdim=128
- **<4% overhead** at batch=4, seqlen=4096 (large problems)

## Top Python-Level Bottlenecks (>5% of dispatch time)

### Forward (total Python: ~73 us/call)

| Function | us/call | % | Actionable? |
|----------|---------|---|-------------|
| `_flash_attn_fwd` body (validation, tensor setup, compile key construction) | 22.1 | 30.2% | Yes — fast-path for repeated shapes |
| CuTeDSL `wrapper` (TVM FFI) | 9.3 | 12.7% | Upstream (cutlass-dsl) |
| `active_fake_mode()` via `is_fake_mode()` (3x/call) | 7.1 | 9.7% | Yes — cache or check once |
| `torch.empty` (output alloc) | 5.3 | 7.2% | Yes — pre-alloc workspace |

### Backward (total Python: ~95 us/call)

| Function | us/call | % | Actionable? |
|----------|---------|---|-------------|
| `_flash_attn_bwd` body (validation, tile config, compile key) | 22.6 | 23.8% | Yes — fast-path |
| `active_fake_mode()` (4x/call) | 9.4 | 9.9% | Yes — cache or check once |
| `_bwd_preprocess` dispatch wrapper | 8.5 | 8.9% | Yes — inline/reduce overhead |
| `torch.empty_like` (6 tensor allocs) | 7.9 | 8.3% | Yes — workspace pre-alloc |
| CuTeDSL `wrapper` | 6.7 | 7.1% | Upstream |

## Suggested Optimizations

1. **Cache `is_fake_mode()` at call entry**: Check once in `flash_attn_func` and thread through, instead of re-checking 3-4x per call via `is_fake_mode()` -> `active_fake_mode()` -> `_get_current_dispatch_mode_stack()`.

2. **Cache `get_device_properties()`**: Called every forward to determine tile sizes. The result never changes for a given device. Use `@lru_cache` or module-level singleton.

3. **Fast-path for repeated calls**: When `(dtype, shape, causal, window_size)` match the previous call, skip all validation/assertions and go straight to kernel launch. This would eliminate the ~22 us of validation per call.

4. **Pre-allocate backward workspace**: The 6 tensor allocations in backward (`dq, dk, dv, dq_accum, dpsum, lse_log2`) could use a pre-allocated workspace pool, saving ~8 us.

5. **Upstream: CuTeDSL wrapper overhead**: The TVM FFI `wrapper` function adds ~7-9 us per kernel launch. This is in `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` and would need upstream optimization.

## Profiling Details

See comment on #11 for full profiling data tables.

- GPU: Hopper (SM90), CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4
- Profiling: `cProfile` (Python overhead) + CUDA events (GPU kernel time)
- Branch: `consort/varlen-uniform-v2` (based on `acceleration_main`)

issues.title: [ROCm/CK] Use aiter's gfx950 asm backward kernels in the CK backend (1.2–2.25× faster backward on MI350X)
issues.body:
### Proposal

Let the CK backward (`csrc/flash_attn_ck`) run aiter's gfx950 assembly backward kernels (`fmha_v3_bwd`) where they
match `fmha_bwd` against an fp32 reference, and fall back to `fmha_bwd` everywhere else. PyTorch's SDPA backward on
gfx950 already runs these kernels (via AOTriton).

**MI350X, bf16, causal backward, ms (CK → with aiter).** Columns are batch × seqlen; heads are 32/21/16/10 for
hdim 64/96/128/192.

| hdim | 2×8192 | 4×4096 | 16×1024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 4.10 → 3.41 (1.20×) | 2.23 → 1.80 (1.24×) | 0.79 → 0.66 (1.20×) |
| 96 | 4.68 → 3.18 (1.47×) | 2.57 → 1.74 (1.48×) | 1.19 → 0.61 (1.93×) |
| 128 | 3.45 → 2.19 (1.57×) | 1.78 → 1.20 (1.48×) | 0.72 → 0.47 (1.54×) |
| 192 | 8.33 → 6.22 (1.34×) | 5.14 → 3.20 (1.60×) | 2.15 → 0.96 (2.25×) |

Non-causal is 1.3–1.9× for hdim 96/128. Non-causal hdim 64 and hdim 256 stay on CK (no gain, or no kernel).

### How (a branch is ready; I'll open a PR that references this issue)

- `setup.py` runs aiter's codegen and embeds the gfx950 `fmha_v3_bwd` code objects with `.incbin` (4.5 MB), so
  nothing is looked up at runtime. `third_party/aiter` is already a submodule for the Triton backend.
- `mha_bwd.cpp` tries aiter first. A gate admits only the validated shapes: hdim 64–192 with hdim_q == hdim_v; no
  dropout, ALiBi or deterministic mode; seqlen_q ≥ 16; aligned seqlens when masked; bf16 only for hdim 64/192.
- Switches: `FLASH_ATTENTION_CK_BWD_ASM=0` at runtime, `FLASH_ATTENTION_CK_AITER_BWD=FALSE` at build time.

### Things you may not want

1. A C++ build dependency on aiter, whose codegen needs pandas at build time. If pandas is missing it warns and
   builds without the kernels.
2. **A build-time binary patch.** aiter's hdim-128 causal kernels miss an `s_barrier` and can write zeros into dK when
   other processes share the GPU (ROCm/aiter#5894). `setup.py` changes one instruction in the two kernels FA uses, and
   only when the file's SHA256 matches. It is removed once aiter ships fixed binaries.
3. gfx950 only. The gfx942 kernels exist, but I couldn't test them.

### Validation (MI350X, ROCm 7.1)

- 441 shapes vs fp32 reference; 580 edge shapes (ragged seqlens, GQA, masks); `tests/test_flash_attn_ck.py`
  (not kvcache/varlen): 51,842 passed.
- Race stress: 0 bad calls in 38,400 with 32 processes per GPU. The unpatched kernels fail about 0.4% of calls under the same load.

Would you take this? Should it be opt-in (off by default) at first?

issues.title: [CuTe, SM80] Forward silently ignores `block_sparse_tensors` and returns dense attention
issues.body:
## Problem

On SM80-class GPUs, calling `flash_attn_func(..., block_sparse_tensors=...)` ignores the block sparse configuration entirely. 
The kernel computes dense attention and returns it without any error or warning, so the caller believes they got a sparse result when they did not.

## Reproduction

Environment: RTX A6000 (SM86), torch 2.14.0+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, main @ 1bda8f9

Configure every Q block to attend only to KV block 0 (all full blocks, no `mask_mod` needed),
then compare against PyTorch dense / sparse references:

```python
import torch, math
from flash_attn.cute import flash_attn_func
from flash_attn.cute.block_sparsity import BlockSparseTensorsTorch

torch.manual_seed(0)
B, S, H, D = 1, 512, 2, 64
q, k, v = [torch.randn(B, S, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16) for _ in range(3)]
M, N = S // 128, S // 64
bst = BlockSparseTensorsTorch(
    mask_block_cnt=torch.zeros(B, H, M, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    mask_block_idx=torch.zeros(B, H, M, N, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    full_block_cnt=torch.ones(B, H, M, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    full_block_idx=torch.zeros(B, H, M, N, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
    block_size=(128, 64),
)
out, lse = flash_attn_func(q, k, v, block_sparse_tensors=bst, return_lse=True)

qt, kt, vt = [x.float().transpose(1, 2) for x in (q, k, v)]
keep = torch.zeros(S, S, dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda"); keep[:, :64] = True
dense = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(qt, kt, vt).transpose(1, 2)
sparse = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(qt, kt, vt, attn_mask=keep).transpose(1, 2)
print("vs dense :", (out.float() - dense).abs().max().item())
print("vs sparse:", (out.float() - sparse).abs().max().item())
```

Output:

```
vs dense : 0.00014
vs sparse: 0.95
```

## Expected behavior

Either honor the block sparse configuration, or raise an explicit error.

## Cause

- The SM80 branch in `interface.py` (`arch // 10 == 8`) only asserts that paged KV and SplitKV are unsupported. Unlike the SM120 branch, it has no `assert not use_block_sparsity`.
- `FlashAttentionForwardSm80.__call__` accepts a `blocksparse_tensors` argument, but the function body never uses it.

## Suggested fix

The minimal fix is to add the following to the SM80 branch:

```python
assert not use_block_sparsity, "Block sparsity not supported on SM 8.0"
```

I am happy to submit a PR for this if the maintainers agree. 
Whether to actually implement block sparsity in the SM80 kernel is a separate discussion.

issues.title: splitkv early-exit path ignores unpadded_lse, writing -inf to the wrong LSE slot
issues.body:
**Title:** splitkv early-exit path ignores `unpadded_lse`, writing `-inf` to the wrong LSE slot

**Repo:** Dao-AILab/flash-attention (also present in the vllm-project fork)

---

`flash_fwd_splitkv_kernel` computes the LSE write offset two different ways depending on
which exit it takes, and only one of them honours `params.unpadded_lse`.

**Normal exit** — `csrc/flash_attn/src/flash_fwd_kernel.h:1030`:

```cpp
const index_t row_offset_lseaccum = (Split || !params.unpadded_lse ?
        ((n_split_idx * params.b + bidb) * params.h + bidh) * params.seqlen_q
      : bidh * params.total_q + binfo.q_offset(params.seqlen_q, 1, bidb)
    ) + m_block * kBlockM;
```

**Early exit** (taken when `n_block_max <= n_block_min`, e.g. a zero-length or fully-masked
KV sequence) — `flash_fwd_kernel.h:552`:

```cpp
const index_t row_offset_lseaccum = ((n_split_idx * params.b + bidb) * params.h + bidh) * params.seqlen_q
    + m_block * kBlockM;
```

The ternary is missing. So when `unpadded_lse` is set and `Split` is false, the early exit
writes `-inf` into `params.softmax_lse_ptr` at a **dense** `(b, h, seqlen_q)` offset, while
the buffer is laid out **unpadded** as `(h, total_q)`. The two offsets coincide only when
`b == 1` and `seqlen_q == total_q`.

**Effect:** a varlen batch containing a zero-length (or fully masked) KV sequence writes
`-inf` into a different sequence's LSE slot, or out of bounds. `unpadded_lse` is set on the
varlen path, so any caller passing `return_softmax_lse=True` with a mixed batch is exposed.

**Why it is rarely seen:** early-exit CTAs finish almost immediately, so in practice the
correct value is usually written afterwards by the CTA that owns the slot, masking the race.
It is a genuine wrong-address write regardless of who wins.

**Fix:** apply the same ternary at `:552` as at `:1030`.

**Found while** validating a split-k change to `mha_varlen_fwd` in the vllm-project fork; this
bug is independent of that change and predates it. With split-k engaged the `-inf` is routed
correctly through the combine kernel, so the patched path does not hit it — this is about the
unsplit path.

**Not tested by:** the current suite never constructs a zero-length KV sequence in a varlen
batch with `return_softmax_lse=True`.

issues.title: Using `torch.library.wrap_triton` introduces measurable CPU overhead in `rotary`
issues.body:
older releases such as 2.7.4 don't do this
```
AFFECTED PATTERN: flash-attn 2.8.3.post1 rotary uses bare wrap_triton
installed path:    89.97 us/call
direct bypass:     19.97 us/call
recoverable:       70.00 us/call (4.5x)
```
minimal repro:
```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal reproducer for eager torch.library.wrap_triton overhead."""

import statistics
import time
import inspect

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def touch(x):
    tl.store(x, 0.0)


x = torch.empty(1, device="cuda")
raw = touch
wrapped = torch.library.wrap_triton(touch)  # Cache it: construction is not the issue.
grid = lambda meta: (1,)  # Match the callable-grid path used by FlashAttention.


def time_calls(fn, calls=1000, repeats=7):
    fn()  # Compile/warm up outside the measurement.
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    samples = []
    for _ in range(repeats):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(calls):
            fn()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        samples.append((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1e6 / calls)
    return statistics.median(samples)


raw_us = time_calls(lambda: raw[grid](x))
wrapped_us = time_calls(lambda: wrapped[grid](x))
print(f"raw:     {raw_us:8.2f} us/launch")
print(f"wrapped: {wrapped_us:8.2f} us/launch")
print(f"overhead:{wrapped_us - raw_us:8.2f} us/launch ({wrapped_us / raw_us:.1f}x)")


print("\nInstalled FlashAttention check:")
try:
    import flash_attn
    from flash_attn.ops.triton import rotary
except ImportError as error:
    print(f"SKIP: FlashAttention is not importable ({error})")
else:
    version = getattr(flash_attn, "__version__", "unknown")
    source = inspect.getsource(rotary.apply_rotary)
    if "torch.library.wrap_triton" not in source:
        print(f"UNAFFECTED: flash-attn {version} rotary does not use bare wrap_triton")
    else:
        print(f"AFFECTED PATTERN: flash-attn {version} rotary uses bare wrap_triton")
    q = torch.ones((1, 1, 1, 2), device="cuda")
    cos = torch.ones((1, 1), device="cuda")
    sin = torch.zeros((1, 1), device="cuda")
    call = lambda: rotary.apply_rotary(q, cos, sin, inplace=True)
    native_us = time_calls(call, calls=500, repeats=5)
    original_wrap_triton = torch.library.wrap_triton
    try:
        torch.library.wrap_triton = lambda kernel: kernel
        direct_us = time_calls(call, calls=500, repeats=5)
    finally:
        torch.library.wrap_triton = original_wrap_triton
    print(f"installed path: {native_us:8.2f} us/call")
    print(f"direct bypass:  {direct_us:8.2f} us/call")
    print(f"recoverable:    {native_us - direct_us:8.2f} us/call ({native_us / direct_us:.1f}x)")
```

issues.title: Support head_dim=512 on SM89 (Ada) for Gemma 4 global attention layers
issues.body:
## Feature request

Add a `head_dim=512` forward path in FlashAttention for **compute capability 8.9 (Ada — L40, L40S, RTX 4090)**.

## Why

Google's Gemma 4 ships a hybrid attention design with 4 global-attention layers at `head_dim=512` (alongside 26 layers at `head_dim=256`, which FA2 already handles cleanly). On SM89, `flash_attn_varlen_func` currently rejects `head_dim=512` outright — the model can't use FlashAttention for those layers at all.

## Why a separate ask from #2427

#2427 tracks `head_dim=512` generically. The path being explored there is **FA4 / cute** kernels, which depend on Hopper TMA + WGMMA. FA3 and FA4 are gated to compute capability ≥ 8 **excluding 8.6 and 8.9**, so anything that lands in FA4 will not reach Ada GPUs.

For SM89 the realistic path is **extending FA2** (or a dedicated SM89 kernel) to handle `head_dim=512`. We understand this is harder:
- No TMA — global→shared loads have to be hand-staged.
- No WGMMA — smaller MMA tiles → tighter SMEM budget for a 512-wide head.

## What would be sufficient

A `head_dim=512` forward path (varlen + paged-KV) on SM89, FP16/BF16 Q/K/V, with FP8 KV-cache support if feasible. Prefill is the more painful case for long-context Gemma 4 inference; decode is a bonus. Causal-mask + sliding-window support to match the rest of FA2.

issues.title: [FA4/B200] return_lse=True makes D64 forward about 19% faster
issues.body:
I had my agent create this reproducer while doing some heuristic tuning. This is quite strange, and I wanted to track it.

On B200, the FA4 CuTe forward kernel for dense BF16 attention with `(B, S, H, D) = (2, 16384, 16, 64)` is consistently faster when `return_lse=True`, even though that specialization calculates and writes the additional LSE output.


### Agent notes

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA B200 (SM100)
- PyTorch: `2.14.0.dev20260722+cu132`
- PyTorch CUDA runtime: 13.2
- NVIDIA CuTe DSL: `4.6.0.dev0`
- FlashAttention commit: `00756db9d921da0846453283ddfbeb7457abd09b`
- Dtype: BF16
- Causal: false
- Measurement: fixed-pointer CUDA graph replay, 25 warmups and 100 measured replays per round, five alternating A/B rounds

## Result

```text
GPU: NVIDIA B200
Torch: 2.14.0.dev20260722+cu132 (CUDA 13.2)
CuTe DSL: 4.6.0.dev0
FA4 commit: 00756db9d921da0846453283ddfbeb7457abd09b
no-LSE: median=3.0018 ms rounds=[3.007457275390625, 3.0017739868164064, 3.001456604003906, 3.0028912353515627, 3.0008636474609376]
with-LSE: median=2.5281 ms rounds=[2.5091484069824217, 2.545796203613281, 2.512978210449219, 2.5281126403808596, 2.532301177978516]
with-LSE speedup: 1.187x
```

Both paths pass a correctness check against PyTorch SDPA.

A focused Nsight Compute comparison showed the same launch topology and resource limits for both specializations (148 blocks, 512 threads, 128 registers/thread, and approximately 232 KB dynamic shared memory). The no-LSE specialization had substantially fewer eligible/issued warps and more samples around the pipeline synchronization path. This looks more like a compiler scheduling/code-generation cliff than an inherent benefit from calculating LSE.

I have only established this behavior on B200; this report does not claim the same result on GB300.

## Minimal reproducer

Run with:

```bash
python repro_fa4_lse_b200.py /path/to/flash-attention
```

```python
"""Reproduce the FA4 D64 B200 performance inversion caused by returning LSE."""

import argparse
import importlib
import importlib.metadata
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType
from typing import Callable

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def load_fa4_interface(fa4_root: Path) -> ModuleType:
    """Load the CuTe FA4 interface without requiring the FA2 extension."""
    package = ModuleType("flash_attn")
    package.__path__ = [str(fa4_root / "flash_attn")]
    sys.modules["flash_attn"] = package
    return importlib.import_module("flash_attn.cute.interface")


def make_call(
    interface: ModuleType,
    q: torch.Tensor,
    k: torch.Tensor,
    v: torch.Tensor,
    return_lse: bool,
) -> Callable[[], torch.Tensor]:
    """Create one allocation-free FA4 forward specialization."""
    out = torch.empty_like(q)
    lse = (
        torch.empty(q.shape[0], q.shape[2], q.shape[1], device=q.device)
        if return_lse
        else None
    )

    def run() -> torch.Tensor:
        return interface._flash_attn_fwd(
            q, k, v, out=out, lse=lse, return_lse=return_lse
        )[0]

    return run


def capture(function: Callable[[], torch.Tensor]) -> torch.cuda.CUDAGraph:
    """Capture a warmed FA4 call into a fixed-pointer CUDA graph."""
    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
        for _ in range(3):
            function()
    stream.synchronize()
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    wit

issues.body:
## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA RTX 6000D 84 GB (sm_120, GeForce Blackwell), driver 595.84, CUDA 13.2
- flash-attn-4: 4.0.0b26 and 4.0.0b29 (both tested)
- nvidia-cutlass-dsl: 4.6.0.dev0 / 4.6.2 / 4.7.1 (all three tested)
- torch 2.13.0+cu129, torchvision 0.28.0, Python 3.12
- Workload: MiniMax-H3 hybrid-attention video model (VDN-MiniMax-H3) — bf16 packed
  varlen attention, H=56 heads, D=128, per-window varlen segments
  (q ~5040 rows/segment, kv ~17580 rows/segment), called once per DiT block per NFE.

## Summary

Two independent problems when running FA4 on SM120:

1. **`AuxData` cannot cross the CuTe-DSL JIT boundary** — the SM120 forward path
   (`FlashAttentionForwardSm120`) passes `AuxData(cute_aux_tensors, aux_scalars)` as
   positional arg #17, but the DSL has no adapter for this NamedTuple
   (`JitArgAdapterRegistry.default_dataclass_adapter` is never registered in a plain
   `flash_attn_func`/`flash_attn_varlen_func` install, and NamedTuples are not
   auto-adapted). Consequences differ by DSL version:
   - DSL 4.6.2: `CUDADialectError` (empty message) → clean failure, kernel never runs
   - DSL 4.6.0.dev0 / 4.7.1: only a `UserWarning` ("cannot be converted to a
     JitArgument ... implement the JitArgument protocol"), then the kernel is
     launched with a mangled argument → **illegal memory access**

   Workaround that makes the kernel compile and run (register a zero-width
   JitArgument adapter; our calls always have `tensors=None, scalars=None`, at which
   point the kernel body early-returns in `compute_fastdiv_mods`):

   ```python
   import flash_attn.cute.utils as fa_utils
   import cutlass  # canonical DSL import path
   from cutlass.base_dsl.runtime.jit_arg_adapters import JitArgAdapterRegistry

   class _ZeroWidthAux:
       def __init__(self, src): self._src = src
       def __getattr__(self, name): return getattr(self._src, name)
       def __get_mlir_types__(self): return []
       def __c_pointers__(self): return []
       def __new_from_mlir_values__(self, values): return self

   def _adapt(aux):
       if aux.tensors is None and aux.scalars is None:
           return _ZeroWidthAux(aux)
       raise NotImplementedError("non-empty AuxData")

   JitArgAdapterRegistry.register_jit_arg_adapter(fa_utils.AuxData)(_adapt)
   ```

   Suggested upstream fixes (either): register a default dataclass/NamedTuple
   adapter in `base_dsl` when `default_dataclass_adapter` is unset, or annotate/
   adapt `AuxData` in `interface.py` so `flash_attn_func`/`flash_attn_varlen_func`
   work out of the box on SM120.

2. **With (1) worked around, the SM120 kernel still hits an illegal memory access
   once the varlen batch has >= 4 segments under real-workload memory layouts.**
   Details below. This is the blocker: the kernel is ~7x faster than our fallback

issues.title: FA4 SM103 backward preprocess predicate shape mismatch for padded head dimensions
issues.body:
### Summary

On B300/SM103, FA4 beta27's backward preprocess reuses a predicate covering all per-thread row modes after slicing the O/dO source and destination tensors to a single row. CuTe rejects the resulting copy because the predicate has shape `(1,(2,3))` while the data expects `(1,(3))`.

The same `flash_bwd_preprocess.py` code is present in beta29 and current `main` (`4fd8d758c1fb7d93ef2e9a316ba4db1ab7fc05fe` as fetched on 2026-09-03).

### Environment

- NVIDIA B300 / SM103
- CUDA 13.2 base image
- PyTorch 2.10.0a0+3a035ad5.nv25.12
- Python 3.13
- `flash-attn-4==4.0.0b27`
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2`
- BF16, varlen causal attention
- `CUTE_DSL_SHOW_STACKTRACE=1`

### Sanitized reproducer

```python
import torch
from flash_attn.cute import flash_attn_varlen_func

torch.manual_seed(42)
q = torch.randn(256, 16, 80, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
k = torch.randn(256, 4, 80, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
v = torch.randn(256, 4, 80, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
cu = torch.tensor([0, 256], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
result = flash_attn_varlen_func(
    q,
    k,
    v,
    cu_seqlens_q=cu,
    cu_seqlens_k=cu,
    max_seqlen_q=256,
    max_seqlen_k=256,
    causal=True,
)
out = result[0] if isinstance(result, tuple) else result
out.float().square().mean().backward()
```

Backward-preprocess compile key:

```text
dtype=BFloat16, head_dim=80, head_dim_v=80, m_block_size=128,
has_cuseqlens_q=True, has_seqused_q=False, has_dlse=False,
has_dq_accum=True, has_scale_p=False, use_padded_offsets=True,
nheads_major=False, pack_gqa=False, qhead_per_kvhead=1,
nheads_kv=1, has_cu_total_m_blocks=False
```

Compiler diagnostic:

```text
error: unknown: 'cute.copy' op expects pred to have compatible shape with: (1,(3)) but got actual predShape: (1,(2,3))
note: unknown: see current operation: "cute.copy"(...) :
  (!cute_nvgpu.atom.universal_copy<bf16, 128 b>,
   !cute.memref<bf16, gmem, align<16>, "((8,1),(3)):((1,0),(32))">,
   !cute.memref<bf16, rmem, align<16>, "((8,1),(3)):((1,0),(8))">,
   !cute.memref<i8, rmem, align<32>, "(1,(2,3)):(3,(0,1))">) -> ()
```

### Source mapping and proposed correction

`flash_attn/cute/flash_bwd_preprocess.py` constructs `tOpO` from unsliced `tOcO`, then captures it in a `partial`. Inside the `m` loop it slices both data tensors with `[None, m, None]` but does not slice the predicate.

Slicing the predicate over the same row mode makes the preprocess compile and run:

```diff
-copy = partial(copy_utils.copy, pred=tOpO)
 ...
-copy(tOgO[None, m, None], tOrO[None, m, None])
-copy(tOgdO[None, m, None], tOrdO[None, m, None])
+row_predicate = tOpO[None, m, None] if const_expr(tOpO is not None) else None
+copy_utils.copy(tOgO[None, m, None], tOrO[None, m, None], pred=row_predicate)
+copy_utils.copy(tOgdO[None, m, None], tOrdO[None, m, None], pred=row_predicate)
```

This report is limited to the backward-preprocess predicate mismatch; the reproducer may encounter other constraints later in the general SM100 backward kernel once preprocess is repaired.

issues.title: [ROCm][CK][gfx1201][Windows] FlashAttention backward is 4.4–7.4x slower than PyTorch SDPA on RX 9070 XT
issues.body:
## Summary

I am seeing unexpectedly poor backward performance from the ROCm CK backend of FlashAttention on an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (gfx1201, RDNA4) on Windows.

Forward performance is good and consistently faster than PyTorch SDPA, but backward is **4.4x to 7.4x slower** than SDPA, with the gap increasing at longer sequence lengths. Forward + backward is therefore **3.3x to 6.0x slower** than SDPA.

Numerical results look correct, so this appears to be a performance issue rather than a correctness issue.

This resembles the old ROCm FlashAttention backward performance issue:
https://github.com/ROCm/flash-attention/issues/44

That issue was eventually reported as fixed after the ck_tile refactor. I am wondering whether the gfx1201 / RDNA4 backward path is hitting an untuned or fallback CK kernel.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Pro
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT
- Architecture: gfx1201
- PyTorch: `2.15.0a0+rocm10.1.0a20260814`
- HIP: `7.16.26323`
- FlashAttention source tag: `fa4-v4.0.0.beta26`
- FlashAttention Python package version: `2.8.4`
- Composable Kernel submodule: `c56c6750d0fc54ed771d532cc92c316423449614`
- `rocm-sdk-core`: `10.1.0a20260814`
- `rocm-sdk-devel`: `10.1.0a20260814`
- `rocm-sdk-device-gfx1201`: `10.1.0a20260814`

- MSVC: 14.44 / cl 19.44

Build configuration:

```text
BUILD_TARGET=rocm
FLASH_ATTENTION_FORCE_BUILD=TRUE
GPU_ARCHS=gfx1201
PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1201
OPT_DIM=32,64,128,256
MAX_JOBS=8
```

CK backend was used, not the Triton AMD backend.

On this dual-GPU system I exposed the RX 9070 XT as the only visible GPU for the benchmark, so the benchmark device is logical `cuda:0`.

## Benchmark configuration

- dtype: `torch.bfloat16`
- batch: 1
- heads: 16
- head_dim: 128
- causal: False

### Forward only

| Sequence | PyTorch SDPA | Flash CK | Flash / SDPA |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| 2048 | 0.610 ms | 0.439 ms | 0.719x |
| 4096 | 2.011 ms | 1.450 ms | 0.721x |

| 2048 | 3.490 ms | 18.268 ms | 5.234x |
| 4096 | 11.950 ms | 71.421 ms | 5.976x |

Peak allocated memory was effectively identical in this microbenchmark.

## Correctness

For `B=1, S=1024, H=16, D=128`, BF16:

```text

dQ relative L2: 1.489228e-03

So the outputs and gradients appear numerically reasonable.

I see the same qualitative behavior in an actual LoRA training workload: the CK FlashAttention path is substantially slower than PyTorch SDPA during training, despite being slightly faster for inference/sampling.

issues.title: FA4 backward does not return against cutlass-dsl 4.6.0 and 4.6.1 on B300 (sm_103)
issues.body:
On a B300 (sm_103), FA4's backward stops returning when the loaded CuTe DSL runtime is 4.6.0 or 4.6.1. The pinned prerelease and the current release are both fine.

| nvidia-cutlass-dsl runtime | dense backward | varlen backward |

Three runs per cell, and two per cell in a separate environment built from scratch with an independently written test, agreeing cell for cell.

Setup: flash-attn-4 4.0.0b26, torch 2.14.0.dev20260806+cu130, CUDA 13.0. Each run in its own process under an external timeout, since the kernel never returns. Dense goes through SDPA with the FA4 impl active, bf16, B=2 H=4 S=256 D=64, non-causal. Varlen goes through `torch.nn.attention.varlen.varlen_attn`, four segments of 256, 4 heads, head dim 64. The stall is inside `_bwd_postprocess_convert`, with the same stack sampled 75 seconds apart. With grouped-query attention the varlen path stops too — 16 query heads against 8 key/value heads is enough.

Two things about how this stayed hidden, which may be more useful than the table.

The pin moved from `>=4.5.2` to `==4.6.0.dev0` in #2648 on 2026-06-25, and 4.6.0 was released on 07-02 — so no released runtime has been inside the declared range since. The pin also excludes 4.6.2, while `quack-kernels` 0.6.4 requires exactly 4.6.2, so an environment holding both cannot satisfy them.

And the version does not tell you what is loaded. `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` is a meta-package whose runtime ships in `-libs-cu12` and `-libs-cu13`; a process loads one. An environment can report 4.6.2 from `importlib.metadata` while loading a cu13 runtime still at 4.6.0 — which happens when something else pins the cu13 extra, as vllm does with `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.6.0`. The reproduction below prints the mapped library for that reason.

Possibly the same thing, untested from here: #2466 (FA4 with softcap hangs on backward).
